chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) said: “The Divine leaders/Imams after me are twelve in number. You, o’ ʿAlī, are the first of them, and the last of them is the Qāʾim through whose hands Allāh, elevated is His remembrance, will conquer (for Islam) the Earth, from its easternmost to its westernmost reaches.”[1]
arabicText: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: الأئمة من بعدي إثنا عشر، أوّلهم أنت يا علي، وآخرهم القائم الذي يفتح الله—تعالى ذكره—على يديه مشارق الأرض ومغاربها.
thaqalaynSanad: The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Divine leaders/Imams after me are twelve in number. You, o’ ʿAlī, are the first of them, and the last of them is the Qāʾim through whose hands Allāh, elevated is His remembrance, will conquer (for Islam) the Earth, from its easternmost to its westernmost reaches.”[1]

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: The Mistress of the Women (as-f) said: “The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) came to me when al-Ḥusayn was born to me…and said: “O’ Fāṭima! Take him [i.e. al-Ḥusayn (as)], for he is an Imam, the son of an Imam and a forefather of the Imams, nine of them from his loins. They are the righteous Imams, and the ninth of them is the Qāʾim.”
arabicText: وقالت سيّدة النساء عليها‌ السلام: دخل إليّ رسول الله (ص) عند ولادتي الحسين ... ثمّ قال: يا فاطمة، خذيه [أي الحسين « ع »] فإنّه إمام، ابن إمام، وأبو الأئمة، تسعة من صلبه، أئمة أبرار، والتاسع قائمهم.
thaqalaynSanad: The Mistress of the Women (as-f) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) came to me when al-Ḥusayn was born to me…and said: “O’ Fāṭima! Take him [i.e. al-Ḥusayn (as)], for he is an Imam, the son of an Imam and a forefather of the Imams, nine of them from his loins. They are the righteous Imams, and the ninth of them is the Qāʾim.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said to his son, al-Ḥusayn (as): “The ninth from your descendants, o’ Ḥusayn, is the Qāʾim with the Truth.”
arabicText: وقال أمير المؤمنين عليه‌ السلام لابنه الحسين عليه‌ السلام: التاسع من ولدك يا حسين هو القائم بالحقّ.
thaqalaynSanad: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said to his son, al-Ḥusayn (as):
thaqalaynMatn: “The ninth from your descendants, o’ Ḥusayn, is the Qāʾim with the Truth.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Al-Zahrāʾ (as-f) said: “By Allāh! Were they to leave the right (of leadership of the Islamic community) to its people and follow the offspring of His Prophet, no two would dispute about Allāh, and one predecessor would inherit from another, and one successor after another, until our Qāʾim, the ninth of al-Ḥusayn’s descendants, would arise.”
arabicText: وقالت الزهراء عليها‌ السلام: أما والله لو تركوا الحقّ على أهله، واتّبعوا عترة نبيّه، لما اختلف في الله اثنان، ولورثها سلف عن سلف، وخلف بعد خلف، حتى يقوم قائمنا، التاسع من ولد الحسين.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Zahrāʾ (as-f) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “By Allāh! Were they to leave the right (of leadership of the Islamic community) to its people and follow the offspring of His Prophet, no two would dispute about Allāh, and one predecessor would inherit from another, and one successor after another, until our Qāʾim, the ninth of al-Ḥusayn’s descendants, would arise.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Ḥasan (as) said: “That is the ninth of my brother al-Ḥusayn’s descendants, the son of the mistress of the bondswomen, whose lifespan Allāh will extend during his occultation, and then cause him to reappear through His power.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الحسن عليه‌ السلام: ذاك التاسع من ولد أخي الحسين، ابن سيدة الإماء، يطيل الله عمره في غيبته، ثمّ يظهره بقدرته.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Ḥasan (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “That is the ninth of my brother al-Ḥusayn’s descendants, the son of the mistress of the bondswomen, whose lifespan Allāh will extend during his occultation, and then cause him to reappear through His power.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Ḥusayn (as) said: “Among us are twelve Divinely guided ones [Mahdīs], the first of whom is Amīr al-Muʾminīn, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, and the last of whom is the ninth of my descendants. He is the Imam who is the Qāʾim with the Truth.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الحسين عليه‌ السلام: منّا اثنا عشر مهدياً، أولهم أمير المؤمنين عليّ بن أبي طالب وآخرهم التاسع من ولدي، وهو الإمام القائم بالحق.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Ḥusayn (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Among us are twelve Divinely guided ones [Mahdīs], the first of whom is Amīr al-Muʾminīn, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, and the last of whom is the ninth of my descendants. He is the Imam who is the Qāʾim with the Truth.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Sajjād (as) said: “It was concerning us that the verse ﴾He made it a lasting word among his posterity﴿ [43:28] was revealed. Divine leadership/Imamate is for the posterity of al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-d) until the Day of Resurrection, and among us is the Qāʾim who will have two occultations.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام السجّاد عليه‌ السلام: فينا نزلت هذه الآية ﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةًۢ بَاقِيَةًۭ فِى عَقِبِهِ﴾ والإمامة في عقب الحسين بن عليّ بن أبي طالب (ع) إلى يوم القيامة، وإن للقائم منّا غيبتين.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Sajjād (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “It was concerning us that the verse ﴾He made it a lasting word among his posterity﴿ [43:28] was revealed. Divine leadership/Imamate is for the posterity of al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-d) until the Day of Resurrection, and among us is the Qāʾim who will have two occultations.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Bāqir (as) said: “Among us are twelve interlocutors with the angels,[1] and the seventh of my descendants is the Qāʾim.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الباقر عليه‌ السلام: منّا اثنا عشر محدثاً، السابع من ولدي القائم.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Bāqir (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Among us are twelve interlocutors with the angels,[1] and the seventh of my descendants is the Qāʾim.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (as) said: “Mūsā is the Imam after me, and the awaited and hoped-for successor, M-Ḥ-M-D, is the son of al-Ḥasan, the son of ʿAlī, the son of Muḥammad, the son of ʿAlī, the son of Mūsā.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام جعفر الصادق عليه‌ السلام: الإمام من بعدي موسى، والخلف المأمول المنتظر م ح م د ابن الحسن بن علي بن محمد بن علي بن موسى.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Mūsā is the Imam after me, and the awaited and hoped-for successor, M-Ḥ-M-D, is the son of al-Ḥasan, the son of ʿAlī, the son of Muḥammad, the son of ʿAlī, the son of Mūsā.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Kāẓim (as) said: “The Qāʾim, who will scour the earth clean of the enemies of Allāh and fill it with justice as it had been filled with iniquity, is the fifth of my descendants.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الكاظم عليه‌ السلام: القائم الذي يطهّر الأرض من أعداء الله، ويملأها عدلاً كما ملئت جوراً، هو الخامس من ولدي.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Kāẓim (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Qāʾim, who will scour the earth clean of the enemies of Allāh and fill it with justice as it had been filled with iniquity, is the fifth of my descendants.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Riḍā (as) said: “The Qāʾim…that is the fourth of my descendants.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الرضا عليه‌ السلام: القائم ... ذاك الرابع من ولدي.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Riḍā (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Qāʾim…that is the fourth of my descendants.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Jawād (as) said: “The Qāʾim…is the third of my descendants.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الجواد عليه‌ السلام: القائم ... هو الثالث من ولدي.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Jawād (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Qāʾim…is the third of my descendants.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-Hādī (as) said: “Indeed, the Imam after me is my son, al-Ḥasan, and after al-Ḥasan his son, the Qāʾim.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الهادي عليه‌ السلام: إن الإمام بعدي الحسن ابني، وبعد الحسن ابنه القائم.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-Hādī (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Indeed, the Imam after me is my son, al-Ḥasan, and after al-Ḥasan his son, the Qāʾim.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Imam al-ʿAskarī (as) said: “My son, M-Ḥ-M-D, is the Imam/Divine leader and authority after me. Whoever dies without having recognised him dies a death of the pre-Islamic age of ignorance.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام العسكري عليه‌ السلام: ابني م ح م د هو الإمام والحجّة بعدي، من مات ولم يعرفه مات ميتة جاهلية.
thaqalaynSanad: Imam al-ʿAskarī (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “My son, M-Ḥ-M-D, is the Imam/Divine leader and authority after me. Whoever dies without having recognised him dies a death of the pre-Islamic age of ignorance.”

chapter: Introductory Traditions
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: The occulted, awaited Imam—may Allāh hasten the noble Deliverance he will bring—said: “I bear witness that there is no god besides Allāh, Who is One, without any associate of His, and that my grandfather, Muḥammad, is the Apostle of Allāh, and that my father is the Commander of the Believers.”[1] He then counted the Imams, one after the other, until he reached himself. He then said: “O’ Allāh! Accomplish for me what You have promised me, bring my affair to completion, make firm my foothold and fill the Earth with justice and equity through me.”
arabicText: وقال الإمام الغائب المنتظر عجّل الله فرجه الشريف: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأنّ جدي محمداً رسول الله، وأنّ أبي أمير المؤمنين، ثم عدّ إماماً إماماً إلى أن بلغ إلى نفسه، ثم قال: اللهم أنجز لي ما وعدتني، وأتمم لي أمري، وثبّت وطأتي، واملأ الأرض بي عدلاً وقسطاً.
thaqalaynSanad: The occulted, awaited Imam—may Allāh hasten the noble Deliverance he will bring—said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I bear witness that there is no god besides Allāh, Who is One, without any associate of His, and that my grandfather, Muḥammad, is the Apostle of Allāh, and that my father is the Commander of the Believers.”[1] He then counted the Imams, one after the other, until he reached himself. He then said: “O’ Allāh! Accomplish for me what You have promised me, bring my affair to completion, make firm my foothold and fill the Earth with justice and equity through me.”

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Thus, owing to the need for the Occultation, reports proliferated, and transmissions differed on account of meanings pertaining to precautionary dissimulation (taqiyya) and the preservation of lives, for ﴾Allāh does not lead any people astray after He has guided them until He has made clear to them what they should beware of﴿ [9:115]. Were it not for dissimulation and fear, nobody would have been confused, neither would any two persons have disagreed, nor would anything from among the monuments of Allāh’s (taa) religion have emerged except in a word upon which none disagree and a letter which none find confounding. However, Allāh, exalted be His names, entrusted the Imams of guidance with the safeguarding of the community, and placed them in one era in which they were permitted to disseminate knowledge, and in another in which they were forbearing, so that they may ﴾forgive those who do not expect Allāh’s days, that He may [Himself] requite every people for what they used to earn﴿ [45:14]. How momentous and magnificent a matter this is! And surely it was for some momentous cause that it occurred and came to pass! Nor is it strange that, in times such as these, a report should arise that protects the neck-vein and, through the virtue of prudent conciliation, safeguards the general body of the community.
arabicText: فلأجل الحاجة إلى الغيبة اتّسعت الأخبار، والمعاني التقيّة والمدافعة عن الأنفس اختلفت الروايات ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْمًۢا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُبَيِّنَ لَهُم مَّا يَتَّقُونَ﴾. ولولا التقية والخوف، لما حار أحد، ولا اختلف اثنان، ولا خرج شيء من معالم دين الله—تعالى—إلّا على كلمة لا تختلف وحرف لا يشتبه. ولكنّ الله—عظمت أسماؤه—عهد إلى أئمة الهدى في حفظ الأُمة، وجعلهم في زمن مأذون لهم باذاعة العلم، وفي آخر حلماء ﴿يَغْفِرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ لِيَجْزِىَ قَوْمًۢا بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾. عظم هذا من أمر وجلّ! ولأمر ما وقع وحلّ! وغير عجب أن يحدث في مثله من الأوقات خبر يحمي خيط الرقبة. ويحرس بفضل المداراة جمهور البيضة.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: In an era like this, the matter of the number[1] was contested, to the point that there was outwardly brought about a matter concerning that whose inward reality admitted no disagreement, and there was disclosed a reason which there was no doubt ought to have been concealed. Nor does it constitute a well-known indication or an explicit public proclamation for one who is among Allāh’s representatives, and a trustworthy custodian of Allāh’s secrets, to say: “The Master of this Ordinance is more well-established than I am, and lighter in movement,”[2] especially in view of the famous transmissions and numerous traditions stating that the time is unknown and the era unrecognised. Furthermore, were it not for the secrecy surrounding the time and its deliberate concealment, his advent would not have been identified by means of the Cry, the signs and the emergence of the war-banners of the people of misguidance,[3] and it would instead have been said: “He is so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, and his day is a known day among other days.” However, Allāh, magnified be His name, made it an ordinance awaited at every moment and a condition hoped for by the people of every age, lest people’s hearts become hardened by the protracted term that Allāh decrees, and lest the promised punishment for resorting to a misdeed or an obscenity come to be regarded as slow in arriving; and so that every agent may remain in readiness, with hope lying beyond the performance of good deeds, and apprehension and restraint lying before the people of iniquities and misdeeds; and so that Allāh may repel some by means of others. The ancient precedent in this regard is the statement of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) concerning the Hour, when he warned his people: “The Hour has come upon you in the morning! The Hour has come upon you in the evening! The Hour and I have been sent forth like these two.”[4]
arabicText: وفي مثل هذا الزمن خولف الأمر في العدد، حتى أُوقع في الظاهر أمر ما لا خلاف في استبطانه، وكشف عن سبب لا شك في كتمانه. وليست إشارة مشهورة وإذاعة بيّنة أن يقول وليّ من أولياء اللهِ وثقة من خزّان أسرار الله أنّ صاحب هذا الأمر أثبت منّي، وأخفّ ركاباً. هذا، مع الروايات المشهورة والأحاديث الكثيرة: أنّ الوقت غير معلوم، والزمن غير معروف، ولولا كتمان الوقت والمساترةُ به، لما استدلّ عليه بالصيحة، والآيات وخروج رايات أهل الضلالات، ولقيل: إنّه فلان بن فلان، وإنّ يومه يوم معلوم بين الأيام، ولكن الله—جلّ اسمه—جعله أمراً منتظراً في كل حين، وحالاً مرجوّة عند كل أهل عصر، لئلاً تقسو—بطول أجل يضربه الله—قلوب، ويستبطأ في استعمال سيّئة وفاحشة، موعدة عقاب، وليكون كل عامل على اُهبّة، ويكون من وراء أعمال الخيرات اُمنيّةٌ، ومن وراء أهل الخطايا والسيئات خشية وردعة، وليدفع الله بعضاً ببعض، والسنّة القديمة على هذا قول رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله في أمر الساعة حين أنذر قومه: صبّحتكم الساعة، مسّتكم الساعة، بعثت أنا والساعة كهذه من هذه.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: So, were it not for what He intended by way of repulsion and of making the term seem near to the doer of good and evil deeds—and likewise the reward and the retribution—the Prophet (sawa) would have made known that what the misguided community would be brought to would occur before the advent of the Hour, and that what Allāh had promised him concerning the people of his House—namely, that He would cause them to prevail over all other religions—would come to pass before its advent. In accordance with this did the Apostles pass on and the chosen ones proceed, each of them presenting the Resurrection and the Hour as near and bringing glad tidings of the swiftness of requital in retribution and reward. And were information concerning everything, according to its true reality, to have been given beforehand, and the appointed term for every period fixed and laid out in advance, it would have been incumbent by the right of the Apostolate and the duty of notification upon ʿĪsā (as) to command those whom he knew would live to the time of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) to restrict themselves to what he enjoined upon them during his own days, trusting that Muḥammad’s Sacred Law would abrogate the prior Sacred Laws, and knowing that he was the best of the Prophets and the Master of the Apostles. And the people of every interval would have committed horrific sins and countless offences; instead, they remained in a state of expecting imminent retribution or reward, and due to that Allāh repelled some people by means of others. This custom is likewise put into practice among the Imams (as-p), operative throughout their days and established among them.
arabicText: فلولا ما أراد من المدافعة وتقريب المدّة على عامل الخير والشرّ والثواب والعقاب، لعلم (صلّى الله عليه وآله) أن ما جرت إليه الاُمّة الضالّة دون وقوع الساعة، وأنّ ما وعده الله في أهل بيته من إظهارهم على الدين كلّة قبل حدوثها يكون. وعلى هذا مضت الرسل، ودرج الأخيار، كل يقرّب القيامة، ويدني الساعة، ويبشّر بسرعة المجازاة على العقاب والثواب. ولو كان الخبر عن كل شئ بحقيقته مقدّماً، والأجل في كل مدّة مضروباً ممهداً، لكان حق الرسالة وفرض البلاغة على عيسى عليه السلام أن يأمر من يعلم أنّه يبلغ زمن رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله أن يقتصر على ما يعهده في أيّامه، ثقة بأنّ شريعته تنسخ الشرايع، وعلماً بأنّه خير النبيّين وسيد المرسلين. ولأقترف أهل كل فترة ذنوبًا عظيمة وجرائح كثيرة، ولكنّهم كانوا على اقترابٍ من انتظار عقاب أو ثواب وبذلك دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض. وهذه السنّة في الأئمة عليهم السلام مستعملة، وعلى أيّامهم جارية، وفيهم قائمة.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Furthermore, had the matter of the number been left neglected and unheeded, none of the abundant reports about the covenant Allāh took from the prophets and the righteous predecessors of the community would have been transmitted. The statement of Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as)[1] when he was asked about Nūḥ (as) proves as much, when the asker mentioned that: “His Ark had settled upon (the mountain of) al-Jūdiyy, with them in tow,” and then asked: “Was Nūḥ cognisant of their number?,” so the Imam replied: “Yes, and so was Ādam (as).” How could a number known to the father of mankind, to those of his progeny who passed on, and to the Prophets from among his descendants, become a matter of disagreement among a mere fraction of his progeny and a scant remnant of his posterity?!
arabicText: ولو كان أمرهم مهملاً عن العدد وغفلاً، لما وردت الأخبار الوافرة بأخذ الله ميثاقهم على الأنبياء وسالف الصالحين من الأُمة. ويدلك على ذلك قول أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام حين سئل عن نوح عليه السلام لمّا ذكر « استوت سفينته على الجوديّ بهم »: هل عرف نوح عددهم؟ فقال: نعم، وآدم عليه السلام. وكيف يختلف عدد، يعرفه أبو البشر ومن درج من عترته والأنبياء من عقبه، على شرذمة من ذريّته وبقيّة يسيرة من ولده؟!

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And what interpretation could rightly be presented for the tradition of the Tablet,[1] or the tradition of the Sealed Scroll? And what of the report transmitted by Jābir (b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī) concerning the Scroll of Fāṭima (as-f)? And how could it not be known that what the Scholar (as) said: “six days,” or “six months,” or “six years,” was something indeterminate?! Without any doubt, it is possible that a matter whose time may conceivably extend from six days to six months, and from six months to six years, may just as conceivably extend for years beyond that. Is this not understood? If he (as) intended to specify the time, then it is known that he did not specify it; and if he intended to obscure it, then it is no wonder that he should obscure it to the greatest extent within his power and conceal it with the utmost effort possible to him, for a matter concerning which one trusted for his knowledge speaks with uncertainty between six days and six years can have been intended for nothing other than obfuscation and concealment. And were it not for questions being thrust upon them when answering was disadvantageous, no verdict would ever have been issued except according to its true reality, nor any statement except in its proper tenor.
arabicText: وأيّ تأويل يدخل على حديث اللوح. وحديث الصحيفة المختومة؟ والخبر الوارد عن جابر في صحيفة فاطمة عليها السلام؟ وكيف لا يعلم: أنّ الذي قالـ[ه] العالم عليه السلام: ستّة أيام، أو ستة أشهر أو ستّ سنين، غير معلوم؟! ومن غير شك يجوز أنّ أمراً لا يمتنع أن يجوز وقته من ستّة أيام إلى ستّة أشهر، ومن ستّة أشهر إلى ستّ سنين، غير ممتنع أن يجوز إلى سنين. وهل هذا مفهومٌ؟ فإن كان عليه السلام أراد تسمية الوقت، فقد علم أنّه لم يسمّ. وإن أراد الأغماض منه فغير عجب أن يغمضه بأشدّ ما يقدر عليه، ويستر عنه بأجهد ما يمكنه، لأنّ أمراً يخبر عنه من يوثق بعلمه بالشك بين ستّة أيام أو ستّ سنين، لا يراد به غير المغامضة والسّتّر. ولولا إقحام السؤال عليهم في أوقات غير مسهّلة للجواب، لما خرج حكم إلّا على حقيقته، ولا كلام إلّا على جهته.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: As for his (as) statement: “The Master of this Ordinance is thirty years old, or thirty-one, or forty; but if he passes forty, then he is not the Master of this Ordinance,” it was intended for the preservation of lives, and so that those among his enemies who heard this tradition and had no doubt concerning the Imamate of the one relating it might become certain that he was not the Master of the Sword, due to that leaving him alone and becoming distracted from seeking him. The Imam’s statement regarding this: “The seventh from among the descendants of the fifth will have dominion, until he fills it with justice just as it had been filled with iniquity,” proves as much. Had it been impossible for the Master of this Ordinance to pass forty years of age, it would likewise have been impossible for any of the Imams (as-p) to remain fit for the Imamate beyond forty, because the Imamate is a single charge, exercised through knowledge and the sword. Nor would Allāh invest this hallowed Ordinance in a man whom He chooses, only then to deprive him of it on account of his age.
arabicText: فأمّا قوله عليه السلام: إنّ صاحب هذا الأمر ابن ثلاثين سنة، أو إحدى وثلاثين سنة، أو أربعين سنة، فإن جاز الأربعين فليس بصاحب هذا الأمر. فإنّه لمعنى المدافعة عن الأنفس، وليتيقّن من لا يشكّ في إمامة من يحدّث بهذا الحديث من أعدائه: أنّه ليس بصاحب السيف فيلهو عنه ويشتغل عن طلبه. ويدلّك على هذا قوله: يملك السابع من ولد الخامس، حتى يملأها عدلاً كما ملئت جوراً. ولو كان صاحب هذا الأمر لا يجوز أن يجوز أربعين سنة، لما جاز لأحد من الأئمة عليهم السلام أن تصلح له الإمامة فوق الأربعين، لأن الإمامة شأن واحد في القيام بالعلم والسيف، وما كان الله ليجعل هذا الأمر العظيم في رجل يختاره، ثم ينزعه عنه لمعنى السنّ.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Were I to withhold what I have articulated by way of this interpretation of the report, there would be, in the interpretation placed upon it by one who clings to it for the purpose of refutation, an even more convincing argument and a more decisive rebuttal, because he who transmits this tradition interprets it as meaning that the impossibility of undertaking the Imamate beyond forty years of age is due to the impairment of the intellects. And I seek refuge in Allāh from saying that they—the Ahl al-Bayt (saa-p)—are in the position of the rest of mankind, or that their intellects are susceptible to corruption at forty years of age and beyond. For the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) is the most excellent role model, and he is the Master of the Prophets and the rightly guided Imams: when he surpassed forty (years of age) he was made a Prophet, and for years after that he made the Mission manifest. As for the matter of Mūsā (al-Kāẓim) (as), and his statement: “He will not die until he has filled the earth with justice just as it had been filled with iniquity,” he said that at a time of intense pursuit and hardness of hearts, so as to bring the term near and restrain the oppressors. As for the decisive argument against those who professed the cessation of the Imamate with him, I have exhaustively set it forth through authentic reports in the chapter concerning his Imamate. By mentioning this tradition, I intended only to adduce his statement: “Allāh made a disclosure (badāʾ) concerning what I said,” because it was uttered during the days of so-and-so, when pursuit and fear had become intense, such that after this tradition there occurred an Occultation and concealment which have continued to this very age and reached this duration; and Allāh would never make a disclosure concerning the designation of an Imam or his emergence. Nor do I differentiate, after having affirmed that Imamate is one of the five religious ordinances, between one who professes Divine disclosure, in that context, with respect to the number and designation (of Imams), and one who professes Divine disclosure with respect to the ritual prayer, fasting and the remaining four religious ordinances. For the four proceed from the one, which is Imamate: if it were possible for Allāh to abrogate the foundation of the religious ordinances, it would be possible for Him to abrogate their ancillaries. And I seek refuge in Allāh from saying that a Sacred Law has been abrogated or a religious dispensation changed, after Allāh has made Muḥammad (sawa) the Seal of the Prophets, his Sacred Law the seal of all Sacred Laws, and perpetuated adherence to his religion and Sacred Law until the advent of the Hour and the transition therefrom to the Gathering of the Resurrection. As for the time, the established precedent regarding it is concealment, and the Sacred Law regarding it requires refraining from public disclosure. And among that which demonstrates dissimulation and soundly orients one to the fact that the numerous reports were transmitted for some particular reason is his (as) statement: “Allāh made a disclosure concerning Ismāʿīl.” What, then, becomes of the decisive argument concerning Ādam (as), namely that he preserved their names? And what is to be said concerning Nūḥ (as), namely that he knew their number? And how can it be maintained that Allāh (azwj) took their covenant from the entire community while He would abrogate their ordinance and make a disclosure concerning their names? And by what evidence can the matter of the Tablet be set aside? Then there are the reports concerning the primordial shadows, and the transmitted traditions stating that Allāh created them before the religious communities. Allāh would never appoint one of His representatives as master over a people and then make a disclosure concerning that after He has already taken upon Himself a great number of them, since it is a truth that He holds none accountable except by means of a decisive argument and punishes none except after the reality has been fully conveyed. Far be it from Allāh that He should appoint among His servants caliphs whose ordinance He would overturn and whose custom He would alter, or that His wisdom, glory be to Him, should be such that He would nominate a man for the safeguarding of the body of the Muslims, only for him to become as one who is removed therefrom before the expiration of his appointed term and the completion of his allotted duration; or that He should place him in a position in which his intellect would become susceptible to corruption upon his reaching the utmost extent of life and the furthest reaches of age. Allāh transcends that with a great transcendence.
arabicText: ولو طويت ما نطقت به من هذا التأويل على هذا الخبر، لكان فيما يتأوّله من يتعلق به للردّ أقنع حجّة وأبلغ دفعاً، لأنّ الذي يروي هذا الحديث يتأوّل: أنّ امتناع القيام بعد الأربعين سنة من طريق النكير في العقول. وأعوذ بالله أن أقول: إنّهم صلوات الله عليهم بمنزلة سائر الناس، وإنّ عقولهم ممّا يدخلها الفساد في الأربعين وما فوقها. والأسوة برسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله حسنة، وهو سيّد النبيّين والأئمة الراشدين، وحين أناف على الأربعين نُبّي، وبعدها بسنين أظهر الدعوة. فأمّا أمر موسى عليه السلام، وقوله: وإنّه لا يموت حتى يملأها عدلاً كما ملئت جوراً، فإنّ ذلك قاله عند شدّة الطلب وقسوة القلوب، ليقرّب المدّة، ويردع الظلمة. والحجّة، فيمن قال بالوقف عليه، قد استقصيت بصحيح الأخبار في باب إمامته. وإنّما أردت بذكر هذا الحديث إيراد قوله: « بدا لله فيما قلت » لأنّه خرج في أيّام فلان حين اشتدّ الطلب والخوف، حتى وقع بعد هذا الحديث من الغيبة والاختفاء ما اتّصل بهذا العهد وبلغ هذه المدّة، وما كان الله ليبدو له في إمام تسميةً ولا خروجاً. وما أُفرّق—بعد قولي: إن الإمامة أحد الشرائع الخمسة—بين من يقول بالبداء فيها بالعدد والتسمية، وبين من يقول بالبداء في الصلاة والصوم وسائر الشرائع الأربعة. لأنّ مَخْرَجَ الأربعة من الواحدة، وهي الإمامة، فإن جاز أن ينسخ الله أصل الشرائع، جاز أن ينسخ فرعها. وأعوذ بالله أن أقول بنسخ شريعة وتبديل ملّة، بعد أن جعل الله محمّداً صلّى الله عليه وآله خاتم النبيّين، وشريعته خاتمة الشرائع، وواصل القيام على دينه وشريعته بقيام الساعة، والانتقال منها إلى محشر القيامة فأمّا الوقت: فالسنّة فيه الكتمان، والشريعة فيه الامساك عن الإعلان. وممّا يدلّ على التقيّة ويرشد إلى أنّ الأخبار الكثيرة وردت لعلّةٍ ما: قوله عليه السلام: « بدا لله في إسماعيل ». فكيف الحجّة الآن في آدم عليه السلام أنّه حفظ أسماءهم؟ وما القول في أمر نوح أنّه علم عددهم؟ وكيف يثبت أنّ الله—عزّ وجلّ–أخذ على الأمّة كلّها عهدهم، وهو ينسخ أمرهم، ويبدو له في أسمائهم؟. وبأيّ دليل يدفع أمر اللوح؟ فأخبار الأظلّة، والآثار الواردة أنّ الله خلقهم قبل الأُمم، وما كان الله ليأخذ مولى من أوليائه على قوم، ثم يبدو له في ذلك وقد قبض إليه منهم العدد الكثير، إذ هو الحق أن لا يحاسب إلا بحجّة، ولا يعذّب إلّا بحقيقة بلاغ. وحاش لله أن يجعل خلفاء في عباده من ينقض أمرهم ويبدّل سنّتهم وتكون حكمته—سبحانه—بمحل يرشّح رجلاً لحفظ بيضة المسلمين فيكون بمنزلة ينحّى عنها قبل انقضاء أجّله وبلوغ مدّته، أو يجعله بمحل من يحدث في عقله الفساد لبلوغه أقصى العمر وأبعد السنّ، تعالى الله عن ذلك علوّاً كبيراً.

chapter: The Reasons for Differences in Transmitted Narrations & the Requisites for Confusion and Uncertainty
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: The decisive argument for this stated principle resembles the argument concerning his designation by name: an Imam was designated, and for what he is; while the stated principle of Divine disclosure was manifested in regard to something analogous to it, or a disclosure was Divinely instituted for the purpose of averting something concerning death, anguish, sustenance or lifespan. But the Imamate does not change, the lineage does not die out and the number neither increases nor decreases. If someone were to say: “The point in time to which the Occultation has reached is the furthest extent of the lifespan of the people of the time and the utmost limit of the years of the people of this age, yet the signs preceding him have not manifested and the indications mentioned as occurring before him have not come about,” then why does he not profess Divine disclosure concerning these indications and argue for their abrogation, since it is admissible according to him that Allāh should disclose something concerning an Imam? Indeed, that would be more fitting and more warranted. Yet you will find that most of them refuse this and argue that these indications are among the predetermined matters! How, then, can he make these indications among those things concerning which Allāh does not make disclosures because they are predetermined, while professing Divine disclosure concerning the Imamate, even though he does not doubt that it is among the predetermined matters?! And why does he not adopt as the decisive argument in this regard that Allāh, magnified be His name, may pardon His servants from the retribution and punishment with which He threatens them, whether that threat be predetermined or conditional, whereas He does not disclose concerning a promise of goodness, be it small or great, so that the duration may remain intact for him, Allāh may render the time near to him, and he may due to that be spared the estrangement caused by the protraction of the Occultation? And if he abandons this explanation concerning the time and instead argues from lifespan, saying that a later lifespan cannot exceed an earlier lifespan, then it is widely reported that the lifespan of Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as) exceeded that of those who preceded him. Whatever is possible in one is possible in another, especially when this is not something that corrupts a Sacred Law or invalidates a custom (of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa)). Perhaps, after all these considerations, the diminisher [1] will seek refuge in submission, saying that it is obligatory to employ it with regard to all reports, while abhorring discernment and rejecting judicious purpose, and will say: “The reports have been relayed, acceptance is incumbent and submission obligatory.” He, on account of that, places the representative in the position of the enemy, obligating Allāh’s representatives to act upon a report that came out from the scholars out of dissimulation before Allāh’s enemies. He does not know that one who strives earnestly in action is superior to one who relies upon mere hopes, and is ignorant of the statement of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as): “O’ Allāh! You know that whenever two matters presented themselves to me—one containing Your satisfaction, and the other my desire—I preferred Your satisfaction over my desire.” This lies far from the immediate mode of this discussion and constitutes a profound consideration in this context, yet subtle consideration leads to it and precise thought necessitates it: if preference is required between two matters which are both true, the satisfaction of Allāh is to be preferred over the desire of one of His representatives. Indeed, the exercise of preference is required in favour of a report transmitted as a binding argument, while taking admonition is obligatory from a report that was issued for the purpose of dissimulation and the preservation of lives. May Allāh render us among those who perceive their rectitude, are guided to its paths, strive in religion to the fullest extent of their capacity and expend in that their utmost strength, fear Him with the fear that is His due, remain vigilant of Him with the vigilance of the people of His obedience, desire His reward and fear the return to Him; and may He seal our deeds with felicity and excellent proximity to Him. I have elucidated, through authentic reports from the Imams of guidance (as-p), the reports I have mentioned concerning the number, everything that occurred during the era of an Imam by way of an indication toward a man or an unwarranted claim on his part, and the impossibility of exceeding the number or altering the names. Upon Allāh, exalted is He, I rely, seeking forgiveness for my shortcomings and seeking refuge in Him—glorified be He—from intending, through what I have undertaken, anything other than rectification. My success is not but through Allāh; upon Him I have relied and to Him I turn.
arabicText: والحجّة على هذا القول، مثل الحجّة على تسميته: فسمّى إماماً، ولما هو، وأظهر القول فيه بالبداء لمثله، أو جعل البداء لمعنى معارضة في موت أو غم أو رزق أو أجل. والإمامة لا تغيّر، والنسب لا ينقطع، والعدد لا يزيد ولا ينقص. فإن قال قائل: إنّ الذي انتهى إليه الوقت في الغيبة غاية عمر أهل الدهر، ونهاية سنّ خلق هذا العصر، وانّ الآيات قبله لم تظهر، والدلالات المذكورة بين يديه لم تحدث؟! فهلّا يقول بالبداء في هذه الدلالات، ويحتجّ بنسخها، إذ؟ هو جائز عنده أن يبدو لله في إمام، فإنّ ذلك أولى وأحق. وستجده أكثر من يمتنع من هذا، ويحتجّ بأنها من المحتوم! فكيف يجعل هذه الدلالات ممّا (لا) يبدو لله فيها، لأنها من المحتوم، ويقول بالبداء في الإمامة ولا يشكّ أنّها من المحتوم؟! وكيف لا يتّخذ الحجّة في ذلك: أن الله—جلّ اسمه—يعفو عن عباده فيما يتوعّدهم به من عقاب وعذاب محتوماً كان ذلك منه أو موقوفاً. فلا يبدو له في وعد خير صغيراً كان أو كبيراً، حتى تسلم له المدّة ويقرب الله عليه الوقت، ويكفيه أمر الوحشة لطول الغيبة. وإن ترك هذه العلّة في الوقت، وقال بالعمر: أنّه لا يجوز عمر متأخر على عمر متقدم؟! فالخبر شائع أنّ عمر أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام أوفى على عمر من تقدّمه. وكلّما جاز أن يكون في واحد، هو جائز أن يكون في آخر، لا سيّما إذا لم يكن ذلك مما يفسد شريعة أو يبطل سنّة. وعسى أن يعتصم بعد هذه الأحوال مقصّر بالتسليم، فيقول: إنّه واجب استعماله في الأخبار كلّها، ويكره التفقّه، ويرفض القصد فيقول: وردت الأخبار، ولزم القبول ووجب التسليم. ويجعل الوليّ في ذلك بمنزلة العدوّ، فيوجب على أولياء الله استعمال خبر خرج من العلماء عن تقيّة لأعداء الله. ولا يعلم أنّ المجتهد في العمل أفضل من المتّكل على الأماني. ويجهل قول أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: اللّهمّ إنك تعلم أنّه ما ورد عليّ أمران أحدهما لك رضا، والآخر لي هوى، إلّا آثرت رضاك على هواي. وهذا بعيد من هذا النمط، وعميق من القول في هذا الموضع، لكنّ لطيف النظر يذهب إليه، ودقيق الفكر يوجب أنّه إذا لزم الإيثار في أمرين كلاهما حق، لفُضّل رضا الله على هوى وليّ من أوليائه. إنّ استعمال الإيثار في خبر ورد لمكان حجة، واستعبار واجب على خبر وقع لمعنى تقيّة ومكان مدافعة. جعلنا الله ممّن يبصر رشده، ويهتدي سننه، ويجتهد في الدين بُلغته ويبذل فيه طاقته، ويخشاه حق خشيته، ويراقبه مراقبة أهل طاعته، ويرغب في ثوابه ويخاف معاده، وختم أعمالنا بالسعادة والزلفى الحسنة. وقد بيّنت الأخبار التي ذكرتها من طريق العدد، وكل ما وقع في عصر إمام من إشارة إلى رجل، أو دعاية منه بغير حق، واستحالة مجاوزة العدد وتبديل الأسماء، بصحيح الأخبار عن الأئمة الهادين عليهم السلام. متوكلاً على الله تعالى، ومستغفراً من التقصير، ومستعيذاً به سبحانه أن أُريد—بما تكلّفته—إلّا الإصلاح وما توفيقي إلّا بالله، عليه توكّلت، وإليه أنيب.

chapter: The Testamentary Succession from the Time of Ādam (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and al-Haytham b. Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb al-Sarrād, from Muqātil b. Sulaymān from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq) (as), who said: “The Prophet (sawa) said: “I am the Master of the Prophets, and my legatee is the Master of the Legatees, and his legatees are the Masters of all Legatees. Ādam (as) had asked Allāh (taa) to install for him a righteous legatee, so Allāh (azwj) revealed to him: “Indeed, I have ennobled the Prophets through (their) Prophethood, then I chose My creation and made the select ones among them Legatees. Ādam (as) replied: “O’ Lord, make my legatee the best of all Legatees!” So, Allāh revealed to him: “O’ Ādam, bequeath to Shīth,” so Ādam bequeathed to Shīth, and he was Hibat Allāh b. Ādam.[1] Shīth bequeathed to his own son, Shabān—the son of a celestial maiden brought down by Allāh to Ādam from Heaven, whom Ādam married to his son, Shīth—and Shabān bequeathed to Mukhlith. Mukhlith bequeathed to Maḥūq, Maḥūq bequeathed to ʿAthmīthā, and ʿAthmīthā bequeathed to Akhnūkh, who was the Prophet Idrīs (as). Idrīs bequeathed to Nāḥūr, and after that Nāḥūr handed it over to Nūḥ the Prophet (as).[2] Nūḥ bequeathed to Sām, and Sām bequeathed to ʿIthāmir. ʿIthāmir bequeathed to Barʿathībāshā, and Barʿathībāshā bequeathed to Yāfuth. Yāfuth bequeathed to Barah, Barah bequeathed to Ḥafṣah, Ḥafṣah bequeathed to ʿImrān, and ʿImrān handed it over to Ibrāhīm (as), the Intimate (of Allāh). Ibrāhīm bequeathed to his son, Ismāʿīl, who in turn bequeathed to (his brother) Isḥāq. Isḥāq bequeathed to Yaʿqūb, Yaʿqūb bequeathed to Yūsuf, Yūsuf bequeathed to Bathariyā, and Bathariyā bequeathed to Shuʿayb. Shuʿayb handed it over to Mūsā b. ʿImrān (as). Mūsā bequeathed to Yūshaʿ b. al-Nūn, Yūshaʿ bequeathed to the Prophet Dāwūd, and Dāwūd bequeathed to Sulaymān. Sulaymān bequeathed to Āṣif b. Barkhiyā, Āṣif bequeathed to Zakariyyā, and Zakariyyā handed it over to ʿĪsā b. Maryam (as). ʿĪsā bequeathed to Shamʿūn b. Ḥamūn al-Ṣafāʾ, Shamʿūn bequeathed to Yaḥyā b. Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā b. Zakariyyā bequeathed to Mundhir, Mundhir bequeathed to Salīma, and Salīma bequeathed to Bardah.” The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) then said: “Bardah handed it over to me, and now I am handing it over to you, o’ ʿAlī. You will hand it over to your legatee, and your legatee will hand it over to the Legatees of yours from among your progeny, one after the other, until it is handed over to the best of all those who will dwell upon the earth after you. The community will disbelieve in you,[3] and dissent concerning you with an abundant, severe dissension. The one who resolutely affirms you (as the Imam) is as if he were standing with me, while the one who deviates from you is in Hellfire. And Hellfire is the residence for the disbelievers.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ومحمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب والهيثم بن أبي مسروق النهدي، عن الحسن بن محبوب السرّاد، عن مقاتل ابن سليمان عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله: أنا سيّد النبيّين، ووصيّي سيّد الوصيّين وأوصياؤه سادة الأوصياء. إنّ آدم عليه السلام سأل الله تعالى أن يجعل له وصيّاً صالحاً، فأوحى الله عزّ وجلّ إليه: إنّي أكرمت الأنبياء بالنبوّة، ثم اخترت خلقي وجعلت خيارهم الأوصياء. فقال آدم عليه السلام: يا ربّ اجعل وصيّي خير الأوصياء. فأوحى الله إليه: يا آدم، أوص إلى شيث فأوصى آدم إلى شيث، وهو هبة الله بن آدم. وأوصى شيث إلى ابنه شبان، وهو ابن نزلة الحوراء التي أنزلها الله على آدم من الجنة، فزوّجها ابنه شيثاً. وأوصى شبان إلى مخلث. وأوصى مخلث إلى محوق. وأوصى محوق إلى عثميثا. وأوصى عثميثا إلى أخنوخ، وهو إدريس النبي عليه السلام. وأوصى إدريس إلى ناحور. ودفعها ناحور إلى نوح النبيّ عليه السلام. وأوصى نوح إلى سام. وأوصى سام إلى عثامر. وأوصى عثامر إلى برعثباشا. وأوصى برعثباشا إلى يافث. وأوصى يافث إلى بره. وأوصى بره إلى حفسه. وأوصى حفسه إلى عمران. ودفعها عمران إلى إبراهيم الخليل عليه السلام. وأوصى إبراهيم إلى ابنه إسماعيل. وأوصى إسماعيل إلى إسحاق. وأوصى إسحاق إلى يعقوب. وأوصى يعقوب إلى يوسف. وأوصى يوسف إلى بثريا. أوصى بثريا إلى شعيب. ودفعها شعيب إلى موسى بن عمران عليه السلام. وأوصى موسى إلى يوشع بن النون. وأوصى يوشع إلى داود النبيّ وأوصى داود إلى سليمان. وأوصى سليمان إلى آصف بن برخيا. وأوصى آصف إلى زكريّا. ودفعها زكريّا إلى عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام. وأوصى عيسى إلى شمعون بن حمون الصفا. وأوصى شمعون إلى يحيى بن زكريّا. وأوصى يحيى بن زكريا إلى منذر. وأوصى منذر إلى سليمة. وأوصى سليمة إلى برده. ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: ودفعها إليّ برده وأنا أدفعها إليك يا عليّ. وأنت تدفعها إلى وصيّك، ويدفعها وصيّك إلى أوصيائك من ولدك واحداً بعد واحد، حتى تُدفع إلى خير أهل الأرض بعدك. ولتكفرنّ بك الاُمّة، ولتختلفنّ عليك اختلافاً كثيراً شديداً الثابت عليك كالمقيم معي، والشاذّ عنك في النار ((والّنٰارُ مَثوى الكافرين)).
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and al-Haytham b. Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb al-Sarrād, from Muqātil b. Sulaymān from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq) (as), who said: “The Prophet (sawa) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I am the Master of the Prophets, and my legatee is the Master of the Legatees, and his legatees are the Masters of all Legatees. Ādam (as) had asked Allāh (taa) to install for him a righteous legatee, so Allāh (azwj) revealed to him: “Indeed, I have ennobled the Prophets through (their) Prophethood, then I chose My creation and made the select ones among them Legatees. Ādam (as) replied: “O’ Lord, make my legatee the best of all Legatees!” So, Allāh revealed to him: “O’ Ādam, bequeath to Shīth,” so Ādam bequeathed to Shīth, and he was Hibat Allāh b. Ādam.[1] Shīth bequeathed to his own son, Shabān—the son of a celestial maiden brought down by Allāh to Ādam from Heaven, whom Ādam married to his son, Shīth—and Shabān bequeathed to Mukhlith. Mukhlith bequeathed to Maḥūq, Maḥūq bequeathed to ʿAthmīthā, and ʿAthmīthā bequeathed to Akhnūkh, who was the Prophet Idrīs (as). Idrīs bequeathed to Nāḥūr, and after that Nāḥūr handed it over to Nūḥ the Prophet (as).[2] Nūḥ bequeathed to Sām, and Sām bequeathed to ʿIthāmir. ʿIthāmir bequeathed to Barʿathībāshā, and Barʿathībāshā bequeathed to Yāfuth. Yāfuth bequeathed to Barah, Barah bequeathed to Ḥafṣah, Ḥafṣah bequeathed to ʿImrān, and ʿImrān handed it over to Ibrāhīm (as), the Intimate (of Allāh). Ibrāhīm bequeathed to his son, Ismāʿīl, who in turn bequeathed to (his brother) Isḥāq. Isḥāq bequeathed to Yaʿqūb, Yaʿqūb bequeathed to Yūsuf, Yūsuf bequeathed to Bathariyā, and Bathariyā bequeathed to Shuʿayb. Shuʿayb handed it over to Mūsā b. ʿImrān (as). Mūsā bequeathed to Yūshaʿ b. al-Nūn, Yūshaʿ bequeathed to the Prophet Dāwūd, and Dāwūd bequeathed to Sulaymān. Sulaymān bequeathed to Āṣif b. Barkhiyā, Āṣif bequeathed to Zakariyyā, and Zakariyyā handed it over to ʿĪsā b. Maryam (as). ʿĪsā bequeathed to Shamʿūn b. Ḥamūn al-Ṣafāʾ, Shamʿūn bequeathed to Yaḥyā b. Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā b. Zakariyyā bequeathed to Mundhir, Mundhir bequeathed to Salīma, and Salīma bequeathed to Bardah.” The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) then said: “Bardah handed it over to me, and now I am handing it over to you, o’ ʿAlī. You will hand it over to your legatee, and your legatee will hand it over to the Legatees of yours from among your progeny, one after the other, until it is handed over to the best of all those who will dwell upon the earth after you. The community will disbelieve in you,[3] and dissent concerning you with an abundant, severe dissension. The one who resolutely affirms you (as the Imam) is as if he were standing with me, while the one who deviates from you is in Hellfire. And Hellfire is the residence for the disbelievers.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Dāwūd b. al-ʿAlā, from Abī Ḥamza al-Thumālī, who said that (Imam) al-Bāqir (as) stated: “The world has not been devoid, ever since Allāh created the heavens and the earth, of a just Imam who serves as an authority of Allāh upon His creation, until the Hour comes.”
arabicText: محمّد بن يحيى، عن عبداللّه بن محمّد بن عيسى، عن محمّد بن إبراهيم، عن زيد الشحّام، عن داود بن العلا، عن أبي حمزة الثمالي، قال: قال الباقر عليه السلام: ما خلت الدنيا—منذ خلق الله السماوات والأرض—من إمام عدل إلى أن تقوم الساعة حجّة لله فيها على خلقه.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Dāwūd b. al-ʿAlā, from Abī Ḥamza al-Thumālī, who said that (Imam) al-Bāqir (as) stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “The world has not been devoid, ever since Allāh created the heavens and the earth, of a just Imam who serves as an authority of Allāh upon His creation, until the Hour comes.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who narrated: “Bashīr al-Duhān and I were with Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), whereupon he said: “When the prophethood of Ādam (as) concluded and his term ended, Allāh (azwj) revealed to him thus: “O’ Ādam! Your prophethood has concluded and your term ended, so look to what you have of knowledge, belief, the heritage of prophethood, the choicest knowledge and the Most Exalted Name, and confer it upon your offspring—with Hibat Allāh [1]—for I will not have left the Earth without a Scholar through whom My ordained religion and obedience to Me is recognised, and whoever obeys him attains salvation.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمّد بن عيسى، عن محمّد بن سنان، عن نعمان الرازي، قال: كنت أنا وبشير الدهان، عند أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، فقال: لمّا انقضت نبوّة آدم عليه السلام وانقطع أجله، أوحى الله عزّ وجلّ إليه أن يا آدم، قد انقضت نبوّتك، وانقطع أجلك، فانظر إلى ما عندك من العلم والإيمان وميراث النبوّة وأثرة العلم والإسم الأعظم، فاجعله في العقب من ذريّتك، عند هبة الله، فإني لن أدع الأرض بغير عالم يعرف به طاعتي وديني، ويكون نجاة لمن أطاعه.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Bashīr al-Duhān and I were with Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), whereupon he said: “When the prophethood of Ādam (as) concluded and his term ended, Allāh (azwj) revealed to him thus: “O’ Ādam! Your prophethood has concluded and your term ended, so look to what you have of knowledge, belief, the heritage of prophethood, the choicest knowledge and the Most Exalted Name, and confer it upon your offspring—with Hibat Allāh [1]—for I will not have left the Earth without a Scholar through whom My ordained religion and obedience to Me is recognised, and whoever obeys him attains salvation.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Hishām b. Sālim, from Abī Isḥāq al-Hamadānī, who said: “A trustworthy member of our companions narrated to me that he heard Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) say: “O’ Allāh, do not leave the Earth devoid of a Divine authority of Yours upon Your creatures, be he apparent, or hidden and obscure, lest Your decisive argument and Your explications be nullified!”
arabicText: وعنه، عن محمّد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن هشام بن سالم، عن أبي إسحاق الهمداني، قال: حدّثني الثقة من أصحابنا: أنّه سمع أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام، يقول: اللّهمّ، لا تُخل الأرض من حجّة لك على خلقك، ظاهر أو خاف مغمور، لئلّا تبطل حجّتك وبيّانتك.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Hishām b. Sālim, from Abī Isḥāq al-Hamadānī, who said: “A trustworthy member of our companions narrated to me that he heard Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) say:
thaqalaynMatn: “O’ Allāh, do not leave the Earth devoid of a Divine authority of Yours upon Your creatures, be he apparent, or hidden and obscure, lest Your decisive argument and Your explications be nullified!”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb al-Sarrāj, who narrated: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Can the Earth remain without a Scholar, living and apparent,[1] to whom people resort concerning what is lawful and unlawful for them?,” so he replied: “Allāh would not be worshipped were that to occur, o’ Abā Yūsuf!”
arabicText: محمّد بن يحيى، عن محمّد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن يعقوب السرّاج، قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: تبقى الأرض بلا عالم حيّ ظاهر يفزع إليه الناس في حلالهم وحرامهم؟ فقال لي: إذاً، لا يعبد الله، يا أبا يوسف.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb al-Sarrāj, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Can the Earth remain without a Scholar, living and apparent,[1] to whom people resort concerning what is lawful and unlawful for them?,” so he replied: “Allāh would not be worshipped were that to occur, o’ Abā Yūsuf!”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-ʿAlā, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): Al-Ḥusayn b. al-ʿAlā narrated: “I said to him: “Can the Earth remain, even for just a day, without an Imam?,” so he replied: “No.”
arabicText: وعنه، عن محمّد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن محمّد بن أبي عمير، عن الحسين بن أبي العلا: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: قال: قلت له: تبقى الأرض—يوماً—بغير إمام؟ فقال: لا.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-ʿAlā, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): Al-Ḥusayn b. al-ʿAlā narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to him: “Can the Earth remain, even for just a day, without an Imam?,” so he replied: “No.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from some trustworthy ones, from al-Ḥasan b. Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The Earth cannot exist without a Scholar residing upon it who rectifies its people, and nothing but that can rectify the people.”
arabicText: وعنه، عن محمّد بن عيسى، عن بعض الثقات، عن الحسن بن زياد: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: الأرض لا تكون إلّا وفيها عالم يصلحهم، ولا يصلح الناس إلّا ذلك.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from some trustworthy ones, from al-Ḥasan b. Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Earth cannot exist without a Scholar residing upon it who rectifies its people, and nothing but that can rectify the people.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥasan b. Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “People are not rectified except by an Imam, nor is the Earth rectified except through that.”
arabicText: سعد، عن محمّد بن عيسى، عن صفوان بن يحيى، عن ابن مسكان عن الحسن بن زياد: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: لا يصلح الناس إلّا بإمام، ولا تصلح الأرض إلّا بذلك.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥasan b. Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “People are not rectified except by an Imam, nor is the Earth rectified except through that.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Abī ʿAmmāra b. al-Ṭayyār, who said: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “Were none to remain upon the Earth except two persons, one of them would be the Divine authority.”
arabicText: سعد، عن محمّد بن عيسى، عن محمّد بن سنان، عن أبي عمّارة بن الطيّار قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام، يقول: لو لم يبق في الأرض إلّا اثنان، لكان أحدهما الحجّة.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Abī ʿAmmāra b. al-Ṭayyār, who said: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Were none to remain upon the Earth except two persons, one of them would be the Divine authority.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from a man, from Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said: “By Allāh, since Allāh took (the soul of) Ādam, He has never left the earth without there being upon it an Imam through whom one is guided to Allāh, and he is the Divine authority of Allāh upon His servants. Nor would the Earth remain without an Imam who is the Divine authority of Allāh upon His servants.”
arabicText: وعنه، عن محمّد بن عيسى، عن رجل، عن أبي حمزة: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال: والله، ما ترك الله الأرض منذ قبض الله آدم، إلّا وفيها إمام يهتدى به إلى الله، وهو حجّة الله على عباده، ولا تبقى الأرض بغير إمام، حجّة لله على عباده.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from a man, from Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “By Allāh, since Allāh took (the soul of) Ādam, He has never left the earth without there being upon it an Imam through whom one is guided to Allāh, and he is the Divine authority of Allāh upon His servants. Nor would the Earth remain without an Imam who is the Divine authority of Allāh upon His servants.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mughīra and ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, altogether from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Allāh has not left the Earth be without a Scholar residing upon it, who knows about (unauthorised) additions and omissions (in religion). So, were the believers to add anything, he would reorient them (to what is correct), and if they were to fall short, he would complete it for them, saying: “Take it completely.” Were it not for that, the affairs of the believers would become disordered, and it would not be possible to differentiate between truth and falsehood.”
arabicText: سعد، عن محمّد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن محمّد بن سنان وصفوان بن يحيى وعبداللّه بن المغيرة وعلي بن النعمان، كلّهم: عن عبداللّه بن مسكان، عن أبي بصير: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: إنّ الله لم يدع الأرض إلّا وفيها عالم يعلم الزيادة والنقصان فإذا زاد المؤمنون ردّهم، وإن نقصوا أكمله لهم، فقال: خذوه كاملاً، ولولا ذلك لالتبس على المؤمنين أمرهم، ولم يفرّق بين الحق والباطل.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mughīra and ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, altogether from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Allāh has not left the Earth be without a Scholar residing upon it, who knows about (unauthorised) additions and omissions (in religion). So, were the believers to add anything, he would reorient them (to what is correct), and if they were to fall short, he would complete it for them, saying: “Take it completely.” Were it not for that, the affairs of the believers would become disordered, and it would not be possible to differentiate between truth and falsehood.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl, from Abī Ḥamza, who said: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Can the Earth remain without an Imam?,” so he said: “Were the Earth to remain without an Imam, it would sink (into itself).”
arabicText: وعنه، عن محمّد بن عيسى، عن محمّد بن الفضيل، عن أبي حمزة قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: تبقى الأرض بغير إمام؟ قال: لو بقيت الأرض بغير إمام، لساخت.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl, from Abī Ḥamza, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Can the Earth remain without an Imam?,” so he said: “Were the Earth to remain without an Imam, it would sink (into itself).”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Aḥmad b. Idrīs, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad, from al-Khashshāb, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from Karām, who has said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said: “Were the people to constitute only two men, one of them would be the Imam.” And he said: “The Imam would be the last to die, lest anyone argue against Allāh that He left him without a Divine authority (to refer to).”
arabicText: أحمد بن إدريس، عن عبداللّه بن محمّد، عن الخشاب، عن جعفر بن محمّد، عن كرام، قال: قال أبو عبداللّه عليه السلام: لو كان الناس رجلين، لكان أحدهما الإمام. وقال: إنّ آخر من يموت الإمام، لئلّا يحتجّ أحد على الله أنه تركه بغير حجّة.
thaqalaynSanad: Aḥmad b. Idrīs, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad, from al-Khashshāb, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from Karām, who has said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Were the people to constitute only two men, one of them would be the Imam.” And he said: “The Imam would be the last to die, lest anyone argue against Allāh that He left him without a Divine authority (to refer to).”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Al-Ḥimyarī, from al-Sindī b. Muḥammad, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. Razīn, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said: “The Earth would not remain without an Imam, be he apparent or hidden.”
arabicText: الحميري، عن السندي بن محمّد، عن العلاء بن رزين، عن محمّد بن مسلم: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال: لا تبقى الأرض بغير إمام ظاهر أو باطن.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥimyarī, from al-Sindī b. Muḥammad, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. Razīn, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Earth would not remain without an Imam, be he apparent or hidden.”

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Ḥafṣ, from ʿAytham b. Aslam, from Dhurayḥ al-Muḥāribī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Dhurayḥ al-Muḥāribī narrated: “I heard him (Imam al-Ṣādiq (as)) saying: “By Allāh, the Earth has not been left by Allāh, ever since (the soul of) Ādam was seized, but that upon it is an Imam through whom one is guided to Allāh, and he is the Divine authority of Allāh upon the servants (of Allāh). Whoever abandons him perishes, while whoever holds fast to him is saved, and it is a right upon Allāh (taa).”[1]
arabicText: وعنه، عن إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن محمّد بن حفص، عن عيثم بن أسلم، عن ذريح المحاربي: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: قال: سمعته يقول: والله، ما ترك الله الأرض—منذ قبض آدم—إلّا وفيها إمام يهتدى به إلى الله، وهو حجّة الله على العباد، من تركه هلك ومن لزمه نجا، حقاً على الله تعالى.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Ḥafṣ, from ʿAytham b. Aslam, from Dhurayḥ al-Muḥāribī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Dhurayḥ al-Muḥāribī narrated: “I heard him (Imam al-Ṣādiq (as)) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “By Allāh, the Earth has not been left by Allāh, ever since (the soul of) Ādam was seized, but that upon it is an Imam through whom one is guided to Allāh, and he is the Divine authority of Allāh upon the servants (of Allāh). Whoever abandons him perishes, while whoever holds fast to him is saved, and it is a right upon Allāh (taa).”[1]

chapter: The Earth is Never Devoid of a Divine Authority
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from al-Ḥasan b. Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, and one another, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Indeed, Jibraʾīl (as) descended upon the Prophet (sawa) so that he may inform him of something from his Lord, so he said to him (from Allāh): “O’ Muḥammad! Indeed, I have not left the Earth without there being a Scholar residing upon it through whom (correct) obedience to Me, and My right guidance, is recognised, and he will be a means of salvation during the interval between the passing of one Prophet to the emergence of another. Nor have I left Iblis to misguide people without someone who is a Divine authority, acting on My behalf, upon the Earth, a missionary (inviting people) to Me, a guide to My path, and one cognisant of My ordinance. Verily, I have designated for every people a guide, through whom I guide the felicitous, and who is a Divine authority upon the wretched.”
arabicText: سعد، عن الحسن بن موسى الخشاب، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي نجران، عن عبدالكريم، وغيره: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: إنّ جبرئيل عليه السلام نزل على النبيّ صلى الله عليه وآله يخبر عن ربّه، فقال له: يا محمّد، إنّي لم أترك الأرض إلّا وفيها عالم يعرف طاعتي وهداي، ويكون نجاة فيما بين قبض النبيّ إلى خروج النبيّ الآخر، ولم أكن أترك إبليس يضلّ الناس وليس في الأرض حجّة لي، وداع إليّ، وهادٍ إلى سبيلي، وعارف بأمري، وإنّي قد قيّصت لكل قوم هادياً أهدي به السعداء ويكون حجّة على الأشقياء.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from al-Ḥasan b. Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, and one another, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Indeed, Jibraʾīl (as) descended upon the Prophet (sawa) so that he may inform him of something from his Lord, so he said to him (from Allāh): “O’ Muḥammad! Indeed, I have not left the Earth without there being a Scholar residing upon it through whom (correct) obedience to Me, and My right guidance, is recognised, and he will be a means of salvation during the interval between the passing of one Prophet to the emergence of another. Nor have I left Iblis to misguide people without someone who is a Divine authority, acting on My behalf, upon the Earth, a missionary (inviting people) to Me, a guide to My path, and one cognisant of My ordinance. Verily, I have designated for every people a guide, through whom I guide the felicitous, and who is a Divine authority upon the wretched.”

chapter: Divine Leadership/Imamate is a Covenant from Allāh (taa)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from ʿAlī b. Ismāʿīl, from al-ʿAbbās b. Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, who said: “Ismāʿīl b. ʿAmmār asked a question of the first Abā’l-Ḥasan (as),[1] so he said to him: “Has Allāh obliged the Imam to bequeath to and entrust the covenant to (his successor), before he departs from this world?,” so he replied: “Yes.” Ibn ʿAmmār then said: “Is it an obligation from Allāh?” The Imam replied: “Yes.”
arabicText: سعد، عن عليّ بن إسماعيل، عن العبّاس بن معروف، عن عليّ ابن مهزيار، عن الحسن بن عليّ بن فضّال، قال: سأل إسماعيل بن عمّار أبا الحسن الأوّل عليه السلام، فقال له: فرض الله على الإمام أن يوصي—قبل أن يخرج من الدنيا—ويعهد؟ فقال: نعم. فقال: فریضة من الله؟ قال: نعم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from ʿAlī b. Ismāʿīl, from al-ʿAbbās b. Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Ismāʿīl b. ʿAmmār asked a question of the first Abā’l-Ḥasan (as),[1] so he said to him: “Has Allāh obliged the Imam to bequeath to and entrust the covenant to (his successor), before he departs from this world?,” so he replied: “Yes.” Ibn ʿAmmār then said: “Is it an obligation from Allāh?” The Imam replied: “Yes.”

chapter: Divine Leadership/Imamate is a Covenant from Allāh (taa)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl and ʿAlī b. Asbāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr, from ʿAmrū b. al-Ashʿath, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Ibn al-Ashʿath narrated: “I heard him (Imam al-Ṣādiq) saying—and we were in the house with him, approximately twenty persons: “Perhaps you see that this ordinance belongs to a man from among us who assigns it wherever he wills?! No, by Allāh, it is a covenant from the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) characterised by explicit designation, from one man to another, until the Ordinance reaches its (final rightful) master.”
arabicText: وعنه، عن أحمد بن محمّد بن عيسى ومحمّد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن الحسن بن عليّ بن فضّال وعلي بن أسباط، عن عبداللّه بن بكير، عن عمرو بن الأشعث: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه‌ السلام: قال: سمعته يقول—ونحن في البيت معه نحو من عشرين إنساناً—: لعلكم ترون أنّ هذا الأمر إلى رجل منّا يضعه حيث يشاء؟! لا، والله، إنّه لعهد من رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله مسمّى رجل فرجل، حتى ينتهي الأمر إلى صاحبه.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl and ʿAlī b. Asbāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr, from ʿAmrū b. al-Ashʿath, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Ibn al-Ashʿath narrated: “I heard him (Imam al-Ṣādiq) saying—and we were in the house with him, approximately twenty persons:
thaqalaynMatn: “Perhaps you see that this ordinance belongs to a man from among us who assigns it wherever he wills?! No, by Allāh, it is a covenant from the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) characterised by explicit designation, from one man to another, until the Ordinance reaches its (final rightful) master.”

chapter: Divine Leadership/Imamate is a Covenant from Allāh (taa)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: And from him, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad, from Muḥammad b. ʿAmrū b. Saʿīd, from Yaḥyā b. Mālik, from Abī’l-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (as). Yaḥyā b. Mālik narrated: “I asked him about the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾Indeed Allāh commands you to deliver the trusts to their [rightful] owners﴿ [4:58]. He said: “The Imam delivers (the trust of Imamate) to the (next) Imam.” Then he said: “O’ Yaḥyā, indeed it is not from him, by Allāh. It is but an order from Allāh.”
arabicText: وعنه، عن أحمد بن محمّد، عن محمّد بن عمرو بن سعيد، عن يحيى بن مالك: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال: سألته عن قول الله عزّ وجلّ: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا۟ ٱلْأَمَـٰنَـٰتِ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهَا﴾. فقال: الإمام يؤدّي إلى الإمام. ثم قال: يا يحيى إنّه، والله، ليس مِنه، إنّما هو أمر من الله.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad, from Muḥammad b. ʿAmrū b. Saʿīd, from Yaḥyā b. Mālik, from Abī’l-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (as). Yaḥyā b. Mālik narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I asked him about the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾Indeed Allāh commands you to deliver the trusts to their [rightful] owners﴿ [4:58]. He said: “The Imam delivers (the trust of Imamate) to the (next) Imam.” Then he said: “O’ Yaḥyā, indeed it is not from him, by Allāh. It is but an order from Allāh.”

chapter: Divine Leadership/Imamate is a Covenant from Allāh (taa)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar, from Abī’l-Qāsim al-Hāshimī, from ʿUbayd b. Qays al-Anṣārī, who said: “al-Ḥasan b. Samāʿa narrated to us, from Jaʿfar b. Samāʿa, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Jibraʾīl descended upon the Prophet (sawa) with a scroll from the sky. Allāh has never revealed any book like it, before or after it. Within it are seals of gold. Jibraʾīl said to the Prophet: “O’ Muḥammad! This is your testament to the electee of your family.” He replied: “O’ Jibraʾīl, who is the electee of my family?,” so he said: “ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as). Command him, at the time of your passing, to break a seal, then act upon what is in it.” So, when the Prophet (as) died, ʿAlī broke a seal and then acted upon what was in it, and he did not go beyond it. He then handed it over to al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī (as), who broke a seal, acted upon what was within it without going beyond it, and handed it over to al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī (as). He broke a seal, and found (inscribed) within it: Go out, with a people, towards martyrdom, and sell your soul to Allāh,[1] so he acted upon what was within it and did not go beyond it. He then handed it over to a man after him, who broke a seal and found therein: Maintain inconspicuousness, be silent, hold fast to your domicile, and worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.[2] Then, he handed it over to a man after him, who broke a seal and found therein: That you narrate traditions to the people and give them legal rulings, and spread the knowledge of your forefathers. So, he did as per what was within it and then handed it over to a man after him. He broke a seal, and found therein: That you narrate traditions to the people and give them legal rulings, prove the truthfulness of your father, and fear none but Allāh, for you are under Allāh’s protection and guarantee. And he handed the scroll over to a man after him,[3] and he handed it over to who was after him, and he to who was after him, until the Day of Resurrection.”
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر، عن أبي القاسم الهاشميّ، عن عبيد بن قيس الأنصاري، قال: حدثنا الحسن بن سماعة، عن جعفر بن سماعة: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: نزل جبرئيل على النبيّ صلّى الله‌ عليه‌ وآله بصحيفة من السماء، لم ينزل الله كتاباً مثلها قطّ قبله ولا بعده، فيه خواتيم من ذهب فقال له: يا محمّد، هذه وصيّتك إلى النجيب من أهلك، قال له: يا جبرئيل، من النجيب من أهلي؟ قال: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام، مره إذا توفيت: أن يفكّ خاتماً ثمّ يعمل بما فيه. فلمّا قبض النبيّ عليه السلام، فكّ عليّ خاتماً ثم عمل بما فيه ما تعدّاه ثمّ دفعها إلى الحسن بن عليّ عليه السلام، ففكّ خاتماً وعمل بما فيه ما تعدّاه ثمّ دفعها إلى الحسين بن عليّ عليه السلام، ففكّ خاتماً، فوجد فيه: اُخرج بقوم إلى الشهادة لهم معك، واشر نفسك لله، فعمل بما فيها ما تعدّاه ثمّ دفعها إلى رجل بعده، ففكّ خاتماً، فوجد فيه: أطرق، واصمت والزم منزلك، واعبد ربّك حتى يأتيك اليقين. ثمّ دفعها إلى رجل بعده، ففكّ خاتماً، فوجد فيه: أن حدّث الناس وأفتهم، وانشر علم آبائك، ففعل بما فيه ما تعدّاه. ثمّ دفعها إلى رجل بعده، ففكّ خاتماً، فوجد فيه: أن حدّث الناس وأفتهم، وصدّق أباك ولا تخافنّ أحداً إلّا الله، فإنّك في حرز من الله وضمان. وهو يدفعها إلى رجل مِن بعده. ويدفعها مَن بعده إلى مَن بعده، إلى يوم القيامة.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar, from Abī’l-Qāsim al-Hāshimī, from ʿUbayd b. Qays al-Anṣārī, who said: “al-Ḥasan b. Samāʿa narrated to us, from Jaʿfar b. Samāʿa, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Jibraʾīl descended upon the Prophet (sawa) with a scroll from the sky. Allāh has never revealed any book like it, before or after it. Within it are seals of gold. Jibraʾīl said to the Prophet: “O’ Muḥammad! This is your testament to the electee of your family.” He replied: “O’ Jibraʾīl, who is the electee of my family?,” so he said: “ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as). Command him, at the time of your passing, to break a seal, then act upon what is in it.” So, when the Prophet (as) died, ʿAlī broke a seal and then acted upon what was in it, and he did not go beyond it. He then handed it over to al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī (as), who broke a seal, acted upon what was within it without going beyond it, and handed it over to al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī (as). He broke a seal, and found (inscribed) within it: Go out, with a people, towards martyrdom, and sell your soul to Allāh,[1] so he acted upon what was within it and did not go beyond it. He then handed it over to a man after him, who broke a seal and found therein: Maintain inconspicuousness, be silent, hold fast to your domicile, and worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.[2] Then, he handed it over to a man after him, who broke a seal and found therein: That you narrate traditions to the people and give them legal rulings, and spread the knowledge of your forefathers. So, he did as per what was within it and then handed it over to a man after him. He broke a seal, and found therein: That you narrate traditions to the people and give them legal rulings, prove the truthfulness of your father, and fear none but Allāh, for you are under Allāh’s protection and guarantee. And he handed the scroll over to a man after him,[3] and he handed it over to who was after him, and he to who was after him, until the Day of Resurrection.”

chapter: Allāh (azwj) has Selected the House of Muḥammad (as) for Imamate, to the Exclusion of all Others
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhayna, who said that Burayd b. Muʿāwiya al-ʿIjlī narrated to him, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) regarding the statement of Allāh (taa): ﴾Do they envy those people for what Allāh has given them out of His bounty?﴿ [4:54], so the Imam said: “We are the people envied for what Allāh has given us, of the Imamate, to the exclusion of all of His other creatures. ﴾We have certainly given the progeny of Ibrāhīm the Book and wisdom, and We have given them a great sovereignty﴿ [4:54]—He has made among them Apostles, Prophets and Imams. So how is it that they affirm as such for the House of Ibrāhīm, but deny it for the House of Muḥammad (as-p)? ﴾Of them are some who believe in him, and of them are some who deter [others] from him; and hell suffices for a blaze! Indeed We shall soon make those who deny Our signs enter a Fire: as often as their skins become scorched, We shall replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment. Indeed Allāh is all-mighty, all-wise. As for those who have faith and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them into gardens with streams running in them, to remain in them forever. In it, there will be chaste mates for them, and We shall admit them into a deep shade.﴿” [4:55-57]
arabicText: سعد، عن أحمد بن محمّد بن عيسى، عن أبيه، عن محمّد بن أبي عمير، عن ابن أُذينة، قال: حدّثني بريد بن معاوية العجلي: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قول الله تعالى: ﴿أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾. قال: فنحن المحسدون على ما آتانا الله من الإمامة، دون خلقه جميعاً، ﴿فَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ ءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُم مُّلْكًا عَظِيمًۭا﴾: فجعلنا منهم الرسل والأنبياء والأئمّة، فكيف يقرّون به في آل إبراهيم، وينكرونه في آل محمّد عليهم السلام؟ ﴿فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَمِنْهُم مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ ۚوَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا ۝ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ نَارًۭا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلْنَـٰهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا لِيَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ۗإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًۭا ۝ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًۭا ۖلَّهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَٰجٌۭ مُّطَهَّرَةٌۭ ۖوَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِلًّۭا ظَلِيلًا﴾.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhayna, who said that Burayd b. Muʿāwiya al-ʿIjlī narrated to him, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as)
thaqalaynMatn: regarding the statement of Allāh (taa): ﴾Do they envy those people for what Allāh has given them out of His bounty?﴿ [4:54], so the Imam said: “We are the people envied for what Allāh has given us, of the Imamate, to the exclusion of all of His other creatures. ﴾We have certainly given the progeny of Ibrāhīm the Book and wisdom, and We have given them a great sovereignty﴿ [4:54]—He has made among them Apostles, Prophets and Imams. So how is it that they affirm as such for the House of Ibrāhīm, but deny it for the House of Muḥammad (as-p)? ﴾Of them are some who believe in him, and of them are some who deter [others] from him; and hell suffices for a blaze! Indeed We shall soon make those who deny Our signs enter a Fire: as often as their skins become scorched, We shall replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment. Indeed Allāh is all-mighty, all-wise. As for those who have faith and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them into gardens with streams running in them, to remain in them forever. In it, there will be chaste mates for them, and We shall admit them into a deep shade.﴿” [4:55-57]

chapter: Allāh (azwj) has Selected the House of Muḥammad (as) for Imamate, to the Exclusion of all Others
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Mughīra and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Thaʿlaba b. Maymūn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Quṣayr,[1] who said: “I asked Abā Jaʿfar (as) about the saying of Allāh (taa): ﴾We have certainly given the progeny of Ibrāhīm the Book and wisdom, and We have given them a great sovereignty.﴿ [4:54]—What is the “great sovereignty”?,” so he replied: “It is ours.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Quṣayr continued his narration: “I said: “What thing is it?,” and he responded: “An obligation to take the Imam’s ally as one’s own, oppose his enemy, and take as Imams the Legatees after him. For indeed, they are my offspring, of my flesh and blood, and Allāh has granted them my understanding and my knowledge. I complain to Allāh about those who deny their distinction and sever my bond with them. By Allāh, they [2] will surely kill my son, so may Allāh not include them in my intercession.”[3]
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى والحسن بن علي بن عبداللّه بن المغيرة ومحمّد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطّاب، عن الحسن بن عليّ بن فضال، عن ثعلبة بن ميمون، عن عبدالرحمن القصير، قال: سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام، عن قول الله تعالى: ﴿فَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ ءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُم مُّلْكًا عَظِيمًۭا﴾. ما الملك العظيم؟ قال: فينا. قال: قلت: أيّ شيء؟ قال: افتراض. وليتولّ وليّه، ويعاد عدوّه، وليأتمّ بالأوصياء من بعده، فإنّهم عترتي من لحمي ودمي، أعطاهم الله فهمي وعلمي، إلى الله أشكوا المنكرين لفضلهم، القاطعين فيهم صلتي، وأيم الله ليقتلنّ ابني، لا أنالهم الله شفاعتي.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Mughīra and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Thaʿlaba b. Maymūn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Quṣayr,[1] who said:
