thaqalaynMatn: “There was a Prophet among the Children of Israel to whom Allāh had promised that He would help him in fifteen nights, but when he informed his people of that, they said: “By Allāh, when it happens, He will surely do such-and-such and such-and-such.” So, Allāh delayed it for fifteen years. There was another among them whom Allāh promised victory within fifteen years. When the Prophet (as) informed his people of that, they said: “It is as Allāh has willed,” so Allāh hastened it for them to fifteen nights.”

chapter: Miscellaneous Reports
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. Aḥmad, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Muḥammad b. Muslim narrated: “I was with him (Imam al-Ṣādiq) when Mihzam came in,[1] saying to him: “May I be sacrificed for you. Would you inform me of when this matter, for which we are waiting, will come to pass?” The Imam replied: “O’ Mihzam, the time-setters have lied and those who call for the matter to be hastened have perished,[2] while the ones who accept it as it is are saved, and to us they shall come.”
arabicText: محمّد بن يحيى، عن محمّد بن أحمد، عن صفوان بن يحيى، عن أبي أيوب الخزّاز، عن محمّد بن مسلم، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: كنت عنده، إذ دخل عليه مهزم، فقال له: جعلت فداك، أخبرني عن هذا الأمر الذي ننتظره، متى هو؟ قال: يا مهزم، كذب الوقّاتون، وهلك المستعجلون، ونجا المسلّمون، وإلينا يصيرون.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. Aḥmad, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Muḥammad b. Muslim narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I was with him (Imam al-Ṣādiq) when Mihzam came in,[1] saying to him: “May I be sacrificed for you. Would you inform me of when this matter, for which we are waiting, will come to pass?” The Imam replied: “O’ Mihzam, the time-setters have lied and those who call for the matter to be hastened have perished,[2] while the ones who accept it as it is are saved, and to us they shall come.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Imamate of Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Jawād and Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Hādī
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Refer to tradition no. 46 of our book, which is on Abī’l-Ḥasan al-Riḍā’s (as) explicit textual designation of his son.[1] And tradition no. 94—the Tradition of the Tablet [2]—which includes: “And ʿAlī (al-Riḍā), My vicegerent and supporter…for I will gladden his eye with Muḥammad (al-Jawād), his son, who is his caliph after him. For he is the inheritor of My knowledge, the repository of My wisdom, the locus of My secret and My Divine authority upon My creatures. I have made Paradise his residence and granted him the right of intercession for seventy people of his household, all of whom had deserved the Fire. And I will seal (this) with felicity for his son, ʿAlī (al-Hādī), My vicegerent and supporter, the witness (for Me) among My creation and My trustee in regard to My revelations. From him I will derive the missionary (inviting people) to My path and the custodian of My knowledge, al-Ḥasan (al-ʿAskarī). Then, I will complete that through his son, a mercy to the worlds…etc.” Refer, also, to tradition no. 93—the Tradition of al-Khiḍr [3]—in which is: “And I bear witness, in regard to Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, that he is the upholder of ʿAlī b. Mūsā’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness, in regard to ʿAlī b. Muḥammad, that he is the upholder of Muḥammad b. ʿAlī’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness, in regard to al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, that he is the upholder of ʿAlī b. Muḥammad’s Divine ordinance…etc.” And, in tradition no. 103:[4] “After al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, (it will be) among the descendants (of al-Ḥusayn), generation after generation.”
arabicText: لاحظ ح ٤٦ من كتابنا في نصّ أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام في ولده. وح ٩٤ ((حديث اللوح)) وفيه: ((وعليّ وليّي وناصري…لأقرنَّ عينه بمحمد إبنه وخليفته من بعده فهو وارث علمي ومعدن حكمتي وموضع سرّي وحجّتي على خلقي جعلت الجنّة مثواه وشفّعته في سبعين من أهل بيته كلّهم قد استوجبوا النار. وأختم بالسعادة لابنه عليّ وليّي وناصري والشاهد في خلقي وأميني على وحيي، أخرج منه الدّاعي الى سبيلي والخازن لعلمي الحسن ثمّ أكمل ذلك بابنه رحمة للعالمين…الخ)). ولاحظ ح ۹۳ ((حدیث الخضر)) وفيه: ((وأشهد على محمّد بن علي أنّه القائم بأمر علي بن موسى وأشهد على عليّ بن محمد أنّه القائم بأمر محمّد بن علي وأشهد على الحسن بن علي أنّه القائم بأمر عليّ بن محمد…الخ)). وح ۱۰۳ وفيه: ((بعد الحسن والحسين في الأعقاب بعد الأعقاب)).

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Imamate of Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī al-ʿAskarī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī said: “Aḥmad b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: “I entered upon our master, Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī al-ʿAskarī (as), whereupon he said: “O’ Aḥmad, what was your condition amid the doubt and uncertainty in which the people found themselves?” I said: “O’ my master! When the letter arrived, there remained no man, woman or boy, mature and comprehending, among us except that they accepted the truth.” The Imam replied: “Praise Allāh for that. O’ Aḥmad, did you all not know that the Earth is never devoid of a Divine authority? I am that Divine authority.” Imam al-ʿAskarī (saa) may have instead said: “I am the Divine authority.”
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، قال: حدّثنا أحمد بن اسحاق، قال: دخلت على مولانا أبي محمد الحسن بن علي العسكري عليه السلام، فقال: يا أحمد، ما كان حالكم فيما كان فيه الناس من الشكّ والارتياب؟ فقلت له: يا سيّدي، لمّا ورد الكتاب لم يبق منّا رجل ولا امرأة ولا غلام بلغ الفهم، إلّا قال بالحق، فقال:—إحمد الله على ذلك—يا أحمد، أما علمتم أنّ الأرض لا تخلو من حجّة، وأنا ذلك الحجّة، أو قال: أنا الحجّة.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī said: “Aḥmad b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “I entered upon our master, Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī al-ʿAskarī (as), whereupon he said: “O’ Aḥmad, what was your condition amid the doubt and uncertainty in which the people found themselves?” I said: “O’ my master! When the letter arrived, there remained no man, woman or boy, mature and comprehending, among us except that they accepted the truth.” The Imam replied: “Praise Allāh for that. O’ Aḥmad, did you all not know that the Earth is never devoid of a Divine authority? I am that Divine authority.” Imam al-ʿAskarī (saa) may have instead said: “I am the Divine authority.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Imamate of Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī al-ʿAskarī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Those who were present when al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī (as-p) died, and participated in his burial, narrated to us—so many that their number could not be determined, nor is it feasible for that many to have colluded upon a lie.”[1]
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه قال: حدّثنا من حضر موت الحسن بن علي بن محمد العسكري عليهم السلام ودفنه ممّن لا يوقف على إحصاء عددهم ولا يجوز على مثلهم التواطؤ بالكذب.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Those who were present when al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī (as-p) died, and participated in his burial, narrated to us—so many that their number could not be determined, nor is it feasible for that many to have colluded upon a lie.”[1]

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Imamate of the Qāʾim (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd and al-Ḥimyarī together, from Ibrāhīm b. Mahziyār, from his brother, ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from Faḍḍāla b. Ayyūb, from Abān b. ʿUthmān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-ʿAlāʾ narrated: “I said to him: “Can the Earth be without an Imam?” He said: “No.” I continued: “Can there be two Imams at one time?” He replied: “No, unless one of them is silent.” I asked: “Is the Imam cognisant of the Imam who comes after him?” He said: “Yes.” I followed up: “Is the Qāʾim an Imam?” He replied: “Yes. An Imam, the son of an Imam, who has already been taken as an Imam before that.”
arabicText: سعد والحميري معاً، عن إبراهيم بن مهزيار، عن أخيه علي بن مهزيار، عن فضالة بن أيوب، عن أبان بن عثمان، عن ابن أبي عمير، عن الحسين بن أبي العلاء، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: قلت له: تكون الأرض بغير إمام؟ قال: لا. قلت: أفيكون إمامان في وقت واحد؟ قال: لا، إلّا وأحدهما صامت. قلت: فالامام يعرف الامام الذي من بعده؟ قال: نعم. قال: قلت: القائم إمام؟ قال: نعم، إمام إبن إمام، قد اؤتمّ به قبل ذلك.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd and al-Ḥimyarī together, from Ibrāhīm b. Mahziyār, from his brother, ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from Faḍḍāla b. Ayyūb, from Abān b. ʿUthmān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-ʿAlāʾ narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to him: “Can the Earth be without an Imam?” He said: “No.” I continued: “Can there be two Imams at one time?” He replied: “No, unless one of them is silent.” I asked: “Is the Imam cognisant of the Imam who comes after him?” He said: “Yes.” I followed up: “Is the Qāʾim an Imam?” He replied: “Yes. An Imam, the son of an Imam, who has already been taken as an Imam before that.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Imamate of the Qāʾim (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that he spoke about the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾The day when some of your Lord’s signs do come, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed beforehand﴿ [6:158]—so, he said: “The signs are the Imams, and the awaited sign is the Qāʾim (as). So, on that day « faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed before » his rising with the sword, even if that soul had believed in the forefathers who preceded him (as-p).”[1]
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه قال: حدّثنا محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن علي بن رئاب، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام أنّه قال في قول الله عزّ وجلّ:﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِى بَعْضُ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَـٰنُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ ءَامَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾. فقال: الآيات هم الأئمّة، والآية المنتظرة هو القائم عليه السلام فيومئذ « لا ينفع نفساً إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل » قيامه بالسيف، وان آمنت بمن تقدّمه من آبائه عليهم السلام.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that

So, on that day « faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed before » his rising with the sword, even if that soul had believed in the forefathers who preceded him (as-p).”[1]

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: A Mention of the Tradition of the Tablet (Ḥadīth al-Lawḥ) & that the Twelfth Imam is the Divine Authority who is the Son of al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together, from Abī’l-Ḥasan Ṣāliḥ b. Abī Ḥammād and al-Ḥasan b. Ṭarīf together, from Bakr b. Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sālim, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who narrated: “My father (as) once said to Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī: “I have a need of you. So, when would it be convenient for you that I seclude myself with you so that I may ask you about it?” Jābir said to him: “Whenever you wish.” So, Abū Jaʿfar (as) secluded himself with him and said to him: “O’ Jābir, inform me about the Tablet which you saw in the hand of my mother, Fāṭima (as-f), the daughter of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa), and what she informed you was inscribed upon that Tablet.” Jābir responded: “I bear witness, by Allāh, that I once entered upon your mother, Fāṭima (as-f), during the lifetime of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) to congratulate her upon the birth of al-Ḥusayn (as), whereupon I saw in her hand a green Tablet. I supposed that it was made of emerald, and I saw upon it writing, white as sunlight. So, I said to her: “May my father and mother be made your ransom, o’ daughter of the Apostle of Allāh. What is this Tablet?” She said: “This is the Tablet which Allāh (azwj) gifted to His Apostle (sawa). In it are the name of my father, the name of my husband, the names of my two sons and the names of the Legatees from among my offspring. My father gave it to me to bring me comfort because of it.” Jābir said: “Your mother, Fāṭima (as-f), then gave it to me, so I read it and made a transcription of it.” My father (as) said to him: “Would you, o’ Jābir, show it to me?” He replied: “Yes.” So, my father (as) walked with him until they reached Jābir’s house, whereupon Jābir brought out for my father a scroll of parchment. My father said: “O’ Jābir, you look at your copy while I read it to you.” So, Jābir looked at his transcription while my father (as) read it to him—and, by Allāh, not a single letter differed from another. Jābir said: “I bear witness, by Allāh, that this is how I saw it inscribed upon the Tablet: In the name of Allāh, the Entirely and Innately Merciful. This is a book from Allāh, the supremely Majestic and Wise, to His light, His envoy, His veil and His proof, Muḥammad, which has been brought down by the Trusted Spirit from the Lord of the Worlds. O’ Muḥammad, exalt My names, express gratitude for My blessings and do not persistently deny My bounties. Verily, I am Allāh. There is no god but Me, Breaker of tyrants, Obliterator of the arrogant, Humiliator of oppressors and Reckoner of the Day of Reckoning. Verily, I am Allāh. There is no god but Me. So, whoever hopes for other than My favour or fears other than My justice, I will punish him with a punishment with which I have punished no-one among the worlds. So, worship Me alone, and place your trust in Me. I have never sent forth a Prophet, completed his days and brought his tenure to its conclusion without appointing for him a Legatee. I have favoured you over the Prophets and favoured your Legatee over the Legatees, and I have honoured you after him through your two lionets, your two grandsons, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. I have made Ḥasan the repository of My knowledge after the conclusion of his father’s term, and I have made Ḥusayn the custodian of My revelation, honoured him with martyrdom and sealed his life with felicity, for he is the best of those who are martyred and the highest of the martyrs in rank. I have placed My complete Word with him and My consummate Divine authority with him; through his posterity I reward and I punish. The first of them is ʿAlī, chief of the worshippers and ornament of My representatives who have passed on, and his son, the namesake of his praiseworthy forefather, Muḥammad—the one who will cleave open My knowledge and the repository of My wisdom. Those who doubt concerning Jaʿfar will perish; for the one who stands against him stands against Me. It is an utterance in truth from Me that I will surely honour Jaʿfar’s abode and will surely gladden him in regard to his representatives, his partisans and his supporters. And after him I have chosen Mūsā; there will be a blind, pitch-black tribulation, for the thread of My obligation will not be severed, My Divine authority will not be hidden and My representatives will never be wretched. See! Whoever persistently denies one of them has persistently denied My blessing, and whoever alters a verse of My Book has fabricated upon Me. Woe betide the fabricators upon the conclusion of the tenure of Mūsā, My servant, My beloved and My chosen one! See! The one who repudiates the eighth has repudiated all of My representatives. ʿAlī is My representative and supporter, the one upon whom I will place the burdens of prophethood and whom I will test in undertaking them. An arrogant rogue will murder him, and he will be buried in the city built by the righteous servant Dhū’l-Qarnayn, beside the most evil of My creation.[1] It is an utterance in truth from Me that I will surely gladden his eyes with Muḥammad, his son and his caliph after him, for he is the inheritor of My knowledge, the repository of My wisdom, the locus of My secret and My Divine authority over My creation. I have made Paradise his residence and granted him intercession for seventy members of his household, all of whom had deserved the Fire. And I will seal with felicity for his son ʿAlī, My representative and supporter, the witness among My creation and My trustee over My revelation. From him I will bring forth the missionary (inviting people) to My path and the custodian of My knowledge, al-Ḥasan. Then I will bring this to completion through his son, as a mercy to the worlds. Upon him will be the perfection of Mūsā, the splendour of ʿĪsā and the patience of Ayyūb. My representatives will be subjected to debasement during his time, and their heads will be passed around as gifts just as the heads of the Turks and Daylamites are passed around. They will be killed and burned, and will be fearful, terrified and apprehensive. The earth will be dyed with their blood, and lamentation and wailing will become prevalent among their women. Those are My representatives in truth. Through them I will repel every blind, pitch-black tribulation, through them I will dispel earthquakes, and I will remove from them their encumbrances and fetters. ﴾It is they who receive the blessings of their Lord and [His] mercy, and it is they who are the [rightly] guided.﴿ [2:157].” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sālim reported that Abū Baṣīr said: “Had you heard nothing in the course of your lifetime except this tradition, it would have sufficed you. So, keep it with only its people.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري جميعاً، عن أبي الحسن صالح بن أبي حماد، والحسن بن طريف جميعا:ً عن بكر بن صالح، عن عبدالرحمن بن سالم، عن أبي بصير، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: قال أبي عليه السلام لجابر بن عبداللّه الأنصاري: إنّ لي اليك حاجة، فمتى يخفّ عليك أن أخلو بك فأسألك عنها؟ فقال له جابر: في أيّ الأوقات شئت. فخلى به أبو جعفر عليه السلام، قال له: يا جابر، أخبرني عن اللّوح الذي رأيته في يد(ي) أُمّي فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وما أخبرتك به أنّه في ذلك اللّوح مكتوباً، فقال جابر: أشهد بالله، أنّي دخلت على اُمّك فاطمة عليها السلام في حياة رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله أُهنّئها بولادة الحسين عليه السلام، فرأيت في يدها لوحاً أخضر، ظننت أنّه من زمرّد، ورأيت فيه كتابة بيضاء شبيهة بنور الشمس، فقلت لها: بأبي أنتِ واُمّي، يابنت رسول الله ما هذا اللّوح؟ فقالت: هذا اللّوح أهداه الله عزّ وجلّ الى رسوله صلّى الله عليه وآله فيه إسم أبي، واسم بَعْلي، واسم إبنيّ، وأسماء الأوصياء من ولدي، فأعطانيه أبي ليسرّي بذلك. قال جابر: فأعطتنيه اُمّك فاطمة عليها السلام، فقرأته وانتسخته، فقال له أبي عليه السلام: فهل لك—يا جابر—أن تعرضه عليّ؟ فقال: نعم، فمشى معه أبي عليه السلام، حتى انتهى الى منزل جابر فأخرج الى أبي صحيفة من رقّ، فقال: يا جابر، اُنظر أنت في كتابك، لأقرأه أنا عليك. فنظر جابر في نسخته فقرأه عليه أبي عليه السلام، فوالله ما خالف حرف حرفاً قال جابر: فانّي اشهد بالله أنّي هكذا رأيته في اللوح مكتوباً: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم؛ هذا كتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم لمحمد نوره وسفیره وحجابه ودلیله، نزل به الرّوح الأمين من عند ربّ العالمين عظّم يا محمد أسمائي، واشكر نعمائي، ولا تجحد آلائي، إنّي أنا الله، لا إلٰه إلّا أنا، قاصم الجبّارين (ومبير المتكبّرين) ومذلّ الظالمين، وديّان يوم الدين، إنّي أنا الله، لا إلٰه إلّا أنا، فمن رجا غير فضلي أو خاف غير عدلي، عذبته عذاباً لا اُعذّبه أحداً من العالمين فايّاي فاعبد، وعليّ فتوكّل، إنّي لم أبعث نبيّاً، فأكملت أيّامه وانقضت مدّته، إلّا جعلت له وصيّاً، وانّي فضّلتك على الأنبياء، وفضّلت وصيك على الأوصياء وأكرمتك بشبليك بعده وبسبطيك الحسن والحسين، وجعلت حسناً معدن علمي بعد انقضاء مدّة أبيه، وجعلت حسيناً خازن وحيي، وأكرمته بالشهادة، وختمت له بالسعادة فهو أفضل من استشهد، وأرفع الشهداء درجة، جعلت كلمتي التامّة معه، والحجّة البالغة عنده، بعترته اُثيب واُعاقب، أوّلهم عليّ سيّد العابدين، وزين أوليائي الماضين، وابنه سميُّ جدّه المحمود، محمد الباقر العلمي والمعدن الحكمتي، سيهلك المرتابون في جعفر، الرادّ عليه كالراد عليّ، حقّ القول مني لأكرمنّ مثوى جعفر، ولاُسرنّه في أوليائه وأشياعه وأنصاره، وانـتـجـبـت « بعد » موسى « فتنة » عمياء حندس، لأنّ خيط فرضي لا ينقطع، وحجّتي لا تخفى، وأن أوليائي لا يشقون أبداً، ألا ومن جحد واحداً منهم فقد جحد نعمتي، ومن غيّر آية من كتابي فقد افترى عليّ، وويل للمفترين الجاحدين عند انقضاء مدّة عبدي موسى وحبيبي وخيرتي ألا إنّ المكذّب بالثامن مكذّب بكلّ أوليائي، وعليّ وليّي وناصري، ومن أضع عليه أعباء النبوّة، وأمتحنه بالاضطلاع، يقتله عفريت مستکبر، يدفن بالمدينة التي بناها العبد الصالح ذوالقرنين، الى جنب شرّ خلقي، حقّ القول منّي لاُقرّنّ عينه بمحمد إبنه وخليفته من بعده، فهو وارث علمي ومعدن حكمتي وموضع سرّي وحجّتي على خلقي، جعلت الجنّة مثواه وشفّعته في سبعين من أهل بيته كلّهم قد استوجبوا النار، وأختم بالسعادة لابنه عليّ وليّي وناصري، والشاهد في خلقي، وأميني على وحيي، أخرج منه الدّاعي الى سبيلي، والخازن لعلمي الحسن، ثمّ أكمل ذلك بابنه، رحمة للعالمين، علیه کمال موسی، وبهاء عيسى وصبر أيوب، ستذلّ أوليائي في زمانه، ويتهادون رؤوسهم كما تهادى رؤوس الترك والديلم، فيقتلون ويحرقون، ويكونون خائفين مرعوبين وجلين، تصبغ الأرض من دمائهم، ويفشو الويل والرّنين في نسائهم، اُولئك أوليائي حقاً، بهم أدفع كلّ فتنة عمياء حـنـدس، وبهم أكشف الزّلازل، وأرفع عنهم الآصار والأغلال ﴿أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَٰتٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌۭ ۖوَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُهْتَدُونَ﴾. قال عبدالرحمن بن سالم: قال أبو بصير: لو لم تسمع في دهرك إلّا هذا الحديث لكفاك، فصنه إلّا عن أهله.

From him I will bring forth the missionary (inviting people) to My path and the custodian of My knowledge, al-Ḥasan. Then I will bring this to completion through his son, as a mercy to the worlds. Upon him will be the perfection of Mūsā, the splendour of ʿĪsā and the patience of Ayyūb. My representatives will be subjected to debasement during his time, and their heads will be passed around as gifts just as the heads of the Turks and Daylamites are passed around. They will be killed and burned, and will be fearful, terrified and apprehensive. The earth will be dyed with their blood, and lamentation and wailing will become prevalent among their women. Those are My representatives in truth. Through them I will repel every blind, pitch-black tribulation, through them I will dispel earthquakes, and I will remove from them their encumbrances and fetters. ﴾It is they who receive the blessings of their Lord and [His] mercy, and it is they who are the [rightly] guided.﴿ [2:157].” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sālim reported that Abū Baṣīr said: “Had you heard nothing in the course of your lifetime except this tradition, it would have sufficed you. So, keep it with only its people.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: A Mention of the Tradition of the Tablet (Ḥadīth al-Lawḥ) & that the Twelfth Imam is the Divine Authority who is the Son of al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār and Aḥmad b. Idrīs altogether said: “Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to us, saying: “Abū Hāshim Dāwūd b. al-Qāsim al-Jaʿfarī narrated to us, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī Muḥammad b. ʿAlī (as-d), who said: “One day, Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) approached, and with him were al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī and Salmān al-Fārisī (ra), and Amīr al-Muʾminīn was leaning on Salmān’s hand, whereupon they entered the Sacred Mosque and sat down. A handsome-looking, well-dressed man approached, greeting Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) with a greeting of peace he reciprocated, so the man sat down. Then, he said: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I would ask you three questions. If you inform me (about the truth) in regard to them, I will have known that the people have undertaken, in regard to the Divine ordinance you are currently in charge of,[1] something I deem to have rendered them unreliable in both their worldly affairs as well as those of the Hereafter. But, if it be otherwise, I will know that you and they are on the same footing.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) responded to him: “Ask me. What has occurred to you?” The man said: “Inform me about when a man sleeps, where does his soul go? And about how a man remembers or forgets? And about why a man’s progeny (sometimes) resembles their paternal or maternal uncles?” Amīr al-Muʾminīn turned to Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan, and said: “Answer him, o’ Abā Muḥammad.” Imam al-Ḥasan al-Mujtabā (saa) said: “As for what you have asked in regard to the matter of man in terms of where his soul goes while he is asleep, then (consider that) the soul is attached to the wind, and the wind is attached to the air, until such time as it stirs its owner to wake up. If Allāh (azwj) permits that soul to return to its owner, that soul will pull on the wind, and that wind will pull on the air until the soul returns and resides tranquilly in the body of its owner. If Allāh (azwj) does not permit that soul to return to the body of its owner, the air pulls on the wind, and the wind pulls on the soul, so it will not return to the body of its owner until such time as he is resurrected. As for what you have mentioned in regard to the matter of remembrance and forgetfulness, the heart of a man is in a receptacle, and over the receptacle is a covering. So, if the man sends, at that point, salutations upon Muḥammad and the House of Muḥammad with a complete salutation, then that covering will be taken off that receptacle, the heart will lighten up and the man will remember what he had forgotten. And, if he does not send salutations upon Muḥammad and the House of Muḥammad, or there is deficiency in his salutations upon them,[2] then that covering closes over that receptacle so that the heart is darkened, and the man forgets what he had remembered. As for what you have mentioned in regard to the matter of a newborn who resembles his paternal or maternal uncles—when a man comes onto his wife and has intercourse with her with a tranquil heart, calm veins and an undisturbed body, then that drop of semen comes to reside tranquilly in the womb’s cavity, and the child comes out resembling his father and mother. But, if he comes onto her with a heart that is not tranquil, veins that are not calm and body that is agitated, he will have agitated that drop of semen, and in a disturbed state it will collide with some veins. If it collides with one of the veins associated with his maternal uncles, the boy will come out resembling his maternal uncles.” So, the man said: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allāh, and I have never ceased to bear witness as such. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Apostle of Allāh, and I have never ceased to bear witness as such. And I bear witness that you are his Legatee and the Upholder of his Divine authority after him”—and he pointed, with his hand, towards Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as)—“and I have never ceased to bear witness as such. And I bear witness that you are his Legatee and the Upholder of his Divine authority after him”—and he pointed towards al-Ḥasan (as)—“and I bear witness that al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī is the Legatee of your father and the Upholder of his Divine authority after you.[3] And I bear witness upon ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, that he is the Upholder of al-Ḥusayn’s Divine ordinance after him. And I bear witness upon Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, that he is the Upholder of ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, that he is the Upholder of Muḥammad b. ʿAlī’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon Mūsā b. Jaʿfar, that he is the Upholder of Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon ʿAlī b. Mūsā, that he is the Upholder of Mūsā b. Jaʿfar’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, that he is the Upholder of ʿAlī b. Mūsā’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon ʿAlī b. Muḥammad, that he is the Upholder of Muḥammad b. ʿAlī’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, that he is the Upholder of ʿAlī b. Muḥammad’s Divine ordinance. And I bear witness upon a man from the offspring of al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, who is not to be called by his teknonym or given name until his matter becomes apparent, whereupon he will fill the Earth with justice as it was previously full of iniquity. And peace be upon you, o’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and the mercy of Allāh and His blessings.” The man then stood up and left. Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said: “O’ Abā Muḥammad! Follow him, so that you may see where he is going.” Al-Ḥasan (as) exited (the Sacred Mosque) out onto his path, and said: “As soon as he stepped outside the Mosque, I could no longer tell where in Allāh’s land he had gone, so I returned to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as), and let him know.” He said: “O’ Abā Muḥammad, did you recognise him?” I replied: “Allāh, His Apostle and Amīr al-Muʾminīn know best.” Imam ʿAlī (saa) said: “He is al-Khiḍr (as).”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، ومحمد بن يحيى العطار، وأحمد بن ادريس، جميعاً قالوا: حدّثنا أحمد بن أبي عبداللّه البرقي، قال: حدّثنا أبو هاشم داود بن القاسم الجعفري، عن أبي جعفر الثاني محمد بن عليّ عليهما السلام قال: أقبل أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام ذات يوم ومعه الحسن بن عليّ وسلمان الفارسيّ رضي الله عنه، وأمير المؤمنين متّكئ على يد سلمان، فدخل المسجد الحرام فجلس، إذ أقبل رجل حسن الهيئة واللّباس، فسلّم على أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فردّ عليه السلام فجلس، ثمّ قال: يا أمير المؤمنين أسألك عن ثلاث مسائل إن أخبرتني بهنّ علمت أنّ القوم ركبوا من أمرك ما أقضي عليهم أنّهم ليسوا بمأمونين في دنياهم ولا في آخرتهم، وان تكن الاُخرى علمت أنّك وهم شرع سواء. فقال له أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: سلني عمّا بدا لك؟ فقال: أخبرني عن الرجل اذا نام أين تذهب روحه؟ وعن الرّجل كيف يذكر وينسى؟ وعن الرجل كيف يشبه ولده الأعمام والأخوال؟ فالتفت أمير المؤمنين الى أبي محمد الحسن فقال: يا با محمد أجبه. فقال: أمّا ما سألت عنه من أمر الانسان إذا نام أين تذهب روحه، فانّ روحه متعلّقة بالرّيح والرّيح متعلّقة بالهواء الى وقت ما يتحرّك صاحبها لليقظة، فان أذن الله عزّ وجلّ بردّ تلك الرّوح الى صاحبها جذبت تلك الرّوح الرّيح، وجذبت تلك الرّيح الهواء، فرجعت الرّوح فاسكنت في بدن صاحب، وان لم يأذن الله عز وجلّ بردّ تلك الرّوح الى صاحبها جذب الهواء الرّيح، وجذبت الرّيح الروح، فلم تردّ الى صاحبها الى وقت ما يبعث، وأمّا ما ذكرت من أمر الذّكر والنسيان: فانّ قلب الرّجل في حقّ، على الحقّ طبق فان صلّى الرجل عند ذلك على محمد وآل محمد صلاة تامّة إنكشف ذلك الطبق عن ذلك الحقّ فأضاء القلب وذكر الرّجل ما كان نسيه، وان هو لم يصلّ على محمد وآل محمد أو نقص من الصلاة عليهم انطبق ذلك الطبق على ذلك الحقّ فأظلم القلب ونسي الرّجل ما كان ذكر. أمّا ما ذكرت من أمر المولود الذي يشبه أعمامه وأخواله، فانّ الرّجل اذا أتى أهله فجامعها بقلب ساكن وعروق هادئة و بدن غير مضطرب فأسكنت تلك النطفة في جوف الرّحم خرج الولد يشبه أباه وأُمّه، وان هو أتاها بقلب غیر ساکن وعروق غير هادئة وبدن مضطرب، اضطربت تلك النطفة فوقعت في حال اضطرابها على بعض العروق فان وقعت على عرق من عروق الأخوال أشبه الرّجل أخواله، فقال الرّجل: أشهد أن لا إله إلّا الله، ولم أزل أشهد بها، وأشهد أنّ محمداً رسول الله، ولم أزل أشهد بها، وأشهد أنّك وصيه والقائم بحجّته بعده—وأشار بيده الى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام—ولم أزل أشهد بها، وأشهد أنك وصيّه والقائم بحجّته—وأشار الى الحسن عليه السلام—وأشهد أنّ الحسين بن عليّ وصيّ أبيك والقائم بحجّته بعدك، وأشهد على عليّ بن الحسين أنّه القائم بأمر الحسين بعده، وأشهد على محمد بن علي أنّه القائم بأمر عليّ بن الحسين، وأشهد على جعفر بن محمد أنّه القائم بأمر محمد بن عليّ، وأشهد على موسى بن جعفر أنّه القائم بأمر جعفر بن محمد، وأشهد على عليّ ابن موسى أنّه القائم بأمر موسى بن جعفر، وأشهد على محمد بن علي أنّه القائم بأمر علي بن موسى، وأشهد على عليّ بن محمد أنه القائم بأمر محمد بن عليّ، وأشهد على الحسن بن عليّ أنّه القائم بأمر عليّ بن محمد، وأشهد على رجل من ولد الحسن ابن عليّ لا يكنّى ولا يسمّى حتى يظهر أمره فيملأ الأرض عدلاً كما ملئت جوراً، والسلام عليك يا أمير المؤمنين ورحمة الله وبركاته، ثمّ قام فمضى. فقال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: يا أبا محمد اتبعه فأنظر أين يقصد؟ فخرج الحسن عليه السلام في أثره، قال: فما كان إلّا أن وضع رجله خارج المسجد فما دريت أين أخذ من أرض الله، فرجعت الى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام، فأعلمته. فقال: يا أبا محمد أتعرفه؟ فقلت: الله ورسوله وأمير المؤمنين أعلم، فقال: هو الخضر عليه السلام.

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Birth of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Al-Ḥasan b. Mūsā al-Khashshāb narrated to us from Isḥāq b. Muḥammad b. Ayyūb, who narrated: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Mūsā (as) saying: “The Master of this Ordinance is he about whom people will say: “He has not yet been born.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا الحسن بن موسى الخشّاب عن اسحاق ابن محمد بن أيوب، قال: سمعت أبا الحسن عليّ بن محمد بن علي بن موسى عليه السلام يقول: صاحب هذا الأمر من يقول الناس: لَمْ يولد بَعْد.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Al-Ḥasan b. Mūsā al-Khashshāb narrated to us from Isḥāq b. Muḥammad b. Ayyūb, who narrated: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Mūsā (as) saying:

chapter: The Birth of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Al-Muʿallā b. Muḥammad al-Baṣrī narrated to us, from Muḥammad b. Jumhūr and another (from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr) from ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). He (ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān) expressed: “I heard him (Imam al-Ṣādiq) saying: “In regard to the Qāʾim (as), there is a precedent from Mūsā b. ʿImrān (as).” I asked: “And what is the precedent from Mūsā b. ʿImrān?,” to which he replied: “The concealment of his birth, and his occultation from his people.” I followed up: “For how many years was Mūsā b. ʿImrān occulted from his family and his people?” He said: “Twenty-eight years.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا المعلّى بن محمد البصري عن محمد بن جمهور وغيره (عن « محمد » بن أبي عمير) عن عبداللّه بن سنان، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام قال: سمعته يقول: في القائم عليه السلام سنّة من موسى بن عمران علیه السلام. فقلت: وما سنّته من موسی بن عمران؟ قال: خفاء مولده، وغيبته عن قومه. فقلت: وكم غاب موسى عن أهله وقومه؟ فقال: ثماني وعشرين سنة.

chapter: The Mahdī is of the Descendants of al-Ḥusayn (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muskān, from Abān b. Taghlib, from Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilālī, from Salmān al-Fārisī (ra), who narrated: “I entered upon the Prophet (sws) while al-Ḥusayn was on his lap and he was kissing al-Ḥusayn’s eyes and mouth, saying: “You are a master and the son of a master, and you are an Imam and the son of an Imam, and the father of the Imams. You are the Divine authority of Allāh and the son of His Divine authority, and the father of nine Divine authorities originating from your loins, the ninth of whom is their Qāʾim.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا يعقوب بن يزيد، عن حمّاد بن عيسى عن عبداللّه بن مسكان، عن أبان بن تغلب، عن سليم بن قيس الهلالي، عن سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه، قال: دخلت على النبي صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلّم، فاذا الحسين بن عليّ على فخذه، وهو يقبّل عينيه ويلثم فاه، ويقول: أنت سيّد ابن سيّد، أنت إمام ابن إمام أبو أئمة، أنت حجّة الله ابن حجّته، وأبو حجج تسعة من صلبك، تاسعهم قائمهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muskān, from Abān b. Taghlib, from Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilālī, from Salmān al-Fārisī (ra), who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I entered upon the Prophet (sws) while al-Ḥusayn was on his lap and he was kissing al-Ḥusayn’s eyes and mouth, saying: “You are a master and the son of a master, and you are an Imam and the son of an Imam, and the father of the Imams. You are the Divine authority of Allāh and the son of His Divine authority, and the father of nine Divine authorities originating from your loins, the ninth of whom is their Qāʾim.”

chapter: The Mahdī is of the Descendants of al-Ḥusayn (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar b. Udhayna, from Abān b. Abī ʿAyyāsh, from Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilālī, who said: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ṭayyār saying: “We were with Muʿāwiya, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (as-d), ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, ʿUmar b. Abī Salama, and Usāma b. Zayd,” whereupon he mentioned a discussion that occurred between him and Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān, in which he said to Muʿāwiya: “I heard the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) saying: “Indeed, I am closer to the faithful than their own souls.[1] Then, my brother, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as) is closer to the faithful than their own souls. So, when he is martyred, then my scion, al-Ḥasan, is closer to the faithful than their own souls. Then, my scion, al-Ḥusayn, is closer to the faithful than their own souls. So, when he is martyred, then his son, ʿAlī, is closer to the faithful than their own souls. You will come to know him, o’ ʿAlī! Then his son, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, is closer to the faithful than their own souls. You will come to know him, o’ Ḥusayn!”[2] Then the succession is completed as twelve Imams, nine from among the offspring of al-Ḥusayn.” ʿAbd Allāh (b. Jaʿfar al-Ṭayyār) said: “I then called upon al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (saa-d), ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, ʿUmar b. Abī Salama and Usāma b. Zayd to bear witness, so they bore witness for me, before Muʿāwiya.” Sulaym b. Qays said: “I heard that from Salmān, Abī Dharr, al-Miqdād and Usāma b. Zayd,[3] whereupon they narrated it to me that they heard it from the Apostle of Allāh (sws) himself.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن عمر بن اُذينة، عن أبان بن أبي عيّاش، عن سليم بن قيس الهلالي، قال: سمعت عبداللّه بن جعفر الطيّار، يقول: كنّا عند معاوية والحسن والحسين عليهما السلام، وعبداللّه بن عبّاس، وعمر بن أبي سلمة، واُسامة بن زيد—فذكر حديثاً جرى بينه وبينه، أنّه قال لمعاوية بن أبي سفيان—: سمعت رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله، يقول: إنّي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم. ثمّ أخي علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم، فاذا استشهد، فابني الحسن أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم، ثم إبني الحسين أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم، فاذا استشهد، فابنه عليّ أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم، وستدركه يا عليّ، ثمّ ابنه محمد بن عليّ أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم، وستدركه يا حسين، ثمّ تكمله إثني عشر إماماً، تسعة من ولد الحسين. قال عبداللّه: ثمّ استشهدت الحسن والحسين صلوات الله عليهما، وعبداللّه بن عبّاس وعمر بن أبي سلمة واُسامة بن زيد، فشهدوا لي عند معاوية. قال سليم بن قيس: وقد كنت سمعت ذلك من سلمان وأبي ذرّ والمقداد واُسامة بن زيد، فحدّثوني أنهم سمعوا ذلك من رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلّم.

author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, from Jābir al-Juʿfī from Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather (as-p), who said: “The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) once said to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as): “O’ ʿAlī! You and I, your two sons, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and nine descendants of al-Ḥusayn are the cornerstones of the religion and the mainstays of Islam. Whoever follows us is saved, and whoever holds back from us is destined for the Fire.”
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن أبي الخطّاب، عن محمد بن سنان، عن المفضّل بن عمر الجعفي، عن جابر الجعفي عن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن جدّه عليهم السلام، قال: قال رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله لعلي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام: يا عليّ أنا وأنت وابناك الحسن والحسين، وتسعة من ولد الحسين أركان الدين ودعائم الاسلام، من تبعنا نجا، ومن تخلّف عنّا فالى النار.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, from Jābir al-Juʿfī from Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather (as-p), who said: “The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) once said to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as):

englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from Mūsā b. al-Qāsim al-Bajallī, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Samāʿa, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muskān, from al-Ḥakam b. al-Ṣalt, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Bāqir, from his forefathers (as-p), who narrate: “The Apostle of Allāh (sws) said: “Hold fast to the belt of this one whose hairline is receding,” referring to ʿAli—“for he is the greatest Truthful one, and the Distinguisher, who distinguishes between Truth and falsehood. Whoever loves him has been guided by Allāh, and Allāh hates whoever hates him. Whoever remains behind him will be obliterated by Allāh, and from him are the two grandsons of my community, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, my two scions, and from al-Ḥusayn are the guiding Imams. Allāh has granted them my knowledge and my understanding, so affirm them as the ones in charge and do not take anyone besides them as a confidant,[1] lest wrath from your Lord descend upon you. Upon whomever wrath from his Lord descends is truly lost, and ﴾the life of this world is nothing but the wares of delusion.﴿” [3:185]
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن عيسى، عن موسى بن القاسم البجلّي، عن جعفر بن محمد بن سماعة، عن عبداللّه بن مسكان، عن الحكم بن الصلت، عن أبي جعفر الباقر، عن آبائه عليهم السلام قال: قال رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلّم: خذوا بحجزة هذا الأنزع يعني عليّاً—فانّه الصدّيق الأكبر، وهو الفاروق، يفرّق بين الحقّ والباطل، من أحبّه هداه الله ومن أبغضه أبغضه الله، ومن تخلّف عنه محقه الله، ومنه سبطا اُمّتي: الحسن والحسين، هما إبناي، ومن الحسين أئمة هداة، أعطاهم الله علمي وفهمي، فتولّوهم ولا تتّخذوا وليجة من دونهم، فيحلّ عليكم غضب من ربّكم ومن يحلل عليه غضب من ربّه فقد هوى، ﴿وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْغُرُورِ﴾.

chapter: The Mahdī is the Fifth of the Descendants of the Seventh (Mūsā al-Kāẓim (as)) & its Particulars
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿĪsā b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, from ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his brother, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar (as-d), who said: “When the fifth of the seventh’s offspring has become unaccounted for, then for Allāh’s sake, maintain your religious commitments! Do not let anyone turn you away from them. O’ sons of mine, it is necessary for the Master of this Ordinance to undergo an occultation such that he who affirmed this Ordinance will recant his affirmation. It is only a tribulation from Allāh (azwj) by which He tests His creatures. Had your forefathers and ancestors known of a religion more correct than this one, they would have followed it.” I (ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar) asked: “O’ my master, what is the fifth of the seventh’s offspring?,” to which he responded: “O’ sons of mine, your intellects are too feeble for that, and your forbearances are too constricted to bear it. But if you live, you will encounter it.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن الحسن بن عيسى بن محمد بن عليّ بن جعفر عن أبيه، عن جدّه محمد بن عليّ، عن علي بن جعفر، عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليهما السلام، قال: اذا فقد الخامس من ولد السابع، فالله الله في أديانكم لا يزيلنكم أحد عنها يا بنيّ: انّه لابدّ لصاحب هذا الأمر من غيبة حتى يرجع عن هذا الأمر من كان يقول به، إنّما هي محنة من الله عزّ وجلّ إمتحن بها خلقه، ولو علم آباؤكم وأجدادكم ديناً أصحّ من هذا لاتبّعوه. فقلت: يا سيّدي، وما الخامس من ولد السابع؟ فقال: يا بنيّ عقولكم تضعف عن ذلك وأحلامكم تضيق عن حملهِ ولكن إن تعيشوا فسوف تدركونه.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿĪsā b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his father, from his grandfather Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, from ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his brother, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar (as-d), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “When the fifth of the seventh’s offspring has become unaccounted for, then for Allāh’s sake, maintain your religious commitments! Do not let anyone turn you away from them. O’ sons of mine, it is necessary for the Master of this Ordinance to undergo an occultation such that he who affirmed this Ordinance will recant his affirmation. It is only a tribulation from Allāh (azwj) by which He tests His creatures. Had your forefathers and ancestors known of a religion more correct than this one, they would have followed it.” I (ʿAlī b. But if you live, you will encounter it.”

author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh

Abī Ḥayya, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “When three names come together in a sequence: Muḥammad, ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan, then the fourth is the Qāʾim.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه عن الحسن بن علي الزيتوني، ومحمد بن أحمد بن أبي قتادة، عن أحمد بن هلال، عن اُميّة بن عليّ، عن أبي الهيثم بن أبي حيّة عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام، قال: اذا اجتمعت ثلاثة أسماء متوالية: محمد، وعلي، والحسن فالرابع القائم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī al-Zaytūnī, and Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. Abī Qutāda, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl, from Umayya b. ʿAlī, from Abī’l-Haytham b. Abī Ḥayya, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “When three names come together in a sequence: Muḥammad, ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan, then the fourth is the Qāʾim.”

chapter: The Mahdī is the Fifth of the Descendants of the Seventh (Mūsā al-Kāẓim (as)) & its Particulars
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī from Aḥmad b. Hilāl al-ʿAbartāʾī, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as). Al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb narrated: “He said to me: “There must be a deaf and crushing tribulation on account of which all intimate confidants and close associates will fall away, and that is when the third of my descendants will become unaccounted for among our partisans. The people of heaven and earth, and every grieving man and woman, and every sorrowful and every anguished person, will weep.” He (as) then said: “May my father and mother be sacrificed for him, he is named after my grandfather (sawa) while resembling Mūsā b. ʿImrān (as). Upon him are folds of light, blazing intensely with the rays of sanctified radiance. How many a grieving believing woman, and how many a distressed, bewildered and sorrowful believing man there will be, at the loss of running water!”[1]
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري عن أحمد بن هلال العبرتائي، عن الحسن ابن محبوب، عن أبي الحسن علي بن موسى الرضا عليه السلام قال: قال لي: لابدّ من فتنة صمّاء صيلم يسقط فيها كلّ بطانة ووليجة وذلك عند فقدان الشيعة الثالث من ولدي، يبكي عليه أهل السماء وأهل الأرض، وكلّ حرّى وحرّان وكل حزين ولهفان، ثمّ قال عليه السلام: بأبي واُمّي سميّ جدّي صلّى الله عليه وآله وشبيه موسى بن عمران علیه السلام عليه جيوب النور، يتوقّد من شعاع ضياء القدس، كم من حرّى مؤمنة، وكم من مؤمن متأسّف حیران حزين عند فقدان الماء المعين.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī from Aḥmad b. Hilāl al-ʿAbartāʾī, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as). Al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb narrated: “He said to me:
thaqalaynMatn: “There must be a deaf and crushing tribulation on account of which all intimate confidants and close associates will fall away, and that is when the third of my descendants will become unaccounted for among our partisans. The people of heaven and earth, and every grieving man and woman, and every sorrowful and every anguished person, will weep.” He (as) then said: “May my father and mother be sacrificed for him, he is named after my grandfather (sawa) while resembling Mūsā b. ʿImrān (as). Upon him are folds of light, blazing intensely with the rays of sanctified radiance. category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār said: “Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik narrated to us, saying: “Ḥamdān b. Manṣūr narrated to me, from Saʿd b. Muḥammad, from ʿĪsā al-Khashshāb, who narrated: “I said to al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī (as): “Are you the Master of this Ordinance?”[1] He replied: “No, but the Master of the Ordinance is the wandering fugitive whose father’s blood remains unavenged, known by his uncle’s teknonym,[2] who will keep his sword on his shoulder for eight months.”
arabicText: محمد بن يحيى العطّار، قال: حدّثنا جعفر بن محمد بن مالك، قال: حدّثني حمدان بن منصور، عن سعد بن محمد، عن عيسى الخشّاب قال: قلت للحسين بن علي عليه السلام: أنت صاحب هذا الأمر؟ قال: لا، ولكن صاحب الأمر الطريد الشريد الموتور بأبيه، المكنّى بعمّه، يضع سيفه على عاتقه ثمانية أشهر.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār said: “Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik narrated to us, saying: “Ḥamdān b. Manṣūr narrated to me, from Saʿd b. Muḥammad, from ʿĪsā al-Khashshāb, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī (as): “Are you the Master of this Ordinance?”[1] He replied: “No, but the Master of the Ordinance is the wandering fugitive whose father’s blood remains unavenged, known by his uncle’s teknonym,[2] who will keep his sword on his shoulder for eight months.”

chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghafārī, from both Jaʿfar b. Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥusayn b. Zayd, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his forefathers (as-p), who narrated: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (saa) said: “There will never cease to be among my posterity one who is trusted and hoped for.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن يعقوب بن يزيد، عن عبداللّه الغفاري، عن جعفر بن ابراهيم والحسين بن زيد جميعاً، عن أبي عبداللّه، عن آبائه عليهم السلام، قال: قال أمير المؤمنين صلوات الله عليه: لا يزال في ولدي مأمون مأمول.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghafārī, from both Jaʿfar b. Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥusayn b. Zayd, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his forefathers (as-p), who narrated: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (saa) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “There will never cease to be among my posterity one who is trusted and hoped for.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, saying that Mūsā b. ʿUmar b. Yazīd al-Ṣayqal narrated to him, from ʿAlī b. Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾Say, ‘Tell me, should your water sink down [into the ground], who will bring you running water?’﴿ [67:30]—so he said: “This verse was revealed about the Qāʾim. He (Allāh) is saying: “Were your Imam to become occulted from you, and you would not know where he is, who would bring you an apparent Imam who brings you reports about heaven and earth, and that which Allāh (azwj) has made permissible, and what He has made impermissible?” He (as) then said: “By Allāh, the realisation of this verse has not yet come. Its realisation will come, as it must.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه قال: حدّثني موسى بن عمر بن يزيد الصيقل، عن علي بن أسباط، عن علي بن أبي حمزة، عن أبي بصير، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قول الله عزّ وجلّ: ﴿قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْرًۭا فَمَن يَأْتِيكُم بِمَآءٍۢ مَّعِينٍۭ﴾. فقال: هذه الآية نزلت في القائم، يقول: إن أصبح إمامكم غائباً عنكم لا تدرون أين هو، فمن يأتيكم بامام ظاهر، يأتيكم بأخبار السماء والأرض وحلال الله جلّ وعزّ وحرامه. ثمّ قال عليه السلام: والله ما جاء تأويل هذه الآية، ولابدّ أن يجيء تأويلها.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, saying that Mūsā b. ʿUmar b. Yazīd al-Ṣayqal narrated to him, from ʿAlī b. Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (as),
thaqalaynMatn: in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾Say, ‘Tell me, should your water sink down [into the ground], who will bring you running water?’﴿ [67:30]—so he said: “This verse was revealed about the Qāʾim. He (Allāh) is saying: “Were your Imam to become occulted from you, and you would not know where he is, who would bring you an apparent Imam who brings you reports about heaven and earth, and that which Allāh (azwj) has made permissible, and what He has made impermissible?” He (as) then said: “By Allāh, the realisation of this verse has not yet come. Its realisation will come, as it must.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The Qāʾim will go forth without an allegiance to anyone (binding) on his neck.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن عبيد ومحمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن جميل بن صالح، عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام قال: يبعث القائم وليس في عنقه بيعة لأحد.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Qāʾim will go forth without an allegiance to anyone (binding) on his neck.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from both Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd and al-Ḥasan b. Ẓarīf,[1] from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. Sālim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The Qāʾim (as) will rise up without an allegiance to anyone (binding) on his neck.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن يعقوب بن يزيد والحسن بن ظريف جميعاً، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن هشام بن سالم، عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام، قال: يقوم القائم عليه السلام وليس لأحد في عنقه بيعة.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from both Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd and al-Ḥasan b. Ẓarīf,[1] from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. Sālim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Qāʾim (as) will rise up without an allegiance to anyone (binding) on his neck.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Descriptions of the Mahdī (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Salama b. al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad, from Munayʿ b. al-Ḥajjāj al-Baṣrī, from Majāshiʿ, from Muʿallā from Muḥammad b. al-Fayḍ, from Abī Jaʿfar (saa), who said: “The staff of Mūsā was originally with Ādam (as-d), so it passed down to Shuʿayb and then it passed down to Mūsā b. Amran, and now it is in our possession. Indeed, I last saw it very recently. It is green, just as its appearance was when it was plucked from its tree, and it speaks when one bids it to do so. It has been prepared for our Qāʾim (as) so that he may do with it what Mūsā b. Amran (as) used to do with it. It does as it is ordered to, and wherever it is thrown, it swallows what they were faking [1] with its tongue.”
arabicText: محمد بن يحيى، عن سلمة بن الخطاب، عن عبداللّه بن محمد، عن منيع بن الحجّاج البصري، عن مجاشع، عن معلّى عن محمد بن الفيض، عن أبي جعفر، قال: كانت عصا موسى لآدم عليهما السلام، فصارت الى شعيب، ثمّ صارت الى موسى بن عمران، وانّها لعندنا، وانّ عهدي بها آنفاً، وهي خضراء كهيئتها حين انتُزعت من شجرتها وانّها لتنطق اذا استُنطقت اُعدّت لقائمنا عليه السلام يصنع بها ما كان يصنع بها موسى بن عمران عليه السلام، وانّها تصنع ما تؤمر، وأنّها حيث اُلقيت تلقف ما يأفكون بلسانها.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā, from Salama b. al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad, from Munayʿ b. al-Ḥajjāj al-Baṣrī, from Majāshiʿ, from Muʿallā from Muḥammad b. al-Fayḍ, from Abī Jaʿfar (saa), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The staff of Mūsā was originally with Ādam (as-d), so it passed down to Shuʿayb and then it passed down to Mūsā b. Amran, and now it is in our possession. Indeed, I last saw it very recently. It is green, just as its appearance was when it was plucked from its tree, and it speaks when one bids it to do so. It has been prepared for our Qāʾim (as) so that he may do with it what Mūsā b. Amran (as) used to do with it. It does as it is ordered to, and wherever it is thrown, it swallows what they were faking [1] with its tongue.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Prohibition on Uttering his Given Name (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “No-one mentions the Master of this Ordinance by his given name except a disbeliever.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه عن يعقوب بن يزيد، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن عليّ بن رئاب، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام قال: صاحب هذا الأمر رجل لا يسمّيه باسمه إلّا كافر.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “No-one mentions the Master of this Ordinance by his given name except a disbeliever.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Prohibition on Uttering his Given Name (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. Faḍḍāl from al-Rayyān b. al-Ṣalt, who narrated: “Al-Riḍā (as) was asked about the Qāʾim (as), so he said: “He is not (to be) physically seen, nor mentioned by his given name.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن جعفر بن محمد بن مالك، عن عليّ بن الحسن بن فضال عن الرّيان بن الصلت، قال: سُئِلَ الرضا عليه السلام عن القائم عليه السلام فقال: لا يرى جسمه ولا يسمّى باسمه.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. Faḍḍāl from al-Rayyān b. al-Ṣalt, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Al-Riḍā (as) was asked about the Qāʾim (as), so he said: “He is not (to be) physically seen, nor mentioned by his given name.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Prohibition on Uttering his Given Name (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Ismāʿīl b. Abān, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir b. Yazīd al-Juʿfī, who said: “I heard Abā Jaʿfar (as) saying: “ʿUmar asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) about the Mahdī, whereupon he (ʿUmar) said: “O’ son of Abī Ṭālib, inform me of the Mahdī. What is his name?” He replied: “As for his name, then no. My beloved and intimate friend has enjoined me to not narrate his name until Allāh (azwj) sends him forth, and it is part of what Allāh (azwj) has reserved in the knowledge of His Apostle.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن اسماعيل بن أبان، عن عمرو بن شمر، عن جابر بن يزيد الجعفي، قال: سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول: سأل عمر أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام عن المهدي، فقال: يا ابن أبي طالب أخبرني عن المهدي ما اسمه؟ قال: أمّا إسمه فلا، إنّ حبيبي وخليلي عهد إليّ أن لا أحدّث باسمه حتى يبعثه الله عزّ وجل وهو ممّا استودع الله عزّ وجل رسوله في علمه.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Ismāʿīl b. Abān, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir b. Yazīd al-Juʿfī, who said: “I heard Abā Jaʿfar (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “ʿUmar asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) about the Mahdī, whereupon he (ʿUmar) said: “O’ son of Abī Ṭālib, inform me of the Mahdī. What is his name?” He replied: “As for his name, then no. My beloved and intimate friend has enjoined me to not narrate his name until Allāh (azwj) sends him forth, and it is part of what Allāh (azwj) has reserved in the knowledge of His Apostle.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Prohibition on Uttering his Given Name (as)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from Abī Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who narrated: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (as) saying: “The successor (after me, is my son al-Ḥasan), but how will you deal with the successor after the successor?” I said: “Why? May Allāh make me your sacrifice.” He stated: “Because you will not see his person, nor will it be allowable for you to mention him by his given name.” I followed up: “So, how are we to mention him?,” whereupon he replied: “Say “the Divine authority from the House of Muḥammad,” may Allāh’s salutations be upon him, and His peace.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن أحمد العلوي، عن أبي هاشم الجعفري، قال: سمعت أبا الحسن العسكري عليه السلام، يقول: الخلف (من بعدي إبني الحسن) فكيف لكم بالخلف من بعد الخلف؟ قلت: ولِمَ؟ جعلني الله فداك. قال: لأنّكم لا ترون شخصه، ولا يحلّ لكم ذكره باسمه. قلت: فكيف نذكره؟ فقال: قولوا الحجّة من آل محمد صلوات الله عليه وسلامه.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from Abī Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who narrated: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “The successor (after me, is my son al-Ḥasan), but how will you deal with the successor after the successor?” I said: “Why? May Allāh make me your sacrifice.” He stated: “Because you will not see his person, nor will it be allowable for you to mention him by his given name.” I followed up: “So, how are we to mention him?,” whereupon he replied: “Say “the Divine authority from the House of Muḥammad,” may Allāh’s salutations be upon him, and His peace.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī both said: “Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿUmar b. Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-Rabīʿ al-Madāʾinī, saying: “Muḥammad b. Isḥāq narrated to us, from Usayd b. Thaʿlaba, from Umm Hāniʾ, who narrated: “I met Abā Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), whereupon I asked him about this verse: ﴾So I swear by the stars that return—the comets﴿ [81:15-16]. He said: “An Imam who will withdraw during his time, upon the conclusion of the year two hundred and sixty, according to his knowledge.[1] Then, he will appear like a blazing flame in the darkness of the night. If you live to see that, your eyes will be gladdened.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، قالا: حدّثنا أحمد بن الحسين بن عمر بن يزيد، عن الحسين بن الربيع المدائني قال: حدّثنا محمد بن اسحاق، عن أسيد بن ثعلبة، عن امّ هانىء، قالت: لقيت أبا جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب عليهم السلام، فسألته عن هذه الآية: ﴿فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلْخُنَّسِ ۝ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْكُنَّسِ﴾. فقال: إمام يخنس في زمانه، عند انقضاء من علمه سنة ستين ومائتين، ثمّ يبدو كالشهاب الوقّاد في ظلمة الليل، فان أدركت ذلك قرّت عيناك.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī both said: “Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿUmar b. Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-Rabīʿ al-Madāʾinī, saying: “Muḥammad b. Isḥāq narrated to us, from Usayd b. Thaʿlaba, from Umm Hāniʾ, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I met Abā Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), whereupon I asked him about this verse: ﴾So I swear by the stars that return—the comets﴿ [81:15-16]. He said: “An Imam who will withdraw during his time, upon the conclusion of the year two hundred and sixty, according to his knowledge.[1] Then, he will appear like a blazing flame in the darkness of the night. If you live to see that, your eyes will be gladdened.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī and Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār altogether said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, altogether saying: “Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb al-Sarrād narrated to us, from Dāwūd b. al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abī Baṣīr from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his forefathers (as-p), who said that the Apostle of Allāh (sws) stated: “The Mahdī is of my posterity. His name is my name, his teknonym is my teknonym, and he is the most resembling of people to me in constitution and character. There will be an occultation for him, and confusion until the creation are misguided away from their religious commitments. At that time, he will approach as like a piercing flame,[1] whereupon he will fill it (the Earth) with justice and equity just as it had once been filled with oppression and iniquity.”

thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī and Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār altogether said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, altogether saying: “Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb al-Sarrād narrated to us, from Dāwūd b. al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abī Baṣīr from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his forefathers (as-p), who said that the Apostle of Allāh (sws) stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Mahdī is of my posterity. His name is my name, his teknonym is my teknonym, and he is the most resembling of people to me in constitution and character. There will be an occultation for him, and confusion until the creation are misguided away from their religious commitments. At that time, he will approach as like a piercing flame,[1] whereupon he will fill it (the Earth) with justice and equity just as it had once been filled with oppression and iniquity.”

author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, from Hārūn b. Khārija, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (as), who said: “Dhū’l-Qarnayn was not a prophet, but he was a righteous servant who loved Allāh and whom Allāh loved, and he was sincere to Allāh, so Allāh dealt sincerely with him. He adjured his people to be conscious of Allāh, so they struck him on one of his horns,[1] whereupon he occulted from them for a time, and then returned to them, so they struck him on his other horn. And among you is one who follows his precedent.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن علي بن النعمان، عن هارون بن خارجة، عن أبي بصير، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال: إنّ ذا القرنين لم يكن نبيّاً، ولكنّه كان عبداً صالحاً أحبّ الله فأحبّه الله، وناصح لله فناصحه الله، أمر قومه بتقوى الله، فضربوه على قرنه، فغاب عنهم زماناً، ثمّ رجع اليهم، فضربوه على قرنه الآخر، وفيكم من هو على سنّته.

chapter: About the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from Faḍḍāla b. Ayyūb, from Sudayr, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “There is in the Qāʾim a precedent from Yūsuf (as).” I said: “It is as though you are mentioning his story, or his occultation?,” so he told me: “What of it does this community object to? They resemble swine! Verily, Yūsuf’s brothers were the grandsons and offspring of Prophets, and they traded with Yūsuf and had commercial dealings with him. They were his brothers, and he was theirs, yet they did not recognise him until he said to them: ﴾‘I am Yūsuf’﴿ [12:90]. So, what does this community object to that Allāh (azwj) would, at any time, seek to conceal His Divine authority?! Yūsuf (as) was the king of Egypt, and there was between him and his father a distance of eighteen days’ travel. Had Allāh (azwj) intended to render Jacob cognisant of Yūsuf’s whereabouts, He had all power to do that. By Allāh, when they received the glad tidings, Jacob and his sons travelled for nine days from their hinterland encampment towards Egypt. So, what does this community object to that Allāh (azwj) would do with His Divine authority as He did with Yūsuf, that he would be walking among their markets and treading on their carpets, yet they would not recognise him? Until Allāh (azwj) permits him to make himself known to them, just as He permitted in the case of Yūsuf, whereupon he said to them: ﴾He said, ‘Have you realized what you did to Yūsuf and his brother, when you were senseless?’ They said, ‘Are you really Yūsuf?!’ He said, ‘I am Yūsuf, and this is my brother.’﴿ [12:89-90]
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن أحمد بن هلال، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي نجران، عن فضالة بن أيوب، عن سدير قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام يقول: إنّ في القائم سنّة من يوسف عليه السلام. قلت: كأنّك تذكر خبره أو غيبته؟ فقال لي: وما تنكر من ذلك هذه الاُمّة، أشباه الخنازير، إنّ إخوة يوسف كانوا أسباطاً أولاد أنبياء، تاجروا يوسف وبايعوه، وهم إخوته وهو أخوهم فلم يعرفوه حتى قال لهم: ﴿أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ﴾. فما تنكر هذه الاُمّة أن يكون الله عزّ وجل—في وقت من الأوقات—يريد أن يستر حجّته؟! لقد كان يوسف عليه السلام اليه ملك مصر، وكان بينه وبين والده مسيرة ثمانية عشر يوماً، فلو أراد الله عزّ وجل أن يُعرّفه مكانه لقدر على ذلك، والله لقد سار يعقوب وولده عند البشارة مسيرة تسعة أيّام من بدوهم الى مصر. فما تنكر هذه الاُمّة أن يكون الله عزّ وجل يفعل بحجّته ما فعل بيوسف أن يكون يسير في أسواقهم، ويطأ بُسطهم، وهم لا يعرفونه؟ حتى يأذن الله عزّ وجل أن يُعرّفهم بنفسه كما أذن ليوسف حتى قال لهم: ﴿قَالَ هَلْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا فَعَلْتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنتُمْ جَـٰهِلُونَ ۝ قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُ ۖقَالَ أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ وَهَـٰذَآ أَخِى﴾و.

author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Ziyād al-Makfūf, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī ʿUqba the poet, who narrated: “I heard Amīr al-Muʾminīn, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as) saying: “It is as though I see you wandering as camels wander in search of pasture, but you will not find it, o’ assembly of the Shīʿa.” Something like this has also been transmitted from Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Abī’l-Jārūd Ziyād b. al-Mundhir, from the poet ʿAbd Allāh.
arabicText: علي بن ابراهيم، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن سنان، عن زياد المكفوف، عن عبداللّه بن أبي عقبة الشاعر، قال: سمعت أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام يقول: كأنّي بكم تجولون جولان الابل تبتغون المرعى، فلا تجدونه يا معشر الشيعة. ورواه عن سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن محمد بن سنان، عن أبي الجارود زياد بن المنذر، عن عبداللّه الشاعر مثله.

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: About the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Khālid, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Never are the servants closer to Allāh (azwj), nor is He more pleased by them, than when the Divine authority of Allāh (azwj) has become unaccounted for to them, so he does not appear to them and they do not know of his whereabouts, but they know that it does not refute Allāh’s proofs and clear signs to them.[1] So, on account of that, they continue to expect the Deliverance, be it morning or evening. And never is Allāh’s (taa) wrath upon His enemies severer than when the Divine authority of Allāh has become unaccounted for to them, whereupon he does not appear to them, while He knows that His allies would not fall prey to misgivings. For had He known that they would fall prey to misgivings, He would not have occulted His Divine authority for so much as the blink of an eye, and that is not to be except when the evilest of people are in charge (of worldly affairs).”[2]
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري جميعاً، عن ابراهيم بن هاشم، عن محمد بن خالد، عن محمد بن سنان، عن المفضّل بن عمر، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: أقرب ما يكون العباد من الله عزّ وجل وأرضى ما يكون عنهم اذا افتقدوا حجّة الله عزّ وجل، فلم يظهر لهم، ولم يعلموا بمكانه، وهم في ذلك يعلمون أنّه لم تبطل حجج الله عنهم وبيّناته، فعندها فتوقّعوا الفرج صباحاً ومساءاً، وانّ أشدّ ما يكون غضب الله تعالى على أعدائه اذا افتقدوا حجّة الله فلم يظهر لهم وقد علم أنّ أولياءه لايرتابون، ولو علم أنّهم يرتابون لما غيّب حجّته طرفة عين، ولا يكون ذلك إلّا على رأس شرار الناس.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Khālid, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Never are the servants closer to Allāh (azwj), nor is He more pleased by them, than when the Divine authority of Allāh (azwj) has become unaccounted for to them, so he does not appear to them and they do not know of his whereabouts, but they know that it does not refute Allāh’s proofs and clear signs to them.[1] So, on account of that, they continue to expect the Deliverance, be it morning or evening. And never is Allāh’s (taa) wrath upon His enemies severer than when the Divine authority of Allāh has become unaccounted for to them, whereupon he does not appear to them, while He knows that His allies would not fall prey to misgivings. For had He known that they would fall prey to misgivings, He would not have occulted His Divine authority for so much as the blink of an eye, and that is not to be except when the evilest of people are in charge (of worldly affairs).”[2]

chapter: About the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from Mūsā b. Saʿdān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Qāsim, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, who narrated: “I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) about the exegesis of Jābir, so he said: “Do not narrate it to ruffians, for they will disseminate it (if you do that). Have you not read, in the Book of Allāh (azwj): ﴾When the Trumpet will be sounded﴿? [74:8]—Indeed, one of us is an Imam concealed. When Allāh (azwj) intends to make his matter apparent, He will make a mark upon his heart. So, he will appear, and issue orders on the basis of Allāh’s (azwj) ordinance.”
