chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd al-Yaqṭīnī altogether narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from ʿĪsā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿUmar b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, from his maternal uncle al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d). ʿĪsā al-ʿAlawī narrated: “I said to him: “If something were to happen—may Allāh not let me see your day—who would I take as my Imam?” He nodded in the direction of Mūsā (as). I continued: “If Mūsā were to die, then to whom?” He said: “To his son.” I said: “If his son were to die, and leave behind a brother who is older and a son who is younger, who do I take as my Imam?” He said: “His son.” Then, he said: “It will always be as such.” I followed up with: “If I am not cognisant of him, nor do I recognise his whereabouts, what am I to do?” He responded: “You say: O’ Allāh, I seek to take as authority over me whoever remains of Your Divine authorities from among the posterity of the late Imam, for that will suffice you.” This has also been transmitted by way of Saʿd and al-Ḥimyarī, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn ʿUbayd.
arabicText: محمد بن الحسن الصفار، قال: حدّثنا محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، ومحمد بن عيسى بن عبيد اليقطيني، جميعاً، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي نجران، عن عيسى بن عبداللّه بن محمد بن عمر بن علي بن أبي طالب، عن خاله الصادق جعفر بن محمد عليهما السلام، قال: قلت له: إنْ كان كونٌ—لا أراني الله يومك—فبمن أئتمّ؟ فأومأ الى موسى عليه السلام، فقلت: فان مضى موسى فالى من؟ قال: الى ولده، قلت: فان مضى ولده، وترك أخاً كبيراً وابناً صغيراً، فبمن أئتمّ؟ قال: بولده، ثمّ قال: هكذا أبداً، قلت: فإنّ أنا لم أعرفه ولم أعرف موضعه، فما أصنع؟ قال: تقول: (اللّهمّ إني أتولّى من بقي من حججك من ولد الامام الماضي) فان ذلك يجزيك. ورواه عن سعد والحميري عن ابن أبي الخطاب وابن عبيد.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd al-Yaqṭīnī altogether narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from ʿĪsā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿUmar b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, from his maternal uncle al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d). ʿĪsā al-ʿAlawī narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to him: “If something were to happen—may Allāh not let me see your day—who would I take as my Imam?” He nodded in the direction of Mūsā (as). I continued: “If Mūsā were to die, then to whom?” He said: “To his son.” I said: “If his son were to die, and leave behind a brother who is older and a son who is younger, who do I take as my Imam?” He said: “His son.” Then, he said: “It will always be as such.” I followed up with: “If I am not cognisant of him, nor do I recognise his whereabouts, what am I to do?” He responded: “You say: O’ Allāh, I seek to take as authority over me whoever remains of Your Divine authorities from among the posterity of the late Imam, for that will suffice you.” This has also been transmitted by way of Saʿd and al-Ḥimyarī, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn ʿUbayd.

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Ayyūb b. Nūḥ, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Darrāj, from Zurāra, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said: “An era will come upon people in which their Imam is occulted from them.” I asked him: “What are people to do in that era?” He said: “They are to adhere to the Ordinance that they affirm, until it is clarified to them.”
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن أيوب بن نوح، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن جميل بن درّاج، عن زرارة قال: قال أبو عبداللّه علیه السلام: يأتي على الناس زمان يغيب عنهم إمامهم. فقلت له: ما يصنع الناس في ذلك الزمان؟ قال: يتمسّكون بالأمر الذي هم عليه حتى يتبيّن لهم.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Ayyūb b. Nūḥ, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Darrāj, from Zurāra, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “An era will come upon people in which their Imam is occulted from them.” I asked him: “What are people to do in that era?” He said: “They are to adhere to the Ordinance that they affirm, until it is clarified to them.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Mūsā b. al-Qāsim, from Muʿāwiya b. Wahab al-Bajalī and Abī Qutāda ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Ḥafṣ, from ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his brother, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar (as-d). ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar narrated: “I said: “What is the interpretation of Allāh’s (azwj) statement: ﴾Say, ‘Tell me, should your water sink down [into the ground], who will bring you running water?’﴿?” [67:30]—whereupon Imam al-Kāẓim (saa) replied: “If your Imam becomes unaccounted for and you cannot see him, what will you do?”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن موسى ابن القاسم، عن معاوية بن وهب البجلي، وأبي قتادة علي بن محمد بن حفص، عن علي بن جعفر، عن أخيه موسى بن جعفر عليهما السلام، قال: قلت: ما تأويل قول الله عزّ وجل: ﴿قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْرًۭا فَمَن يَأْتِيكُم بِمَآءٍۢ مَّعِينٍۭ﴾. فقال: اذا فقدتم إمامكم فلم تروه، فماذا تصنعون؟.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Mūsā b. al-Qāsim, from Muʿāwiya b. Wahab al-Bajalī and Abī Qutāda ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Ḥafṣ, from ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar, from his brother, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar (as-d). ʿAlī b. Jaʿfar narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said: “What is the interpretation of Allāh’s (azwj) statement: ﴾Say, ‘Tell me, should your water sink down [into the ground], who will bring you running water?’﴿?” [67:30]—whereupon Imam al-Kāẓim (saa) replied: “If your Imam becomes unaccounted for and you cannot see him, what will you do?”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, al-Ḥimyarī and Ibn Idrīs said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Jabbār and ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿĀmir b. Saʿd al-Ashʿarī narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from Muḥammad b. al-Musāwir, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Al-Mufaḍḍal narrated: “I heard him saying: “Beware of drawing attention,[1] for truly, by Allāh, your Imam will be occulted from you for years of your lives, and you will be sifted until it will be said: “He has died or perished, or which valley has he gone into?” The eyes of the believers will shed tears over him, and you will be thrown about as the ships are upon the waves of the sea. None will be saved but he from whom Allāh has taken His covenant, inscribed belief into his heart and supported him with a spirit from Him. Twelve banners will be raised, resembling each other, such that it will not be known which is which.” Al-Mufaḍḍal continued his narration: “I started crying,” so the Imam said to me: “What has made you cry, o’ Abā ʿAbd Allāh?”[2] I responded: “How can I not cry? You said: “Twelve banners resembling each other, such that it will not be known which is which,” so what are we to do?” Al-Mufaḍḍal continued to narrate: “He observed the Sun as its light shone into the portico, whereupon he said: “O’ Abā ʿAbd Allāh, do you see this Sun?” I said: “Yes.” He concluded: “By Allāh, our Ordinance is clearer than this Sun.”
arabicText: سعد والحميري وابن ادريس، قالوا: حدّثنا أحمد بن محمد بن عیسی ومحمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب ومحمد بن عبدالجبار، وعبداللّه بن عامر ابن سعد الأشعري، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي نجران، عن محمد بن المساور، عن المفضّل ابن عمر الجعفي، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: سمعته يقول: إيّاكم والتنويه، أما والله ليغيبنّ إمامكم سنيناً من دهركم، ولتمحّصنّ حتى يقال: « مات أو هلك، بأيّ وادٍ سلك »، ولتدمعنّ عليه عيون المؤمنين، ولتكفأُنّ كما تكفأ السفن في أمواج البحر، ولا ينجو الّا من أخذ الله ميثاقه، وكتب في قلبه الايمان وأيّده بروح منه. ولترفعنّ إثنتا عشرة راية مشتبهة لا يدرى أَيٌّ من أيٍّ. قال: فبكيت، فقال لي: ما يبكيك، يا أبا عبداللّه؟ فقلت: وكيف لا أبكي، وأنت تقول: إثنتا عشرة راية مشتبهة لا يدرى أيّ من أيّ، فكيف نصنع؟ قال: فنظر الى شمس داخلة في الصفّة، فقال: يا أبا عبداللّه ترى هذه الشمس؟ قلت: نعم. قال: والله لأمرنا أبين من هذه الشمس.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, al-Ḥimyarī and Ibn Idrīs said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Jabbār and ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿĀmir b. Saʿd al-Ashʿarī narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Najrān, from Muḥammad b. al-Musāwir, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Al-Mufaḍḍal narrated: “I heard him saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Beware of drawing attention,[1] for truly, by Allāh, your Imam will be occulted from you for years of your lives, and you will be sifted until it will be said: “He has died or perished, or which valley has he gone into?” The eyes of the believers will shed tears over him, and you will be thrown about as the ships are upon the waves of the sea. None will be saved but he from whom Allāh has taken His covenant, inscribed belief into his heart and supported him with a spirit from Him. Twelve banners will be raised, resembling each other, such that it will not be known which is which.” Al-Mufaḍḍal continued his narration: “I started crying,” so the Imam said to me: “What has made you cry, o’ Abā ʿAbd Allāh?”[2] I responded: “How can I not cry? You said: “Twelve banners resembling each other, such that it will not be known which is which,” so what are we to do?” Al-Mufaḍḍal continued to narrate: “He observed the Sun as its light shone into the portico, whereupon he said: “O’ Abā ʿAbd Allāh, do you see this Sun?” I said: “Yes.” He concluded: “By Allāh, our Ordinance is clearer than this Sun.”

chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār said: “Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik al-Fazārī al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Isḥāq b. Muḥammad al-Ṣayrafī, from Yaḥyā b. al-Muthannā al-ʿAṭṭār, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr, from ʿUbayd b. Zurāra, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “The people’s Imam will become unaccounted for, whereupon he will attend the pilgrimage season and he will see them, but they will not see him.”
arabicText: محمد بن يحيى العطار، قال: حدّثنا جعفر بن محمد بن مالك الفزاري الكوفي، عن إسحاق بن محمد الصيرفي، عن يحيى بن المثنّى العطار، عن عبداللّه بن بكير، عن عبيد بن زرارة، قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام يقول: يفقد الناس إمامهم فيشهد الموسم فيراهم ولا يرونه.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār said: “Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Mālik al-Fazārī al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Isḥāq b. Muḥammad al-Ṣayrafī, from Yaḥyā b. al-Muthannā al-ʿAṭṭār, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Bukayr, from ʿUbayd b. Zurāra, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “The people’s Imam will become unaccounted for, whereupon he will attend the pilgrimage season and he will see them, but they will not see him.”

chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Ṣāliḥ b. Muḥammad, from Hānīʾ al-Tammār, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said: “There is for the Master of this Ordinance an occultation. During it, the one who continues to adhere to his religion is like one who strips the desert thorn with his bare hands.”[1] Then, he said, while gesturing with his hand in this manner: “There is for the Master of this Ordinance an occultation, so let a servant be conscious of Allāh, and let him continue to adhere to his religion.”
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن محمد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن صالح بن محمد، عن هانيء التمّار، قال: قال أبو عبداللّه عليه السلام: إنّ لصاحب هذا الأمر غيبة، المتمسّك فيها بدينه كالخارط للقتاد، ثمّ قال—هكذا بيده—ثمّ قال: إنّ لصاحب هذا الأمر غيبة، فليتّق الله عبد، وليتمسّك بدينه.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Ṣāliḥ b. Muḥammad, from Hānīʾ al-Tammār, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “There is for the Master of this Ordinance an occultation. During it, the one who continues to adhere to his religion is like one who strips the desert thorn with his bare hands.”[1] Then, he said, while gesturing with his hand in this manner: “There is for the Master of this Ordinance an occultation, so let a servant be conscious of Allāh, and let him continue to adhere to his religion.”

chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from both Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā and Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Manṣūr, from a man—whose name was ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz [1]—from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated: “He said: “If you reach morning and evening without seeing an Imam whom you can follow, love whom you have loved, and hate whom you have hated, until Allāh (azwj) causes him to reappear.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ويعقوب بن يزيد جميعاً، عن الحسن بن علي بن فضال، عن جعفر بن محمد بن منصور، عن رجل—واسمه عمر بن عبدالعزيز—عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام، قال: قال: اذا أصبحت وأمسيت، لا ترى إماماً تأتمّ به، فأحبب من كنت تحبّ، وابغض من كنت تبغض حتى يظهره الله عزّ وجل.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from both Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā and Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Manṣūr, from a man—whose name was ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz [1]—from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated: “He said:
thaqalaynMatn: “If you reach morning and evening without seeing an Imam whom you can follow, love whom you have loved, and hate whom you have hated, until Allāh (azwj) causes him to reappear.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: What People will Have to Do about the Occultation
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-ʿAbbās b. Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Isḥāq b. Jarīr, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān, who narrated: “My father and I entered upon Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), whereupon he said: “How will you be when your condition becomes one in which you cannot see your Imam of guidance, nor a visible signpost (the like thereof), nor will anyone be saved from it except he who supplicates like the supplication of the drowning man?” So, my father said to him: “If this occurs by night, what are we to do?,” to which he replied: “As for you, you will not (live to) see it. But when that is the case, you (people) are to continue adhering to what is in your hands, until the matter is clarified to you.”
arabicText: محمد بن الحسن الصفّار، عن العباس بن معروف، عن علي بن مهزيار، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن حمّاد بن عيسى، عن إسحاق بن جرير، عن عبداللّه بن سنان، قال: دخلت أنا وأبي على أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، فقال: فكيف أنتم اذا صرتم في حال لا ترون فيها إمام هدى؟ ولا علماً يرى؟ ولا ينجو منها إلّا من دعا دعاء الغريق؟ فقال له أبي: اذا وقع هذا ليلاً فكيف نصنع؟ فقال: أمّا أنت فلا تدركه، فإذا كان ذلك، فتمسّكوا بما في أيديكم، حتى يتّضح لكم الأمر.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-ʿAbbās b. Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī b. Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Isḥāq b. Jarīr, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “My father and I entered upon Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), whereupon he said: “How will you be when your condition becomes one in which you cannot see your Imam of guidance, nor a visible signpost (the like thereof), nor will anyone be saved from it except he who supplicates like the supplication of the drowning man?” So, my father said to him: “If this occurs by night, what are we to do?,” to which he replied: “As for you, you will not (live to) see it. But when that is the case, you (people) are to continue adhering to what is in your hands, until the matter is clarified to you.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that he spoke about the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾The day when some of your Lord’s signs do come, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed beforehand﴿ [6:158]—so, he said: “The signs are the Imams, and the awaited sign [1] is the Qāʾim (as). So, on that day, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed before his rising with the sword, even if that soul had believed in his forefathers (as-p) who preceded him.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن عليّ بن رئاب، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، أنّه قال في قول الله عزّ وجل: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِى بَعْضُ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَـٰنُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ ءَامَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾. فقال عليه السلام: الآيات هم الأئمة، والآية المنتظرة هو القائم عليه السلام، فيومئذ لا ينفع نفساً إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل قيامه بالسيف، وان آمنت بمن تقدّم من آبائه عليهم السلام.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī b. Riʾāb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that
thaqalaynMatn: he spoke about the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾The day when some of your Lord’s signs do come, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed beforehand﴿ [6:158]—so, he said: “The signs are the Imams, and the awaited sign [1] is the Qāʾim (as). So, on that day, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed before his rising with the sword, even if that soul had believed in his forefathers (as-p) who preceded him.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Ibrāhīm b. Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. Ḥukaym, from Maymūn al-Bān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Five (events will occur) before the Qāʾim’s uprising: the emergence of the Yemeni and the Sufyānī, the caller calling from heaven, the swallowing (of an army) into the earth at Baydāʾ [1] and the murder of the Irreproachable Soul.”[2]
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن إبراهيم بن مهزيار عن أخيه علي عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن صفوان بن يحيى، عن محمد بن حكيم، عن ميمون البان، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: خمس قبل قيام القائم: (خروج) اليماني، والسفياني، والمنادي ينادي من السماء، وخسف بالبيداء، وقتل النفس الزكية.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Ibrāhīm b. Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad b. Ḥukaym, from Maymūn al-Bān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Five (events will occur) before the Qāʾim’s uprising: the emergence of the Yemeni and the Sufyānī, the caller calling from heaven, the swallowing (of an army) into the earth at Baydāʾ [1] and the murder of the Irreproachable Soul.”[2]

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz and al-ʿAlāʾ b. Razīn, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “There are signs from Allāh (azwj), for the believers, that precede (the emergence of) the Qāʾim.” I asked: “What are they? May Allāh make me your sacrifice.” He responded: “That is (just as it is mentioned in) the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾We will surely test you﴿ [2:155]—as in, the believers before the Qāʾim’s (as) emergence, ﴾with a measure of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth, lives, and fruits; and give good news to the patient﴿.” He continued: “He will surely test them with something of fear, of the kings of such-and-such a dynasty in the twilight years of their sultanate, and of hunger, because of the steep prices of their goods.” ﴾And a loss of wealth﴿—he continued: “Stagnation in commerce and the scarcity of profits.” And a loss of lives—he said: “Widespread death.” And a loss of fruits—he commented: “Scarcity in yield from whatever was cultivated. ﴾And give good news to the patient﴿, at that time, of the hastening of the Qāʾim’s (as) emergence.” Then, he said to me: “O’ Muḥammad, this is its true interpretation. Allāh (taa) says: ﴾No one knows its interpretation except Allāh and those firmly grounded in knowledge.﴿” [3:7]
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، عن أحمد بن هلال، عن ابن محبوب، عن أبي أيوب الخزّاز، والعلاء بن رزين، عن محمد بن مسلم قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام: يقول: إنّ قدّام القائم علامات تكون من الله عزّ وجل للمؤمنين. قلت: وما هي؟ جعلني الله فداك. قال: ذلك قول الله عز وجل: ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم﴾ يعني المؤمنين قبل خروج القائم عليه السلام ﴿بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَٱلْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ ۗوَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ﴾. قال: يبلوهم بشيءٍ من الخوف، من ملوك بني فلان في آخر سلطانهم والجوع بغلاء أسعارهم. ﴿وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ﴾ قال: كساد التجارات وقلّة الفضل. ونقص من الأنفس، قال: موت ذريع. ونقص من الثمرات، قال: قلّة ريع ما يزرع. ﴿وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ﴾ عند ذلك بتعجيل خروج القائم عليه السلام. ثمّ قال لي: يا محمد، هذا تأويله، إنّ الله تعالى يقول: ﴿وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۗوَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِى ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz and al-ʿAlāʾ b. Razīn, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “There are signs from Allāh (azwj), for the believers, that precede (the emergence of) the Qāʾim.” I asked: “What are they? May Allāh make me your sacrifice.” He responded: “That is (just as it is mentioned in) the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾We will surely test you﴿ [2:155]—as in, the believers before the Qāʾim’s (as) emergence, ﴾with a measure of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth, lives, and fruits; and give good news to the patient﴿.” He continued: “He will surely test them with something of fear, of the kings of such-and-such a dynasty in the twilight years of their sultanate, and of hunger, because of the steep prices of their goods.” ﴾And a loss of wealth﴿—he continued: “Stagnation in commerce and the scarcity of profits.” And a loss of lives—he said: “Widespread death.” And a loss of fruits—he commented: “Scarcity in yield from whatever was cultivated. ﴾And give good news to the patient﴿, at that time, of the hastening of the Qāʾim’s (as) emergence.” Then, he said to me: “O’ Muḥammad, this is its true interpretation. Allāh (taa) says: ﴾No one knows its interpretation except Allāh and those firmly grounded in knowledge.﴿” [3:7]

chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar b. Bashīr from Hishām b. Sālim, from Zurāra, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The caller will issue a call with the Qāʾim’s (as) name.” I (Zurāra) said: “Will it be specific or general?,” to which he replied: “General. Every people (will hear it) in their own language.” I followed up: “Who would oppose the Qāʾim (as) after his name has been called out?” He said: “Iblīs will not leave them be until he calls out at the end of the night and causes people to doubt.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن جعفر ابن بشير، عن هشام بن سالم، عن زرارة: عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: ينادي مناد باسم القائم عليه السلام، قلت: خاصّ أو عامّ؟ قال: عامّ، كلّ قوم بلسانهم. قلت: من يخالف القائم عليه السلام وقد نودي باسمه؟ قال: لا يدعهم إبليس حتى ينادي في آخر الليل ويشكّك الناس.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar b. Bashīr from Hishām b. Sālim, from Zurāra, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The caller will issue a call with the Qāʾim’s (as) name.” I (Zurāra) said: “Will it be specific or general?,” to which he replied: “General. Every people (will hear it) in their own language.” I followed up: “Who would oppose the Qāʾim (as) after his name has been called out?” He said: “Iblīs will not leave them be until he calls out at the end of the night and causes people to doubt.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim Majīlawayh narrated to us, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Kūfī, who said: “Al-Ḥusayn b. Sufyān narrated to us, from Qutayba b. Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Manṣūr al-Bajalī, who narrated: “I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) about the Sufyānī’s name, whereupon he said: “What would you do with his name? When he gains dominion over the five districts of Greater Syria: Damascus, Homs, Palestine, Jordan and Chalcis-on-Belus,[1] then expect the Deliverance.” I said: “Will he rule for nine months?” He responded: “No, but he will rule for eight months, and not a day longer.”
arabicText: حدّثنا محمد بن أبي القاسم ماجيلويه، عن محمد بن علي الكوفي، قال: حدّثنا الحسين بن سفيان، عن قتيبة بن محمد، عن عبداللّه بن أبي منصور البجليّ قال: سألت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام عن اسم السفياني؟ فقال: وما تصنع باسمه؟ اذا ملك كور الشام الخمس؛ دمشق، وحمص، وفلسطين، والاردن، وقنسرين فتوقّعوا عند ذلك الفرج. قلت: يملك تسعة أشهر؟ قال: لا، ولكن يملك ثمانية أشهر لا يزيد يوماً.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim Majīlawayh narrated to us, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Kūfī, who said: “Al-Ḥusayn b. Sufyān narrated to us, from Qutayba b. Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Manṣūr al-Bajalī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) about the Sufyānī’s name, whereupon he said: “What would you do with his name? When he gains dominion over the five districts of Greater Syria: Damascus, Homs, Palestine, Jordan and Chalcis-on-Belus,[1] then expect the Deliverance.” I said: “Will he rule for nine months?” He responded: “No, but he will rule for eight months, and not a day longer.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl, from his father, from Manṣūr, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said: “O’ Manṣūr! This matter will not come to you except after despair. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until you have been winnowed. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until you have been sifted. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until the wretched are brought to wretchedness and the felicitous to felicity.”
arabicText: علي بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن الفضيل، عن أبيه، عن منصور، قال: قال أبو عبداللّه عليه السلام: يا منصور، إنّ هذا الأمر لا يأتيكم إلّا بعد يأس، لا والله، لا يأتيكم حتى تميّزوا، لا والله لا يأتيكم حتى تمحّصوا، ولا والله لا يأتيكم حتى يشقى من شقى، ويسعد من سعد.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl, from his father, from Manṣūr, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “O’ Manṣūr! This matter will not come to you except after despair. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until you have been winnowed. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until you have been sifted. No, by Allāh, it will not come to you until the wretched are brought to wretchedness and the felicitous to felicity.”

chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Bazīʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-Mukhtār al-Qalānisī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Siyāba, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that he said: “How will you people be when you remain (apparently) without an Imam of guidance, or a standard (to rally around)? Will some of you disavow others? For at that time, you will be sieved, sifted and separated from the chaff, and at that time the two swords will clash, and dominion will be had at the beginning of the day, and killing and overthrow at its end.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن محمد ابن اسماعيل بن بزيع، عن عبداللّه بن عبدالرحمن الأصمّ، عن الحسين بن المختار القلانسيّ، عن عبدالرحمن بن سيابة، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام أنّه قال: كيف أنتم اذا بقيتم بلا إمام هدى ولا علم؟ يتبرّأ بعضكم من بعض؟ فعند ذلك تميّزون وتمحّصىن وتغربلون، وعند ذلك اختلاف السيفين، وإمارة أوّل من النهار، وقتل وخلع من آخر النهار.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Bazīʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from al-Ḥusayn b. al-Mukhtār al-Qalānisī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Siyāba, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “How will you people be when you remain (apparently) without an Imam of guidance, or a standard (to rally around)? Will some of you disavow others? For at that time, you will be sieved, sifted and separated from the chaff, and at that time the two swords will clash, and dominion will be had at the beginning of the day, and killing and overthrow at its end.”

chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Ghānim al-Qazwīnī narrated to us, saying that Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. Fāris narrated to him, narrating: “I was with Nūḥ and Ayyūb b. Nūḥ on the road to Mecca, whereupon we descended upon the valley of Zabāla and sat down to talk. The subject of the situation we were in came up, and how difficult the matter had become for us, so Ayyūb b. Nūḥ said: “This year I wrote (to him), mentioning some of this”—so he replied to me: “When your standard is removed from your midst, then expect the Deliverance from under your feet.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا محمد بن عبداللّه بن أبي غانم القزويني، قال: حدّثني ابراهيم بن محمد بن فارس، قال: كنت أنا [ونوح] وأيوب ابن نوح في طريق مكّة فنزلنا على وادي زبالة، فجلسنا تحدّث فجرى ذكر ما نحن فيه، وبعد الأمر علينا، فقال أيوب بن نوح: كتبت في هذه السنة أذكر شيئاً من هذا، فكتب اليّ: اذا رفع علمكم من بين أظهركم، فتوقّعوا الفرج من تحت أقدامكم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Ghānim al-Qazwīnī narrated to us, saying that Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad b. Fāris narrated to him, narrating:
thaqalaynMatn: “I was with Nūḥ and Ayyūb b. Nūḥ on the road to Mecca, whereupon we descended upon the valley of Zabāla and sat down to talk. The subject of the situation we were in came up, and how difficult the matter had become for us, so Ayyūb b. Nūḥ said: “This year I wrote (to him), mentioning some of this”—so he replied to me: “When your standard is removed from your midst, then expect the Deliverance from under your feet.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Muḥammad b. Jumhūr, from Aḥmad b. Abī Harāsa, from Abī Isḥāq Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥammād al-Anṣārī, who said: “ʿAmrū b. Shimr narrated to us, from Jābir b. Yazīd, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said: “It is as though I see the companions of the Qāʾim (as), and they have encompassed whatever is between the two horizons. There is no thing that does not obey them, even the wild beasts of the earth and the birds of prey, seeking their satisfaction in everything, to the point that one part of the earth will exult over another, saying: “A man among the Qāʾim’s (as) companions passed over me today.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أحمد بن الحسين بن سعيد، عن محمد بن جمهور، عن أحمد بن أبي هراسة، عن أبي اسحاق ابراهيم بن اسحاق، عن عبداللّه بن حمّاد الأنصاري، قال: حدّثنا عمرو بن شمر، عن جابر بن يزيد: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال: كأنّي بأصحاب القائم عليه السلام وقد أحاطوا بما بين الخافقين، فليس من شيء إلّا وهو مطيع لهم حتى سباع الأرض وسباع الطير، يطلب رضاهم في كلّ شيء، حتى تفخر الأرض على الأرض وتقول: مرّ بي اليوم رجل من أصحاب القائم عليه السلام.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Muḥammad b. Jumhūr, from Aḥmad b. Abī Harāsa, from Abī Isḥāq Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥammād al-Anṣārī, who said: “ʿAmrū b. Shimr narrated to us, from Jābir b. Yazīd, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “It is as though I see the companions of the Qāʾim (as), and they have encompassed whatever is between the two horizons. There is no thing that does not obey them, even the wild beasts of the earth and the birds of prey, seeking their satisfaction in everything, to the point that one part of the earth will exult over another, saying: “A man among the Qāʾim’s (as) companions passed over me today.”

chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated: “I spoke to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as) in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾You are only a warner, and there is a guide for every people﴿ [13:7], whereupon he said: “Every Imam is a guide for every people during their era.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب ويعقوب بن يزيد جميعاً، عن حمّاد بن عيسى، عن حريز بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن مسلم قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه علیه السلام: في قول الله عزّ وجل: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌۭ ۖوَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ فقال: كلّ إمام هاد لكلّ قوم في زمانهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb and Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I spoke to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as) in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾You are only a warner, and there is a guide for every people﴿ [13:7], whereupon he said: “Every Imam is a guide for every people during their era.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar b. Udhayna, from Burayd b. Muʿāwiya al-ʿIjlī, who narrated: “I said to Abī Jaʿfar (as): “What is the meaning of ﴾You are only a warner, and there is a guide for every people﴿?” [13:7]—so, he said: “The warner is the Apostle of Allāh (sawa), and ʿAlī is the guide. And in every time and age there is an Imam from among us, who guides them (his people) to what the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) came with.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، قال: حدّثنا أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن أبيه، عن ابن أبي عمير، عن عمر بن اُذينة، عن بريد بن معاوية العجلي قال: قلت لأبي جعفر عليه السلام: ما معنى ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌۭ ۖوَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ فقال: المنذر رسول الله صلّى الله عليه واله، وعليّ الهادي، وفي كل وقت وزمان امام منّا يهديهم الى ما جاء به رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh said: “Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar b. Udhayna, from Burayd b. Muʿāwiya al-ʿIjlī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī Jaʿfar (as): “What is the meaning of ﴾You are only a warner, and there is a guide for every people﴿?” [13:7]—so, he said: “The warner is the Apostle of Allāh (sawa), and ʿAlī is the guide. And in every time and age there is an Imam from among us, who guides them (his people) to what the Apostle of Allāh (sawa) came with.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAmrū b. Abī’l-Miqdām, from his father, from ʿUbayd b. Karb, who narrated: “I heard ʿAlī saying: “We, the People of the House, have a banner. Whoever precedes it breaks away, whoever falls behind it is destroyed, and whoever follows it catches up.”
arabicText: علي بن ابراهيم، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن عمرو بن أبي المقدام، عن أبيه، عن عبيد بن كرب، قال: سمعت عليّاً يقول: إنّ لنا أهل البيت راية، من تقدّمها مرق، ومن تأخّر عنها محق، ومن تبعها لحق.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAmrū b. Abī’l-Miqdām, from his father, from ʿUbayd b. Karb, who narrated: “I heard ʿAlī saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “We, the People of the House, have a banner. Whoever precedes it breaks away, whoever falls behind it is destroyed, and whoever follows it catches up.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Faḍḍāla, from Abān from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “There are for Allāh (azwj) creatures whom He created from His light and His mercy, for they are the observing eye of Allāh and His listening ear, His speaking tongue among His creations, by His permission, and His trustees over whatever He has revealed of an excuse, a warning or an authoritative argument. So, through them Allāh erases misdeeds, and through them He overturns subjugation, through them He causes mercy to descend and through them He brings the living to death and the dead back to life. Through them He tests His creations, and through them He issues a decree among His creation.” I said: “May I be made your sacrifice, who are these?” He replied: “The Legatees.”
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن عيسى، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن فضالة، عن أبان عن محمد بن مسلم، قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام، يقول: إنّ لله عزّ وجل خلقاً خلقهم من نوره ورحمته، فَهُمْ عين الله الناظرة، واُذنه السامعة، ولسانه الناطق في خلقه باذنه واُمناؤه على ما أنزل من عذر أو نذر أو حجّة. فَبِهِمْ يمحو الله السيئات، وبهم يدفع الضيم، وبهم ينزل الرحمة، وبهم يحيي ميتاً، ويميت حيّاً، وبهم يبتلي خلقه، وبهم يقضي في خلقه قضيّة. قلت: جعلت فداك، من هؤلاء؟ قال: الأوصياء.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Faḍḍāla, from Abān from Muḥammad b. Muslim, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “There are for Allāh (azwj) creatures whom He created from His light and His mercy, for they are the observing eye of Allāh and His listening ear, His speaking tongue among His creations, by His permission, and His trustees over whatever He has revealed of an excuse, a warning or an authoritative argument. So, through them Allāh erases misdeeds, and through them He overturns subjugation, through them He causes mercy to descend and through them He brings the living to death and the dead back to life. Through them He tests His creations, and through them He issues a decree among His creation.” I said: “May I be made your sacrifice, who are these?” He replied: “The Legatees.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn Asbāṭ, from al-Baṭāʾinī, from Abī Baṣīr, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), that he said: “O’ Abā Baṣīr, we are the tree of knowledge and the people of the Prophet’s (sawa) house, and Jibraʾīl descends in our abode. We are the custodians of Allāh’s knowledge, and the repositories of Allāh’s revelations. Whoever follows us is saved, and whoever holds back from us perishes—it is a right upon Allāh (azwj).”[1]
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن أبي الخطاب، عن ابن أسباط، عن البطائني، عن أبي بصير، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام، أنّه قال: يا أبا بصير، نحن شجرة العلم، ونحن أهل بيت النبيّ صلّى الله عليه وآله، وفي دارنا مهبط جبرئيل، ونحن خزّان علم الله، ونحن معادن وحي الله، من تبعنا نجا، ومن تخلّف عنّا هلك، حقاً على الله عزّ وجل.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn Asbāṭ, from al-Baṭāʾinī, from Abī Baṣīr, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “O’ Abā Baṣīr, we are the tree of knowledge and the people of the Prophet’s (sawa) house, and Jibraʾīl descends in our abode. We are the custodians of Allāh’s knowledge, and the repositories of Allāh’s revelations. Whoever follows us is saved, and whoever holds back from us perishes—it is a right upon Allāh (azwj).”[1]

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad b. Muʿqal al-Qarmīsīnī, from Muḥammad b. Zayd al-Jazarī, from Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥammād, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Jābir narrated: “I said: “Why was Fāṭima al-Zahrāʾ named Zahrāʾ (the Resplendent)?,” so he replied: “Because Allāh (azwj) created her from the light of His exaltedness. So, when she radiated and thereby lit up the heavens and the earth with her light, overwhelming the angels’ eyes and prompting them to fall down into prostration to Allāh, they said: “O’ Deity of ours and our Master, what is this light?,” whereupon Allāh revealed to them: “This is a light from My light, which I have caused to reside tranquilly in My heaven, and I created it from My exaltedness. I will bring it out from the loins of one of My Prophets, having favoured him over the totality of the Prophets, and bring forth from that light Imams who uphold My ordinance, and guide to My truth. I have appointed them as My caliphs upon My earth, after the cessation of My revelations.”
arabicText: محمد بن معقل القرميسيني، عن محمد بن زيد الجزري، عن ابراهيم ابن اسحاق النهاوندي، عن عبداللّه بن حماد، عن عمرو بن شمر، عن جابر، عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام: قال: قلت: لِمَ سمّيت فاطمة الزهراء، زهراء؟ فقال: لأن الله عزّ وجل خلقها من نور عظمته، فلمّا أشرقت أضاءت السموات والأرض بنورها، وغشّيت أبصار الملائكة، وخرّت الملائكة لله ساجدين، وقالوا: إلٰهنا وسيّدنا ما هذا النور؟ فأوحى الله اليهم: هذا نور من نوري، وأسكنته في سمائي، خلقته من عظمتي أُخرجه من صلب نبيّ من أنبيائي، اُفضّله على جميع الأنبياء واُخرج من ذلك النور أئمة يقومون بأمري، يهدون الى حقّي، وأجعلهم خلفائي في أرضي بعد انقضاء وحيي.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Muʿqal al-Qarmīsīnī, from Muḥammad b. Zayd al-Jazarī, from Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥammād, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as). Jābir narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said: “Why was Fāṭima al-Zahrāʾ named Zahrāʾ (the Resplendent)?,” so he replied: “Because Allāh (azwj) created her from the light of His exaltedness. So, when she radiated and thereby lit up the heavens and the earth with her light, overwhelming the angels’ eyes and prompting them to fall down into prostration to Allāh, they said: “O’ Deity of ours and our Master, what is this light?,” whereupon Allāh revealed to them: “This is a light from My light, which I have caused to reside tranquilly in My heaven, and I created it from My exaltedness. I will bring it out from the loins of one of My Prophets, having favoured him over the totality of the Prophets, and bring forth from that light Imams who uphold My ordinance, and guide to My truth. I have appointed them as My caliphs upon My earth, after the cessation of My revelations.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāl, from Ḥammād b. ʿUthmān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (as) in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾O’ you who have faith! Obey Allāh and obey the Apostle and those vested with authority among you﴿ [4:59]—he said: “(They are) the Imams from the progeny of ʿAlī and Fāṭima (as-d), until the occurrence of the Hour.”
arabicText: الحميري، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطاب، عن عبداللّه بن محمد الحجّال، عن حمّاد بن عثمان، عن أبي بصير، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، في قول الله عزّ وجل: ﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَمْرِ مِنكُمْ﴾. قال: الأئمة من ولد عليّ وفاطمة عليهما السلام، الى أنْ تقوم الساعة.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāl, from Ḥammād b. ʿUthmān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (as)
thaqalaynMatn: in regards to the statement of Allāh (azwj): ﴾O’ you who have faith! Obey Allāh and obey the Apostle and those vested with authority among you﴿ [4:59]—he said: “(They are) the Imams from the progeny of ʿAlī and Fāṭima (as-d), until the occurrence of the Hour.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl from Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said: “Allāh (twt) sent Muḥammad (sws) as an Apostle to mankind and the jinn, and appointed after him twelve Legatees. Among them are those who have passed on and those who remain, and upon every Legatee from among the Legatees who are after Muḥammad (sawa) applies a precedent of the Legatees of ʿĪsā (as), who were also twelve in number. Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) was upon the precedent of the Messiah.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن محمد بن الفضيل عن أبي حمزة، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال: إنّ الله تبارك وتعالى أرسل محمداً صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلّم الى الجن والانس وجعل من بعده الاثني عشر وصيّاً منهم من مضى ومنهم من بقى، وكلّ وصيّ جرت فيه سنّة من الأوصياء الذين بعد محمد صلّى الله عليه وآله على سنّة أوصياء عیسی علیه السلام، وكانوا إثني عشر. وكان أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام على سنّة المسيح.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl from Abī Ḥamza, from Abī Jaʿfar (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Allāh (twt) sent Muḥammad (sws) as an Apostle to mankind and the jinn, and appointed after him twelve Legatees. Among them are those who have passed on and those who remain, and upon every Legatee from among the Legatees who are after Muḥammad (sawa) applies a precedent of the Legatees of ʿĪsā (as), who were also twelve in number. Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) was upon the precedent of the Messiah.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together said: “Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl—during the period of his uprightness—from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurāra, who narrated: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Does the Imam die without leaving behind offspring of his?” He replied: “That would not be.” I followed up: “What, then, would it be?” He concluded: “That would not be except that Allāh (azwj) therefore expresses His wrath upon His creation, hastening them (towards destruction).”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه وعبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، قالا: حدّثنا يعقوب ابن يزيد عن أحمد بن هلال—في حال استقامته—عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن ابن اُذينة، عن زرارة، قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: يمضي الامام وليس له عقب؟ قال: لا يكون ذلك، قلت: فيكون ماذا؟ قال: لا يكون ذلك إلّا أن يغضب الله عزّ وجل على خلقه، فيعاجلهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī together said: “Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to us, from Aḥmad b. Hilāl—during the period of his uprightness—from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurāra, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “Does the Imam die without leaving behind offspring of his?” He replied: “That would not be.” I followed up: “What, then, would it be?” He concluded: “That would not be except that Allāh (azwj) therefore expresses His wrath upon His creation, hastening them (towards destruction).”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Hāshim, from Abī Yaḥyā al-Madīnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “A Jew came to ʿUmar, asking him about some issues, whereupon he directed him to ʿAlī (as) so that he may ask him instead. So, ʿAlī (as) said to him: “Ask.” The Jew said: “Inform me. How many just Imams are there, after your Prophet? In which Garden is he, and who will dwell with him in his Garden?” So, ʿAlī (as) responded to him: “O’ Aaronite! [1] For Muḥammad (sawa) there are twelve just Imams after him. The abandonment of whoever abandons them does not harm them, nor do they become lonely on account of the opposition of those who oppose them. They are more grounded in Allāh’s religion than the firmly moored mountains. And the dwelling of Muḥammad (sawa) is the Garden of Eden, and those who reside with him therein, in tranquility, are these twelve.” So, the man accepted Islam, and said (to ʿAlī (saa)): “You are more worthy of this assembly than this one.[2] You are the one who surpasses without being surpassed, and the one who excels without anyone transcending your excellence.”
arabicText: الحميري، عن محمد بن عيسى، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي هاشم، عن أبي يحيى المديني، عن أبي عبداللّه علیه السلام، قال: جاء يهوديّ الى عمر، يسأله عن مسائل فأرشده الى عليّ عليه السلام ليسأله، فقال له عليّ عليه السلام: سل. قال: أخبرني، كم بعد نبيّكم من إمام عادل؟ وفي أيّ جنّة هو؟ ومن يسكن معه في جنّته؟ فقال له عليّ عليه السلام: يا هاروني! لمحمد صلّى الله عليه وآله بعده إثنا عشر إماماً عدلاً، لا يضرّهم خذلان من خذلهم، ولا يستوحشون بخلاف من خالفهم، أثبت في دين الله من الجبال الرواسي. ومنزل محمد صلّى الله عليه وآله جنّة عدن، والذين يسكنون معه هؤلاء الاثنا عشر. فأسلم الرجل وقال: أنت أولى بهذا المجلس من هذا، أنت الذي تفوق ولا تفاق، وتعلو ولا تعلى.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥimyarī, from Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Hāshim, from Abī Yaḥyā al-Madīnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “A Jew came to ʿUmar, asking him about some issues, whereupon he directed him to ʿAlī (as) so that he may ask him instead. So, ʿAlī (as) said to him: “Ask.” The Jew said: “Inform me. How many just Imams are there, after your Prophet? In which Garden is he, and who will dwell with him in his Garden?” So, ʿAlī (as) responded to him: “O’ Aaronite! [1] For Muḥammad (sawa) there are twelve just Imams after him. The abandonment of whoever abandons them does not harm them, nor do they become lonely on account of the opposition of those who oppose them. They are more grounded in Allāh’s religion than the firmly moored mountains. And the dwelling of Muḥammad (sawa) is the Garden of Eden, and those who reside with him therein, in tranquility, are these twelve.” So, the man accepted Islam, and said (to ʿAlī (saa)): “You are more worthy of this assembly than this one.[2] You are the one who surpasses without being surpassed, and the one who excels without anyone transcending your excellence.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad b. Khālid al-Barqī, from Khalaf b. Ḥammād from Abān b. Taghlib, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said: “The Divine authority is before the creation, with the creation and after the creation.”[1]
arabicText: سعد، عن النهدي، عن محمد بن خالد البرقي، عن خلف بن حماد عن أبان بن تغلب قال: قال أبو عبداللّه عليه السلام: الحجّة قبل الخلق ومع الخلق وبعد الخلق.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad b. Khālid al-Barqī, from Khalaf b. Ḥammād from Abān b. Taghlib, who narrated: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Divine authority is before the creation, with the creation and after the creation.”[1]

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Qutayba said: “Al-Faḍl b. Shādhān narrated to us, saying: “Isḥāq b. Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Jarīr, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abī’l-Ḍuḥā, from Zayd b. Arqam, from the Prophet (sawa), that he said: “Verily, I am leaving to you the Book of Allāh, and the people of my house, for they will not separate from one another until they both return to me at the Basin.”
arabicText: علي بن محمد بن قتيبة، قال: حدّثنا الفضل بن شاذان، قال: حدّثنا إسحاق بن ابراهيم، عن جرير، عن الحسن بن عبيداللّه، عن أبي الضحى، عن زيد بن أرقم، عن النبيّ صلّى الله عليه وآله، قال: إنّي تارك فيكم كتاب الله، وأهل بيتي، فانّهما لن يفترقا حتى يردا عليّ الحوض.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Qutayba said: “Al-Faḍl b. Shādhān narrated to us, saying: “Isḥāq b. Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Jarīr, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿUbayd Allāh, from Abī’l-Ḍuḥā, from Zayd b. Arqam, from the Prophet (sawa), that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily, I am leaving to you the Book of Allāh, and the people of my house, for they will not separate from one another until they both return to me at the Basin.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Hāshim from Dāwud b. Farqad, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Whoever claims the Imamate without being an Imam has fabricated a lie against Allāh, His Apostle and us.”
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن أبي الخطاب، عن عبدالرحمن بن أبي هاشم عن داود بن فرقد، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام قال: من ادّعى الإمامة وليس بامام فقد افترى على الله وعلى رسوله وعلينا.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Hāshim from Dāwud b. Farqad, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever claims the Imamate without being an Imam has fabricated a lie against Allāh, His Apostle and us.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: The Signs of the Mahdī’s Reappearance
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn Sinān, from Yaḥyā, the brother of Udaym, from al-Walīd b. Ṣubayḥ, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “Verily, no-one makes a claim on this Ordinance other than its rightful Master, except that Allāh sunders his lifespan.”
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن أبي الخطاب، عن ابن سنان، عن يحيى أخي أديم عن الوليد بن صبيح قال: سمعت أبا عبداللّه عليه السلام يقول: إنّ هذا الأمر لا يدّعيه غير صاحبه، إلّا بتر الله عمره.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn Sinān, from Yaḥyā, the brother of Udaym, from al-Walīd b. Ṣubayḥ, who narrated: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily, no-one makes a claim on this Ordinance other than its rightful Master, except that Allāh sunders his lifespan.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Bizanṭī, who narrated: “Abū’l-Ḥasan (as) was asked: “By what signs is the Imam who succeeds an Imam recognised?” He said: “There are indications of the Imam; that he is the eldest of his father’s sons after him, that he possesses virtue, that when a traveller arrives in Medina and asks: “To whom did he bequeath?,” its people say: “To so-and-so,” and the Weapon is among us,[1] holding the same position as the Ark of the Covenant did among the Children of Israel. The Imamate goes with the Weapon, wherever it may be.”
arabicText: محمد العطار، عن ابن أبي الخطاب، عن البزنطي قال: سُئِلَ أبو الحسن عليه السلام: الامام بأيّ شيء يعرف بعد الامام؟ قال: إنّ للامام علامات؛ أن يكون أكبر ولد أبيه بعده، ويكون فيه الفضل، واذا قدم الراكب المدينة، قال: الى من أوصى؟ قالوا: الى فلان، والسلاح فينا بمنزلة التابوت في بني إسرائيل، يدور مع السلاح حيث كان.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from Ibn Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Bizanṭī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Abū’l-Ḥasan (as) was asked: “By what signs is the Imam who succeeds an Imam recognised?” He said: “There are indications of the Imam; that he is the eldest of his father’s sons after him, that he possesses virtue, that when a traveller arrives in Medina and asks: “To whom did he bequeath?,” its people say: “To so-and-so,” and the Weapon is among us,[1] holding the same position as the Ark of the Covenant did among the Children of Israel. The Imamate goes with the Weapon, wherever it may be.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Aḥmad b. Idrīs, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Abī’l-Jārūd, from Abī Jaʿfar (as). Abū’l-Jārūd narrated: “I said to him: “May I be made your sacrifice. When your Scholar from among the People of the House dies, what thing is it by which you recognise he who comes after him?” He replied: “By guidance, a grave and lowered demeanour, the affirmation of his excellence by the House of Muḥammad, and that he is not asked about anything between its two sides but that he gives the answer for it.”
arabicText: أحمد بن إدريس، عن ابن عيسى، عن محمد بن سنان، عن أبي الجارود، عن ابي جعفر عليه السلام، قال: قلت له: جعلت فداك، اذا مضى عالمكم أهل البيت، فبأيّ شيء يعرّفون من يجيء بعده؟ قال: بالهدى، والاطراق، وإقرار آل محمد له بالفضل، ولا يسأل عن شيء ممّا بين صدفيها، إلّا أجاب فيه.
thaqalaynSanad: Aḥmad b. Idrīs, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from Abī’l-Jārūd, from Abī Jaʿfar (as). Abū’l-Jārūd narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to him: “May I be made your sacrifice. When your Scholar from among the People of the House dies, what thing is it by which you recognise he who comes after him?” He replied: “By guidance, a grave and lowered demeanour, the affirmation of his excellence by the House of Muḥammad, and that he is not asked about anything between its two sides but that he gives the answer for it.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad b. Ḥumrān from al-Faḍl b. al-Sukun, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who stated: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said: “Recognise Allāh through Allāh, the Apostle through the Apostolic Message, and those vested with Divine authority through what is (recognised as) proper, as well as justice and beneficence.”
arabicText: سعد، عن ابن عيسى، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن محمد بن حمران عن الفضل بن السكن، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: إعرفوا الله بالله، والرسول بالرسالة وأُولي الأمر بالمعروف والعدل والاحسان.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from Ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad b. Ḥumrān from al-Faḍl b. al-Sukun, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who stated: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Recognise Allāh through Allāh, the Apostle through the Apostolic Message, and those vested with Divine authority through what is (recognised as) proper, as well as justice and beneficence.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. Muḥammad, from Ḥannān b. Sudayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), from his father, who said: “Imamate is not rightfully rendered to anyone but a man who has three characteristics: scrupulous piety that wards him from all that which is forbidden, forbearance with which he controls his anger, and excellent rulership over those placed under his care, such that he is to them like a compassionate father.”
arabicText: محمد العطار، عن الأشعريّ، عن عبدالصّمد بن محمد، عن حنان ابن سدير، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، عن أبيه، قال: إنّ الإمامة لا تصلح إلّا لرجل فيه ثلاث خصال: ورع يحجزه عن المحارم، وحلم يملك به غضبه، وحسن الخلافة على من ولّي عليه حتى يكون له كالوالد الرحيم.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. Muḥammad, from Ḥannān b. Sudayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Imamate is not rightfully rendered to anyone but a man who has three characteristics: scrupulous piety that wards him from all that which is forbidden, forbearance with which he controls his anger, and excellent rulership over those placed under his care, such that he is to them like a compassionate father.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad b. al-Walīd, from Ḥammād b. ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥārith b. al-Mughīra al-Naṣrī, who narrated: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “What is the Master of this Ordinance recognised on the basis of?” He replied: “Tranquility, gravitas, knowledge and the testamentary charge.”
arabicText: محمد العطار، عن الأشعري، عن محمّد بن الوليد، عن حمّاد بن عثمان، عن الحارث بن المغيرة النصريّ، قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: بما يعرف صاحب هذا الأمر؟ قال: بالسكينة والوقار، والعلم، والوصيّة.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad b. al-Walīd, from Ḥammād b. ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥārith b. al-Mughīra al-Naṣrī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “What is the Master of this Ordinance recognised on the basis of?” He replied: “Tranquility, gravitas, knowledge and the testamentary charge.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: Indications of the Imam & Proofs for Cognisance of Him
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from al-Khashshāb, from Yazīd b. Isḥāq Shaʿr, from al-Ghanawī, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who narrated: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “What is the proof against the one who makes a claim on this Ordinance without any right (to it)?” He said: “There are three proofs that do not convene upon a man unless he is the Master of this Ordinance: that he is the most worthy, among people, of he who preceded him, that he has with him the weapon of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa), and that he is the one in charge of the apparent testament, the one who, when you proceed to Medina and ask the general masses and their young ones: “To whom did so-and-so bequeath?,” they reply: “To so-and-so.”
arabicText: محمد العطار، عن الأشعري، عن الخشّاب، عن يزيد بن اسحاق شعر، عن الغنوي، عن عبدالأعلى، قال: قلت لأبي عبداللّه عليه السلام: ما الحجّة على المدّعي لهذا الأمر بغير حق؟ قال: ثلاثة من الحجّة لم يجتمعن في رجل إلّا كان صاحب هذا الأمر: أن يكون أولى الناس بمن قبله. ويكون عنده سلاح رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله. ويكون صاحب الوصيّة الظاهرة، الذي اذا قَدِمْتَ المدينة سألت العامّة والصبيان: الى من أوصى فلان؟ فيقولون: الى فلان.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār, from al-Ashʿarī, from al-Khashshāb, from Yazīd b. Isḥāq Shaʿr, from al-Ghanawī, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as): “What is the proof against the one who makes a claim on this Ordinance without any right (to it)?” He said: “There are three proofs that do not convene upon a man unless he is the Master of this Ordinance: that he is the most worthy, among people, of he who preceded him, that he has with him the weapon of the Apostle of Allāh (sawa), and that he is the one in charge of the apparent testament, the one who, when you proceed to Medina and ask the general masses and their young ones: “To whom did so-and-so bequeath?,” they reply: “To so-and-so.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: With the Imams (as-p) are the Scriptures Revealed to the Prophets
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Aḥmad b. Idrīs and Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār together, from al-Ashʿarī, from Ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Ḥammād, from al-Ḥasan b. Ibrāhīm, from Yūnus, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, who—in a lengthy report—narrated: “Barīha, the catholicos of the Christians,[1] came and said to Abī’l-Ḥasan (as): “May I be made your sacrifice. Are the (true) Torah, Gospel and (other) Prophetic scriptures with you people?”[2] He replied: “They are in our possession, an inheritance from them (the Prophets). We read them as they read them, and we relay them as they relayed them. Allāh would not appoint a Divine authority upon His earth, of whom questions about anything could be asked, only for him to say: “I do not know.”—(so follows the rest of) the report.
arabicText: أحمد بن ادريس، ومحمد العطّار معاً: عن الأشعري، عن ابن هاشم، عن محمد بن حمّاد، عن الحسن بن ابراهيم، عن يونس، عن هشام بن الحكم—في خبر طويل—قال: جاء (بريهة) جاثليق النصارى، فقال لأبي الحسن عليه السلام: جعلت فداك، أنّى لكم التوراة والانحيل وكتب الأنبياء؟ قال: هي عندنا وراثة من عندهم، نقرأها كما قرأوها، ونقولها كما قالوها، إنّ الله لا يجعل حجّة في أرضه يسأل عن شيء؟ فيقول: لا أدري، الخبر.
thaqalaynSanad: Aḥmad b. Idrīs and Muḥammad al-ʿAṭṭār together, from al-Ashʿarī, from Ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Ḥammād, from al-Ḥasan b. Ibrāhīm, from Yūnus, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, who—in a lengthy report—narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Barīha, the catholicos of the Christians,[1] came and said to Abī’l-Ḥasan (as): “May I be made your sacrifice. Are the (true) Torah, Gospel and (other) Prophetic scriptures with you people?”[2] He replied: “They are in our possession, an inheritance from them (the Prophets). We read them as they read them, and we relay them as they relayed them. Allāh would not appoint a Divine authority upon His earth, of whom questions about anything could be asked, only for him to say: “I do not know.”—(so follows the rest of) the report.

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: With the Imams (as-p) are the Scriptures Revealed to the Prophets
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad, from Ḥamdān b. Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Munayʿ b. al-Ḥajjāj, from Ḥusayn b. ʿUlwān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Allāh favoured those with determination [1] among the Apostles, through knowledge, over the Prophets. We have inherited their knowledge, and He favoured us over them with respect to what they were favoured with. The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) was made to know that which they had not known, and we were made to know the Apostle of Allāh’s (sawa) knowledge, which we transmit to our Shīʿa. Whoever among them accepts it is the best of them, and wherever we may be, our Shīʿa are with us.”
arabicText: سعد، عن علي بن محمد، عن حمدان بن سليمان، عن عبداللّه بن محمد اليماني، عن منيع بن الحجّاج، عن حسين بن علوان، عن أبي عبداللّه عليه السلام، قال: إنّ الله فضّل اُولي العزم من الرسل بالعلم على الأنبياء. وورثنا علمهم، وفضّلنا عليهم في فضلهم، وعلّم رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله ما لا يعلمون، وعلّمنا علم رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله فروينا لشيعتنا. فمن قبل منهم فهو أفضلهم، وأينما نكون فشيعتنا معنا.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad, from Ḥamdān b. Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Munayʿ b. al-Ḥajjāj, from Ḥusayn b. ʿUlwān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Allāh favoured those with determination [1] among the Apostles, through knowledge, over the Prophets. We have inherited their knowledge, and He favoured us over them with respect to what they were favoured with. The Apostle of Allāh (sawa) was made to know that which they had not known, and we were made to know the Apostle of Allāh’s (sawa) knowledge, which we transmit to our Shīʿa. Whoever among them accepts it is the best of them, and wherever we may be, our Shīʿa are with us.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyārī, saying that Muḥammad b. Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥamadānī narrated to him, who said: “I wrote to the Master of the Era (as): “The people of my house are harming and taunting me by means of the tradition which has been transmitted from your forefathers (as-p), that they said: “Our stewards and retainers are the worst of Allāh’s creation.” So, he (as) wrote back: “What is the matter with you? Do you not read what He (azwj) said: ﴾We had placed between them and the towns which We had blessed hamlets prominent﴿? [34:18]—We are, by Allāh, the towns that Allāh has blessed, and you are the hamlets prominent.”[1] ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar said: “This tradition has also been narrated to us by ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Kulaynī from Muḥammad b. Ṣāliḥ, from the Master of the Era (as).”
arabicText: عبداللّه بن جعفر الحميري، قال: حدّثني محمد بن صالح الهمداني، قال: كتبت الى صاحب الزمان عليه السلام: إنّ أهل بيتي يؤذونني ويقرعونني بالحديث الذي رُوي عن آبائك عليهم السلام أنّهم قالوا: ((قوّامنا وخدّامنا شرار خلق الله)). فكتب عليه السلام: ويحكم أما تقرأون ما قال عزّ وجل: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقُرَى ٱلَّتِى بَـٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا قُرًۭى ظَـٰهِرَةًۭ﴾. ونحن—والله—القرى التي بارك الله فيها، وأنتم القرى الظاهرة، قال عبداللّه بن جعفر: وحدّثنا بهذا الحديث عليّ بن محمد الكليني عن محمد بن صالح، عن صاحب الزمان عليه السلام.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyārī, saying that Muḥammad b. Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥamadānī narrated to him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I wrote to the Master of the Era (as): “The people of my house are harming and taunting me by means of the tradition which has been transmitted from your forefathers (as-p), that they said: “Our stewards and retainers are the worst of Allāh’s creation.” So, he (as) wrote back: “What is the matter with you? Do you not read what He (azwj) said: ﴾We had placed between them and the towns which We had blessed hamlets prominent﴿? [34:18]—We are, by Allāh, the towns that Allāh has blessed, and you are the hamlets prominent.”[1] ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar said: “This tradition has also been narrated to us by ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Kulaynī from Muḥammad b. Ṣāliḥ, from the Master of the Era (as).”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Isḥāq b. Yaʿqūb, who narrated: “I heard the scholar al-ʿUmarī (ra) saying: “I accompanied a man from the rural districts of Iraq who had with him money for the Creditor (as),[1] so he sent it forth. However, it was returned to him, and he was told: “Take out of it what rightfully belongs to your paternal cousins, which is four hundred dirhams.” The man remained bewildered, dumbfounded and astonished, and then looked at the accounts of the money, in which he found that he had in his possession an estate belonging to his paternal cousins, some of which he had already returned to them and some of which he had withheld from them when, lo and behold, the amount of that money due them was four hundred dirhams, just as he (as) had said. So, the man took it out and sent the remainder, which was accepted.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن اسحاق بن يعقوب، قال: سمعت الشيخ العمري رضي الله عنه يقول: صحبت رجلاً من أهل السواد ومعه مال للغريم عليه السلام، فأنفذه، فردّ عليه، وقيل له: ((أخرج حقّ ولد عمّك منه، وهو أربعمائة درهم)). فبقى الرجل متحيّراً باهتاً متعجّباً، ونظر في حساب المال، وكانت في يده ضيعة لولد عمّه، قد كان ردّ عليهم بعضها وزوى عنهم بعضها، فاذا الذي نصَّ لهم من ذلك المال: أربعمائة درهم، كما قال عليه السلام، فأخرجه وأنفذ الباقي فقبل.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Isḥāq b. Yaʿqūb, who narrated: “I heard the scholar al-ʿUmarī (ra) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “I accompanied a man from the rural districts of Iraq who had with him money for the Creditor (as),[1] so he sent it forth. However, it was returned to him, and he was told: “Take out of it what rightfully belongs to your paternal cousins, which is four hundred dirhams.” The man remained bewildered, dumbfounded and astonished, and then looked at the accounts of the money, in which he found that he had in his possession an estate belonging to his paternal cousins, some of which he had already returned to them and some of which he had withheld from them when, lo and behold, the amount of that money due them was four hundred dirhams, just as he (as) had said. So, the man took it out and sent the remainder, which was accepted.”

chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Rāzī, who said: “A group of our companions narrated to me that he (Imam al-Mahdī (aj)) sent forth a slave boy to Abī ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Junayd, who was in Wāsiṭ, and instructed him to sell that boy. So, he sold him and took his payment, whereupon he assayed the dinars and found them falling short in fineness, by a measure of eighteen carats and a grain.[1] He weighed out, from his own property, eighteen carats and a grain, and sent them off. A dinar was returned to him, whose weight was eighteen carats and a grain.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن علي بن محمد الرازي، قال: حدّثني جماعة من أصحابنا أنّه بعث إلى أبي عبداللّه بن الجنيد—وهو بواسط—غلاماً وأمر ببيعه، فباعه، وقبض ثمنه، فلمّا غيّر الدنانير نقصت من التعيير ثمانية عشر قيراطاً وحبّة، فوزن من عنده ثمانية عشر قيراطاً وحبّة وأنفذها . فردّ عليه ديناراً وزنه ثمانية عشر قيراطاً وحبّة.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Rāzī, who said: “A group of our companions narrated to me that
thaqalaynMatn: he (Imam al-Mahdī (aj)) sent forth a slave boy to Abī ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Junayd, who was in Wāsiṭ, and instructed him to sell that boy. So, he sold him and took his payment, whereupon he assayed the dinars and found them falling short in fineness, by a measure of eighteen carats and a grain.[1] He weighed out, from his own property, eighteen carats and a grain, and sent them off. A dinar was returned to him, whose weight was eighteen carats and a grain.”
