chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Rāzī, saying that Naṣr b. al-Ṣabāḥ narrated to him, saying: “A man from the people of Balkh sent five dinars to Ḥājiz,[1] writing a note in which he altered his own name. The receipt came out to him with his name, his lineage and a supplication for him.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن علي بن محمد الرازي، قال: حدّثني نصر بن الصباح قال: أنفذ رجل من أهل بلخ خمسة دنانير الى حاجز، وكتب رقعة، وغيّر فيها اسمه، فخرج اليه الوصول باسمه ونسبه والدعاء له.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Rāzī, saying that Naṣr b. al-Ṣabāḥ narrated to him, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “A man from the people of Balkh sent five dinars to Ḥājiz,[1] writing a note in which he altered his own name. The receipt came out to him with his name, his lineage and a supplication for him.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī Ḥāmid al-Marāghī, from Muḥammad b. Shādhān b. Naʿīm, who narrated: “A man from the people of Balkh sent some money and a note on which there was no writing, but he had traced on it with his finger in a circular manner without writing anything, and said to the emissary: “Take this money, and whoever informs you of its story and answers the note, deliver the money to him.” So, the man went to al-ʿAskar and sought out Jaʿfar,[1] informing him of the matter, whereupon Jaʿfar said to him: “Do you affirm (the doctrine of) badāʾ?” The man said: “Yes.” Jaʿfar continued: “Verily, a badāʾ has occurred to your master, so he has instructed you to give me the money.”[2] So, the emissary said to him: “This answer does not convince me.” He then left him and went around to our companions, whereupon a note came out to him, saying: “This money had been exposed to loss. It was on top of a chest when thieves entered the house and seized whatever was in the chest, while the money remained unharmed.” The note was returned to him (the man from Balkh), and written on it in a circular fashion was: “And you asked for supplication—may Allāh do such-and-such for you, and so He has done.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن أبي حامد المراغيّ، عن محمد بن شاذان بن نعيم، قال: بعث رجل من أهل بلخ بمال ورقعة ليس فيها كتابة، قد خطّ فيها باصبعه كما تدور من غير كتابة، وقال للرسول: احمل هذا المال، فمن أخبرك بقصّته، وأجاب عن الرقعة، فأوصل اليه المال. فصار الرجل الى العسكر، وقد قصد جعفراً، وأخبره الخبر، فقال له جعفر: تقرّ بالبداء؟ قال الرجل: نعم. قال له: فانّ صاحبك قد بدا له وأمرك أن تعطيني المال، فقال له الرسول: لا يقنعني هذا الجواب. فخرج من عنده، وجعل يدور على أصحابنا، فخرجت اليه رقعة قال: ((هذا مال قد كان غرّر به)). وكان فوق صندوق فدخل اللصوص البيت وأخذوا ما في الصندوق وسلّم المال وردّت عليه الرقعة، وقد كتب فيها كما تدور، ((وسألت الدعاء فعل الله بك وفعل)).
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī Ḥāmid al-Marāghī, from Muḥammad b. Shādhān b. Naʿīm, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “A man from the people of Balkh sent some money and a note on which there was no writing, but he had traced on it with his finger in a circular manner without writing anything, and said to the emissary: “Take this money, and whoever informs you of its story and answers the note, deliver the money to him.” So, the man went to al-ʿAskar and sought out Jaʿfar,[1] informing him of the matter, whereupon Jaʿfar said to him: “Do you affirm (the doctrine of) badāʾ?” The man said: “Yes.” Jaʿfar continued: “Verily, a badāʾ has occurred to your master, so he has instructed you to give me the money.”[2] So, the emissary said to him: “This answer does not convince me.” He then left him and went around to our companions, whereupon a note came out to him, saying: “This money had been exposed to loss. It was on top of a chest when thieves entered the house and seized whatever was in the chest, while the money remained unharmed.” The note was returned to him (the man from Balkh), and written on it in a circular fashion was: “And you asked for supplication—may Allāh do such-and-such for you, and so He has done.”

category: The Addendum (Comprising al-Ṣadūq’s Transmissions from his Father, the Author (rh), in Order to Complete this Work)
chapter: They are the Prominent Hamlets (Qurā al-Ẓāhira)
author: ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh
englishText: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. al-Ṣāliḥ, who narrates: “I wrote to him, requesting supplication for Badāshāla, who had been imprisoned by Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz,[1] and seeking permission to have a child by a bondswoman of mine, so came out: “Have a child with her, for Allāh does what He wills. As for the prisoner, Allāh will free him.” I had a child with the bondswoman and she gave birth, but then died.[2] The prisoner was let go the same day the written directive came out to me.”
arabicText: سعد بن عبداللّه، عن محمد بن الصالح قال: كتبت أسأله الدعاء لباداشاله وقد حبسه ابن عبدالعزيز، وأستأذن في جارية لي أستولدها، فخرج: ((استولدها، ويفعل الله ما يشاء، والمحبوس يخلّصه الله)). فاستولدت الجارية فولدت فماتت، وخلّي عن المحبوس يوم خرج اليَّ التوقيع.
thaqalaynSanad: Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad b. al-Ṣāliḥ, who narrates:
thaqalaynMatn: “I wrote to him, requesting supplication for Badāshāla, who had been imprisoned by Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz,[1] and seeking permission to have a child by a bondswoman of mine, so came out: “Have a child with her, for Allāh does what He wills. As for the prisoner, Allāh will free him.” I had a child with the bondswoman and she gave birth, but then died.[2] The prisoner was let go the same day the written directive came out to me.”
